3. Render: compose and draw text in frames anchored inside stories. An anchored text frame is not a page item, so the document's frame list never reached it. compose_loose_frame composes a story into one frame built from the item itself, and the renderer uses it when a text item has no registered frame. title: Files: saves and exports replace the file atomically
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #436.

Native engine saves, Save a Copy, snippets, books, libraries, swatches and engine/MCP exports replace files atomically instead of truncating the existing file in place. Desktop Services writes and CLI raster exports are separate follow-ups.

The writer stages a uniquely named file in the same folder, preserves existing Unix permissions before writing document bytes, flushes the file, and renames it over the target. Errors before replacement leave the original untouched. Short randomized names support valid long destination names, and temporary files are cleaned up on errors and caught unwinding. Symlinks are resolved with a bound and loop detection; Windows sharing errors get bounded retries. Parent-folder flushing is best effort, so a successful save does not promise power-loss durability.

Validation: full `cargo xtask ci` on the refreshed candidate (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, native tests, assets, layers and WASM compilation). Regression coverage includes private staging permissions, valid long filenames, partial write failures, cleanup on unwind, symlinks, permissions, rename retries, and save/copy round trips. Windows runtime and physical power-loss behavior were not tested.

title: Fix needless horizontal scrollbar in the app bar at 115% scale (#481)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #481.

At 115% interface scale, the app bar's right-hand tools slot was sized to the full remaining width of the row. Fractional-scale rounding could make the row a fraction of a pixel wider than its horizontal scroll area, so a scroll bar appeared that scrolled only a tiny amount.

The slot is now one pixel narrower than the remaining width (`tools_slot_width`). It is still never narrower than the controls, so a narrow window keeps scrolling as before.

A unit test covers both cases: the slot leaves slack when everything fits, and it keeps the controls' width when the window is narrow.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across DesignCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for DesignCraft.

title: UI: Alt + wheel zooms the view at the pointer
author: noah1400
body:
Addresses the first half of #470.

Turning the mouse wheel over a document view with Alt (Option on macOS) held scrolled the view like the plain wheel. It now zooms at the pointer, exactly as Ctrl/Cmd + wheel does.

Like egui's Ctrl/Cmd zoom, a wheel motion keeps its key to its end. The wheel is smoothed over a few frames and a trackpad swipe coasts on, so letting Alt go early does not turn the rest of the motion into scrolling.

Not changed: Ctrl/Cmd + wheel still zooms. The issue also asks for it to scroll sideways. title: Selection tool: Alt and Shift resize around the centre and keep side-handle drags centred
author: aiongg
body:
Problem: resizing with the Selection tool combined the modifiers in the wrong order and anchored them to the wrong points.
- Alt on a corner handle could only grow a frame. Dragging the corner inwards left the frame unchanged, because the opposite corner set the minimum half-size.
- Alt+Shift applied the aspect constraint to the edge-anchored rectangle first and then centred it, so shrinking failed the same way and the driving axis was chosen from the wrong measurement.
- Shift on a side handle scaled the other axis from one edge, so the frame grew to one side instead of staying on its centre line.

Change (`crates/tools/src/select.rs`):
- `finish_resize` applies Alt first, then Shift. With both, the frame scales by one factor around its centre, measured from the centre, and the dragged corner stays under the pointer on the driving axis.
- `apply_alt` mirrors only the dragged sides around the centre, so a drag inwards shrinks the frame and a drag past the centre flips it.
- `apply_aspect` keeps the edges opposite the handle fixed and centres any axis the handle does not move.

Validation: `cargo test -p designcraft-tools --lib -- resize` (`resize_side_shift_keeps_the_other_axis_centred`, `resize_corner_alt_shift_scales_around_the_centre`, `resize_corner_alt_mirrors_the_opposite_side`; all three fail before the change), `shift_alt_resize_keeps_aspect_and_center` and `resize_rect_modifiers` still pass; `cargo clippy -p designcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

title: Text: copied text keeps its endnotes and editorial notes
author: aiongg
body:
`Story::extract` copied footnotes, cross-references, index markers and anchored objects with a text range, but not endnotes or editorial notes, so copy/paste and drag-copy/move left those markers with empty payloads. It also sliced each payload list by marker count, and inserting a footnote, endnote or editorial note indexed the payload list, so a story with more markers than payloads (a damaged or hostile file) panicked.

- `extract` copies endnotes and editorial notes, reads every payload list with `get`, and fits the slice's lists to its markers (`fix_notes`, new `fix_endnotes`, `fix_marks`): a missing payload becomes an empty one.
- `insert_story` writes the payloads into the entries made for the pasted markers; they keep new ids, so a pasted copy is independent of the original.
- `footnote.insert`, `endnote.insert` and `note.new` repair the payload lists first and write through `get_mut`; `insert_note`/`insert_endnote` return `Option<u64>` (commands report an error, Word import a warning).
- Formatted paste into a table cell drops endnote references and note anchors, as it does footnotes. `set_story_text` resets endnotes and editorial notes too.

Validation: `slice::tests::copy_paste_keeps_endnotes_and_editorial_notes`, `slice::tests::extract_survives_more_markers_than_payloads` and `cmd::editorial::tests::notes_insert_into_a_story_whose_markers_lack_payloads` (both panicked before); existing copy/paste, drag, footnote, endnote and Word import tests pass.

title: UI: make the application bar's search field find and run commands
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #480.

**Problem.** The search field at the right of the application bar was only painted: clicking it did nothing and it took no text, on every platform.

**Change.**
- The field is a real text field. A click gives it the keyboard; typing lists the matching menu commands in a dropdown under it, labelled in the interface language with their shortcuts. Labels match in the interface language and in English.
- ↑/↓ move the highlight, Return or a click runs the command the way its menu item does (commands that open a dialog open it). Commands that are off show greyed and don't run. Escape clears the field. Both give the keyboard back to the widget that had it.
- While the field has the keyboard, keys reach neither the shortcuts nor the document. That includes the Escape press that leaves the field, so it no longer switches the tool.
- The search reuses Quick Apply's command list and matching (`menus::command_search`).
- New string "No matching commands" with de/fr/es/ja/zh/ar/pt-BR/it/uk rows; "Search" and "Search commands" get German, French and Spanish translations.

Validation:
- `chrome::tests::the_search_field_finds_and_runs_menu_commands` (German labels listed, a disabled command doesn't run, ↓ ↑ Return groups two frames, the field releases the keyboard)
- `chrome::tests::keys_typed_in_the_search_field_stay_out_of_the_document` (tool keys, Delete, Backspace, Cmd+A and Escape leave the tool and the frames alone)

title: IDML: import and wrap around custom text-wrap boundaries
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #451.
Builds on #384.

## Problem

An IDML item's `TextWrapPreference/Properties/PathGeometry` holds a wrap boundary edited apart from the frame (a triangle on a rectangle, for example). Import read only the wrap mode, side, contour type and offsets, so text wrapped around the frame's bounds and every later line moved.

## Change

- Model: `TextWrap.path`, an optional custom boundary in the item's inner space (the space of its own path), with the offsets already included. Absent by default and not serialized when absent.
- Import: reads the boundary from `TextWrapPreference`'s `PathGeometry`. A boundary with more than 4096 points, a malformed or non-finite point, or no points is dropped with a log warning; the rest of the wrap still imports.
- Export: writes the boundary before `TextWrapOffset`, so it round-trips.
- Compose: with a custom boundary, bounding-box and contour wraps follow it through the contour machinery of #384, band by band; jump modes use its bounds. Offsets are not added again.
- Editing: resizing an item (`transform.resize`, layout adjustment, liquid layout and the other paths through `bake`) transforms the boundary with the frame's path. Setting `offset` or `contour` through `object.textWrap` drops the boundary, because both would otherwise have no effect; mode and side keep it. Other path edits keep it unchanged. The params doc says so.

Validation:
- `idml::tests::custom_wrap_boundary_imports_composes_and_round_trips`
- `idml::tests::hostile_custom_wrap_boundary_is_dropped`
- `engine::tests::custom_wrap_path_follows_resize_and_yields_to_offsets`
- existing wrap and contour tests in `designcraft-compose`, `designcraft-idml` and `designcraft-engine`

title: Layout: parent pages pass margins and guides to their pages
author: aiongg
body:
Follow-up to #468 and #937.

On main, `layout.marginsAndColumns {parent}` updates the document pages whose margins and columns equal the parent's old values. That leaves three cases wrong:

- Applying a different parent (`layout.pages.applyParent`) keeps the page's old margins instead of giving it the new parent's.
- After inserting a page, pages that move to the other side keep the old side's margins.
- A page given margins equal to its parent's counts as following the parent, so the next parent change overwrites them.

This PR replaces the equality rule with an explicit flag:

- Setting margins on document pages makes them the pages' own (`Page::local_margins`). A page without its own takes its parent page's margins and columns (first parent page for left and single-sided pages, last otherwise) and follows later changes, also when it changes side or parent (`Document::sync_parent_margins`, run on repaginate, applyParent and parent margin changes).
- `layout.marginsAndColumns` takes `parent` as a prefix, label or index.
- IDML import: a page whose MarginPreference matches its parent page follows the parent, one that differs is its own, one without takes the parent's. Older `.designcraft` files mark pages that differ from their parent as their own on load, so nothing moves.
- Parent ruler guides draw and snap on the pages based on that parent without a per-page allocation (`Document::parent_guides`); `inherited_guides(abs)` stays for the guide commands and the dialogs. #937's Margins and Columns dialog layout and Preview are unchanged.

Tests: `applying_a_parent_gives_its_margins_and_local_margins_stay_local`, `pages_follow_their_parent_pages_margins_unless_set_locally`, `parent_margins_change_the_parent_and_follow_unoverridden_pages`, `parent_guides_show_on_pages_but_stay_on_the_parent`, `parent_and_page_margins_round_trip_through_idml` (engine); `differing_margins_from_older_files_stay_local` (doc); `parent_page_guides_snap_on_the_document_page` (tools); `parent_g…

title: UI: set the interface language in Preferences
author: aiongg
body:

title: View: leave Presentation mode with Esc or Shift+W
author: aiongg
body:

Problem: Presentation screen mode hides the menus, panels and toolbar, and Esc did nothing in it, so there was no way back to editing short of quitting.

- Esc in Presentation returns to the screen mode Presentation was entered from (Normal if unknown). The key press goes only to that: it no longer reaches the canvas, so it doesn't switch tools or deselect.

title: UI: show Tamil, Indic, Southeast Asian and other scripts from installed fonts

title: Color: retain ICC data and stable profile ids
author: KnottyDyes
body:
PDF/X-4 export always embeds the built-in generic CMYK profile as its output intent. Letting users pick a press profile (#159, #32) needs the colour crate to keep more of an imported ICC profile than it does today. This PR is that first step only.

- Imported ICC profiles keep their declared bytes, profile class and channel count, so a later change can embed them as a `DestOutputProfile`. Profile file reads are capped at 64 MiB.
- A declared length shorter than the header or longer than the data is rejected. Trailing padding is accepted and dropped, so every profile that loads on `main` still loads.
- Built-in profiles get fixed ids. Imported profiles get an id from their file stem, separate from the description label shown to users. Empty ids are rejected.
- Colour settings, working-space and proof lookups use the ids. Saved display names still resolve after the id lookup, so existing settings keep working. The Color Settings dialog shows names and stores ids.
- An imported id that collides with an existing id or name gets a numeric suffix (`press-2`) instead of replacing the existing profile, so the active working space can't be dropped. Loading the same file twice now gives two entries.
- Colour conversion and PDF export are unchanged. Choosing the output intent, finding installed profiles and saving the choice would follow in later PRs.

Validation: 11 colour tests and 1 engine test fail against the previous version of this branch and pass with the change, covering id lookup, legacy names, stem collisions and padded profiles. `cargo test -p designcraft-color -p designcraft-engine` and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

Part of #159 and #32.

title: Recovery: each running app keeps its own recovery data
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #496.

Each running app keeps recovery data in its own locked folder, so matching document IDs in two processes do not overwrite one another. Startup recovers entries from runs whose locks are free and leaves live runs alone.

- Each run creates a folder under the recovery root and holds its lock until exit. Ownership checks validate the current folder and regular lock file, including replacement paths and symlinks; failed validation stops writes and deletion.
- On Unix, held file and directory identities protect against replacement of an owned path. Other platforms validate the lock marker.
- If an isolated run folder cannot be created or locked, recovery is disabled with a warning rather than falling back to the shared root.
- Explicit `file.recovery.*` directories remain supported. Unknown files or entries that cannot be moved preserve the old folder.
- A concurrently running older app still writes unlocked entries in the root; mixed-version isolation remains unresolved. Recovery checkpoint retention is a separate follow-up.

Validation: full `cargo xtask ci` on the refreshed candidate (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, native tests, assets, layers and WASM compilation). Regression coverage includes two real processes with the same document ID, live versus exited runs, replaced folders and lock files, symlinks, failed relocking, and isolation failure. Current runtime qualification is macOS; Windows runtime and network-filesystem locks were not tested.

title: Color parsing: one scale per colour, not per component
author: japbcoelho
body:
`parse_color` chose the scale for each component on its own (above 1 → percent, otherwise a fraction), so a CMYK percentage of 1 or less next to larger ones was read as a fraction. `{"c": 0.7, "m": 0, "y": 12.2, "k": 0}`, a pale cream, became C 70 % Y 12.2 % and exported as `0.7019608 0 0.12156863 0 k`. The params docs say `{c,m,y,k}(0..100)`. RGB arrays had the same rule.

Now a colour is read on one scale: percentages (0..100, RGB 0..255) when any component is above 1, fractions only when every component is within 0..1, so the older fraction form keeps working. A colour whose percentages are all 1 or less is still read as fractions.

Validation: the bug reproduces with the v0.6.0 release CLI (`swatch.create` with the cream above, a frame filled with it, then `file.exportPdf`). New test `color_tests::percent_components_at_most_one_stay_percent` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/style.rs`. On main `ca343e8`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p designcraft-engine` pass; the full `cargo xtask ci` is left to the checks here.

title: Place: PDF pages and SVGs keep their exact size
author: japbcoelho
body:
`file.place` took a placed PDF page's (and an SVG's) natural size from `image_size`, which rounds to whole points, and the export draws the page into that size. A 91.774 × 613.276 pt page became 92 × 613 and was drawn 0.25 % wider and 0.3 % shorter, so pieces of a cover laid edge to edge left gaps of up to 1.9 pt. A 100.4 × 50.4 pt page placed 100.4 pt wide came out `Rect { x0: 0.0, y0: 0.0, x1: 100.4, y1: 50.2 }`.

The natural size is now the exact page (crop box) or SVG size, through a new `designcraft_render::natural_size`; the rounded `pixels` stay for display and preflight. `place.load` (the place cursor) gets the same exact size.

Validation: the bug reproduces with the v0.6.0 release CLI (the placed page is drawn at x 1 by y 0.996). title: MCP: never replay a request after a lost reply
author: KnottyDyes
body:
When a request to the running app fails mid-flight, the MCP remote backend reconnects and sends the same request again. A lost reply doesn't mean the request wasn't applied, so an edit such as `frame.create` can be applied twice.

- A failed request now drops the connection and returns an error saying the operation may have completed and the document should be inspected before retrying. It is never resent.
- The next request reconnects as before, so a restarted app is still picked up. This matches how PhotoCraft's bridge behaves.
- `docs/mcp.md` describes the uncertain outcome in connected mode.

Validation: a loopback test server applies the edit and closes the connection before replying. Before the change the client resent it and the edit was applied twice; now it is applied once, the call returns an error and the next call reconnects. `cargo test -p designcraft-mcp` (18 passed) and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Compose: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words and justify without tearing marks
author: visarutforthaipbs
body:
Fixes #515.

Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar are written without spaces between words. Until now the composer had no word boundaries for them, so lines were split mid-word by the emergency path, and justified lines were letter-spaced through the Single-Word path, pulling combining vowels and tone marks off their consonants.

## What changes
- **`crates/compose/src/sea.rs` (new):** word boundaries from `icu_segmenter` (ICU4X 2.3, already in `Cargo.lock` through other deps; compiled data; wasm-safe). A boundary is kept where the dictionary and the LSTM segmenter agree — the dictionary alone is greedy longest-match and yields `ผลก|า|รตร|วจส|อบ`; the LSTM alone splits compounds. Results are cached per paragraph text. Extra rules: no line starts with ๆ ฯ ะ า ำ, none ends with เ แ โ ใ ไ.
- **`shape.rs`:** `Glyph::word_gap`, set at a boundary between two SEA letters.
- **`breaker.rs`:** in justified text a word gap is a zero-width stretch glue (`Spacing::sea_gap_stretch`, 0.5 of a word space), so Knuth–Plass sees stretch between Thai words. Ragged text keeps the `penalty(0)` path.
- **`lib.rs`:** `layout_line`/`distribute` treat word gaps as justification slots and never add letter space before an *attached* glyph (a mark, or a later glyph of the same cluster — `Glyph::ch` is the cluster's first char, so detection goes by cluster). Inside Thai words letter-space stretch is withheld when the line has word gaps.
- Only pairs where **both** glyphs are SEA letters get a boundary; ICU word boundaries around `(`, `.`, `-` are not line-break opportunities.
- Non-SEA paragraphs return before any of this runs; a Latin snapshot test shows identical breaks and widths.

## Evidence
Corpus of 30 Thai paragraphs scored against PyThaiNLP `newmm` boundaries ([harness](https://github.com/visarutforthaipbs/designcraft-thai-eval)):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| line wraps | 106 | 99 |
| wraps off a PyThaiNLP boundary | 38 (36%) | 13 (13%) — all at compound joints (`ตรวจ\|สอบ`, `คณะ\|กรร…

title: Corner Options keep curves and round every corner point
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4). Its four "petals" are made by intersecting an ellipse with a square (Pathfinder › Intersect), then Corner › Rounded.

## Problem
Corner Options (`object.cornerOptions`, Properties › Corner) applied a corner only where two straight segments meet. `apply_subpath` also redrew every other segment as a straight `line_to`. A quarter circle with rounded corners therefore rendered as a triangle with one rounded corner. The selection outline still showed the arc, and so did the frame's path, because the bug is in the drawn shape only (screen, PDF export).

## Fix
`crates/geom/src/corners.rs`:
- **Corner points:** a corner point is an anchor where the path turns (incoming and outgoing directions differ by more than about 1°), whatever the segments are. Smooth points are left alone.
- **Trimming:** the segments on each side of a corner are trimmed by the corner size along their length (`inv_arclen`). Curves stay curves.
- **Corner shape:** it is drawn between the two trim points along their tangents, so a rounded corner joins an arc smoothly.
- **Unchanged:** rectangles and straight-sided frames give the same result as before (existing tests). The size is still clamped to half of each adjacent side, and the shape of anchor `i` is still `corners[i % 4]`.

## Before / after
The tutorial's petals: Pathfinder › Intersect, then Corner › Rounded, 50 pt.

title: Object fills and strokes must name a swatch
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4). Its white circle is filled with Paper, but `object.fill {"swatch": "Paper"}` returned `{"changed": 1}` and the circle disappeared, because the swatch is named `[Paper]`.

## Problem
`object.fill` and `object.stroke` (`swatch` and `gapSwatch`) stored any string as the swatch. A name the document doesn't have paints nothing, with no error: `Paper`, `Black`, `[black]`, `#ff0000`, or a typo. An existing engine test (`scale_strokes_and_dimensions_with_stroke`) itself stroked with `"Black"`, which drew no stroke.

## Fix
- **Unknown names refused:** both commands now return a bad-params error for a swatch name the document doesn't have, and change nothing.
- **Suggestion:** when the name differs from a real swatch only in case or brackets, the error names that swatch: ``swatch: no swatch named `Paper` (did you mean `[Paper]`?); create one with `swatch.create` and use its returned name``.
- **Same rule as #403:** that PR applies it to character fills (`type.char`, styles, `find.change`); this one covers objects. The two are independent.
- **Test fixed:** the test above now uses `[Black]`.

## Tests
- `fills_and_strokes_must_name_a_swatch_and_change_nothing_otherwise`: `Paper`, `[black]`, `Missing Ink` and `#ff0000` are refused for fills, strokes and gap swatches. The suggestion appears when there is one, and the document is untouched. `[Paper]`, `[None]` and a CMYK swatch still apply.
- Engine, UI and MCP tests pass (except `package_refuses_windows_directory_redirects`, which needs symlink privilege this Windows account lacks); clippy is clean.

title: Duplicate, Step and Repeat and copy-moves report the copies' ids
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4) with a command script. The tutorial copies a petal three times and flips each copy, but the script couldn't refer to the copies.

## Problem
`transform.move {copy: true}` and `edit.duplicate` returned only `{"moved": 1}`, and `edit.stepAndRepeat` only `{"created": n}`. The copies are selected, but a script, the MCP server or `$N.ids.0` references had no way to name them. The only way round was copy and paste, because `edit.paste` does return `ids`.

## Change
All three now also return `ids`:
- `transform.move`: the objects moved, or the copies with `copy`.
- `edit.duplicate`: the copies (it runs `transform.move` with `copy`).
- `edit.stepAndRepeat`: every copy, in creation order.

The existing `moved` and `created` counts are unchanged, and the command descriptions say what they return.

## Tests
- `copies_report_their_ids`: a plain move reports the moved id; a copy-move and Duplicate report new ids that exist and are the selection; Step and Repeat ×3 reports 3 ids that exist.
- Engine (except `package_refuses_windows_directory_redirects`, which needs symlink privilege this Windows account lacks), MCP and UI tests pass; clippy is clean.

title: Every command that writes story text reads CR as a paragraph return
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4) with a command script. A small text block written with `story.replaceRange` as `"heading\rbody"` showed the heading and the body run together, with a missing-glyph box between them.

## Problem
InDesign's scripting, IDML and classic Mac text end paragraphs with `\r`. `frame.create`, `text.insert` and `edit.paste` already read `\r` and `\r\n` as `\n`, the paragraph separator, through `text_param`. These commands kept the CR in the story instead, where it drew as a missing glyph and joined the paragraphs:
- `story.replaceRange` and `story.setText`
- `note.new`
- `footnote.insert` and footnote editing
- `endnote.insert` and `endnote.edit`
- type on a path
- table cell text (`set_cell`)

## Fix
These commands now read their `text` with `text_param`. Alt text, caption templates, variables, scripts and XML keep their text unchanged, since it isn't story text.

## Tests
- `carriage_returns_separate_paragraphs` now also covers `story.replaceRange` and `story.setText` with `\r` and `\r\n`. It fails on main: `("Zero\rOne\nTwo\nThree\nFour", 4)` instead of 5 paragraphs.
- Engine and MCP tests pass (except `package_refuses_windows_directory_redirects`, which needs symlink privilege this Windows account lacks); clippy is clean.

title: Parent-page items are composed for their page by index, not page name
author: seanth
body:
## Problem
A text variable in a parent-page frame (e.g. a running header) is empty or wrong on any page
whose page number repeats an earlier one. With two sections that both number from 1
(front matter 1–10, body 1–…), body pages 1–10 show no running header.

The renderer and PDF export pass only the page's *name* to `CompositionCache::get`, which
looks the page up with `(0..page_count).find(|i| doc.page_name(i) == n)`. That returns the
first page with the name, in the front matter, before any matching text, so the header
comes out empty. The cache is also keyed by name, so two pages with the same name share
one composed header.

## Change
- `CompositionCache::get` takes the absolute page index (`None` for a story's own frames),
  keys its cache by it, and derives the name for page-number markers from it.
- The renderer and PDF export pass `first_page_of_spread + i` for parent-page items.
- 5 files, ~80 lines; no change to stories composed for their own frames.

## Test
`running_header_on_parent_page_with_repeated_page_numbers`: pages named 1, 2, 1, 2, with the
only heading on the third page. Before: the third page's header is empty (0 glyphs).
After: "Epsilon". The full workspace test suite, clippy `-D warnings`, `xtask layers` and
`xtask assets` pass. (`xtask wasm` not run: no wasm target in my environment.)

## Relation to other PRs
Found with a real InDesign IDML: a dictionary with two sections numbered from 1 and a
parent-page header made of three frames: "first on page" and "last on page" Match Character
Style running headers, and `Page <current page number>`.

- **This PR is independent** and fixes documents created in DesignCraft with
  `variables.define` / `variables.insert` (as in the test).
- **For IDML files it needs #301**, which imports text variables. Without #301 the
  variables are dropped on import and the header frames are empty on every page.

title: Tint and Apply To in the Properties Fill and Stroke menus
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4). The tutorial uses the Fill menu in Properties twice:
- It colours a heading's text by choosing Apply To: Text with the frame selected.
- It sets the background to Tint 25%.

## Problem
In InDesign, the Fill and Stroke chips in Properties › Appearance open a menu with Apply To (Frame or Text, for a text frame), a Tint field, then the swatches. DesignCraft's menu listed only the swatches:
- **Tint:** it needed the Swatches panel.
- **Text frame:** the menu could colour only the frame. Its text needed a text selection first.

## Change
`swatch_menu` in `panels/properties.rs`:
- **Apply To: Frame / Text** (text frames only). With Text, a swatch or tint goes to the whole story through `type.char` (`fill` / `fillTint`, `stroke` / `strokeTint`). The choice is remembered while the app runs, separately for Fill and Stroke.
- **Tint:** shows the current tint of the frame's fill or stroke, or of the text's. Changing it keeps the swatch (`object.fill {swatch, tint}`, `object.stroke {tint}`).
- **Text selected:** the menu applies to the selected text, with its tint (Apply To isn't shown).
- New strings `Apply To:` and `Frame` are in every language table (`Text` and `Tint:` existed).

## Screenshot
A text frame selected, Stroke menu:

![Fill/Stroke menu with Apply To and Tint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/swatch-popup/after.png)

title: Place: an image placed into a frame leaves Auto-Fit off
author: aiongg
body:
Placing an image into an existing frame (File › Place with a frame selected, or dropping the loaded place cursor on a frame) filled the frame proportionally and also turned Auto-Fit on. Every later resize refitted the image around the centre, so dragging the top handle down cropped the bottom as well, and a frame could not be cropped from one side.

- The image still fills the frame proportionally when it is placed. Auto-Fit stays off, so resizing the frame crops the image and leaves it where it is. Frame Fitting Options › Auto-Fit turns it on.

Validation: `place_gun_click_drag_and_into_frame` now drags the frame's top edge down and checks the image doesn't move; it fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: IDML: a spread's view rotation is read and written
author: aiongg
body:
A rotated spread (Rotate Spread) opened from IDML came in unrotated, and exported IDML lost the rotation (#484).

- Import reads the rotation part of the Spread's `ItemTransform`: `0 1 -1 0` is a quarter turn clockwise, `-1 0 0 -1` a half turn (`-0` included), `0 -1 1 0` a quarter turn counter-clockwise. Any other matrix, or malformed numbers, leaves the spread unrotated. The rotation only turns the view; page and item geometry are the same as for the unrotated spread.
- Export writes the same matrices for rotated spreads; parent spreads stay identity.

Validation: `crates/idml/src/tests/spread_rotation.rs` imports each rotation from synthetic IDML (and malformed, scaled and 45° matrices), checks geometry against the unrotated import, and round-trips rotations 0–3. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: View: draw the document grid
author: aiongg
body:
Show Document Grid turned on but drew nothing: the grid settings and Snap to Document Grid worked, but the canvas never read the show flag (#530).

- The grid is drawn on the lines Snap to Document Grid uses: every `vertical / subdivisions` and `horizontal / subdivisions`, counted from each page's top-left corner the way snapping counts them, with subdivision lines lighter than the major lines.
- Grids in Back draws it between the paper and the page items; otherwise it is drawn over them. It is part of the screen render only (`RenderOptions::document_grid`, empty by default), so exports never include it.
- Lines too close together at the current zoom are left out (subdivisions first), a grid denser than 4096 lines per axis draws nothing on that axis, and zero, negative or non-finite spacing draws nothing. Hidden in Preview and Presentation.
- View › Grids & Guides › Show/Hide Document Grid (`view.documentGrid`, Cmd/Ctrl+'); the Properties toggle runs the same command, and the control channel's `ui.set` accepts `documentGrid`.

Validation: `document_grid_is_drawn_where_points_snap_to_it` snaps a point to the grid and finds the drawn lines there; `show_document_grid_toggles_from_the_grids_and_guides_menu`; `unusable_spacing_draws_nothing_and_dense_grids_thin_out` (render). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Type: a Justification dialog for the selected paragraphs
author: aiongg
body:
Word Spacing, Letter Spacing and Glyph Scaling could only be set in a paragraph style; a paragraph without its own style had no way to get them (#531).

- Type › Justification… and the Paragraph panel menu (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J) open a Justification dialog for the selected paragraphs, text frames or cells, with the same controls as Paragraph Style Options › Justification: both dialogs draw one shared section.
- Where the selected paragraphs differ, a field shows empty and is left alone unless edited (`type.selectionAttrs {mixed: true}` reports which paragraph attributes differ). OK applies the edited fields as one undo step; Cancel changes nothing.
- Both dialogs check the values: word spacing 0–1000%, letter spacing −100–500%, glyph scaling 50–200%, and minimum ≤ desired ≤ maximum. A bad value keeps the dialog open with the reason; nothing is clamped.

Validation: `justification_dialog_applies_to_a_local_paragraph_and_cancel_changes_nothing`, `justification_dialog_leaves_mixed_fields_alone_and_refuses_bad_values`. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

`actionlint` passes.

title: Fonts: format, classification and PANOSE of each face, read without keeping fonts loaded
author: moppeeer
body:
Split out of #466 (InDesign-style font menu), at review's request: this is its fonts-crate part, with no UI. #466 builds on it.

## What it adds
- **Kind of each face:** `FontFace::kind()` returns its format, class and PANOSE numbers (`FaceKind`), read once from its tables and cached on the face.
  - Formats: TrueType, OpenType/CFF, variable, colour.
  - Classes: Serif, Slab Serif, Sans Serif, Script, Monospaced, Decorative, Symbol.
  - The class comes from PANOSE, else the OS/2 IBM family class, else the family name, else the glyph: an "l" much wider at its foot than mid-stem has serifs.
- **File date:** `FontFace::added()` is when the file was added (created, else modified). The font menu's Show Recently Added uses it.
- **Similarity:** `panose_distance` measures how close two faces' PANOSE numbers are, for Show Similar Fonts.
- **Kind of a family without loading it:** `ScopedFonts::family_kind(family)` gives a family's kind and file date from its Regular face.
  - A loaded face is asked directly.
  - An installed family that isn't loaded is read from its file, which is let go afterwards. Files over `MAX_DOCUMENT_FONT_BYTES` are skipped.
  - This answers the review on #466: its filters look at every installed family, and reading them through `face()` loaded each one and kept its bytes for the rest of the session.

On this machine's fonts: Times, Georgia and Cambria are serif; Arial, Calibri and Segoe UI sans; Rockwell slab; Courier and Consolas monospaced; Segoe Script script; Gabriola decorative; Symbol symbol; emoji colour; Bahnschrift variable.

title: Words in capitals hyphenate like capitalized words
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4). Its heading, typed in capitals, breaks in InDesign as "FERRUM COM- / MODI UNTI / RAECTAT". DesignCraft moved the whole of COMMODI to the next line.

## Problem
`hyphen_points` never hyphenated a word made only of capital letters, whatever the paragraph's settings. InDesign hyphenates words in capitals under the same rule as capitalized words, **Hyphenate Capitalized Words**, which is on by default. Turning it off is InDesign's way of keeping acronyms and words in capitals whole.

## Fix
- **Same rule:** words in capitals follow `hyph_capitalized` like words with a capital first letter.
  - On (the default), they hyphenate at their dictionary or pattern points: COM-MO-DI, TY-POG-RA-PHY.
  - Off, they stay whole, like any capitalized word.
- **Minimum word length:** short acronyms (NASA) are still too short to hyphenate.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/hyphenate-caps/before.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/hyphenate-caps/after.png) |

(Source Sans 3 Bold 48 pt in a two-column frame, as the tutorial's heading.)

## Tests
- `case_apostrophes_and_punctuation`: TYPOGRAPHY → TY-POG-RA-PHY and COMMODI → COM-MO-DI by default, and TYPOGRAPHY stays whole with capitalized words off. It previously asserted that words in capitals never hyphenate.

title: One underline bar per stretch of text, no seams between letters
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4), whose heading is underlined.

## Problem
On the canvas, an underline (and a strikethrough) was drawn as one rectangle per glyph. Where two anti-aliased edges met at a fractional pixel, they left a faint lighter seam between the letters. PDF export already merges a stretch of text into one bar, so this was screen-only.

## Fix
`render::text::build_line` merges a glyph's bar into the previous one when it continues it: same colour, tint and vertical extent, starting within 0.5 pt of where the previous one ends. That's the same rule as `pdf::text::text_rules`.

The zoom below (8×, nearest-neighbour) shows the underline under FERRUM in Source Sans 3 Bold 48 pt:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/underline-seams/before.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/underline-seams/after.png) |

title: Rotation, shear, scale, rotate and flip in Properties › Transform
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to Page Layout Design in Adobe InDesign](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvO9QpPyXc4). At 9:30 it selects a petal and clicks **Flip Horizontal** and then **Flip Vertical** in the Properties panel's Transform section. The Properties panel then shows the petal at 180° and −100%.

## Problem
InDesign's Properties › Transform shows these under X/Y/W/H:
- the rotation and shear angles, beside the X and Y scale;
- a row of buttons: Rotate 90° Clockwise, Rotate 90° Counterclockwise, Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical.

DesignCraft's showed only X/Y/W/H. The rest was in the Control bar and Object › Transform, so the tutorial's step couldn't be done from Properties.

## Change
- **Angle and scale fields:** rotation and shear angles beside Scale X and Scale Y, filled from `transform.info`. Editing one sets that total through `transform.set` around the panel's reference point, as the Control bar does.
- **Buttons:** Rotate 90° Clockwise and Counterclockwise run `transform.rotate`; Flip Horizontal and Vertical run `transform.flip`.
  - The icons are original drawings: an arc over a square, and a shape mirrored across a dashed axis.
  - Each button reports its name to screen readers.
- **Unchanged:** the "…" still opens the Info panel.

## Screenshot
The tutorial's petal after Flip Horizontal and Flip Vertical:

![Properties Transform](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/properties-transform/after.png)

## Tests
- `transform_flips_and_rotates_from_properties`: Flip Horizontal mirrors the frame; Flip Vertical then makes it a half turn (`transform.info` 180°); Rotate 90° Clockwise from there gives 90°, shown in the rotation field.

title: Preserve typing formats in trailing blank paragraphs

title: UI: quitting asks to save documents with unsaved changes
author: aiongg
body:
Addresses #544 for window close and application/menu quit. Dock Quit remains open.

- Closing the window, choosing Quit from the application menu, or using Cmd+Q/Ctrl+Q asks about each document with unsaved changes: Save, Don't Save or Cancel.
- No document is discarded until every quit decision is complete and still current. A later Cancel, cancelled Save As, or failed save keeps all documents open and restores the original active tab. Explicit saves already completed remain saved.
- Approvals are bound to document identity and revision; later edits or newly opened unsaved documents are checked again before closing.
- With no unsaved documents, the app quits immediately. The control channel's `app.quit` still quits without prompting so automation does not wait on a dialog.
- macOS uses a normal Quit menu command instead of the predefined item that terminated the app directly.

**Scope:** this PR does not provide a cancelable macOS Dock Quit prompt. The pinned window backend does not expose the required native termination interception. Orderly-exit recovery is a separate follow-up; this PR does not close all of #544.

Validation: full `cargo xtask ci` on the refreshed candidate (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, native tests, assets, layers and WASM compilation), fourteen quit regressions, and three inspected offscreen screenshots. Cases cover later Cancel after Don't Save, cancelled/failed saves, active-tab changes, retained recovery, stale approvals, late edits and new documents. Physical Dock Quit was not tested.

title: SVG text: find fonts by PostScript name (#430)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
About the five lines in #430:

Lines 1 to 4 already work on current main. Placed SVG text started using installed and shared fonts with #116, which landed after 0.5.0.

Line 5 (`font-family="Source Serif 4"`) is invalid CSS: an unquoted family name can't start with a digit, so the whole value is dropped, and browsers drop it too. Quoting it works: `font-family="'Source Serif 4'"`.

What was still missing is a font named by its PostScript name, like `font-family="'MyriadPro-Regular'"` or `SourceSerif4-Semibold`. Illustrator writes names like that in its SVG export. usvg only matches family names, so such text fell back to the serif default.

The fix: when a name in `font-family` matches no family, `select_font` now looks for a face with that PostScript name (ignoring case). It checks the SVG's font database (bundled fonts) first, then the shared fonts, loaded or installed. Installed fonts are found through the catalog without loading them first. To support that, `designcraft-fonts` now records PostScript names: the font scan reads them into the catalog, `FontFace::postscript_name()` reads them on first use, and the lookup is `FontDb::postscript_face()`.

A PostScript name selects exactly that face, so font-weight and font-style don't change it. The name already says which weight and style to use, and switching to another face of the family would contradict it. Families listed earlier in `font-family` still win, generic families resolve as before, and an unknown name falls back the same way as before. Named instances of variable fonts aren't matched by PostScript name, since the file's name table only holds the default instance's name.

Tests: `svg_text_finds_fonts_by_postscript_name` in designcraft-images covers a bundled face (quoted, and in lowercase), a shared font, weight and style being ignored, list order, family-name lookup and the unknown-name fallback. It failed before the fix: `SourceSerif4-Semibold` came out as `SourceSerif4-Regular`. `installed_and_loaded…

title: Transform values act on a selected placed graphic, not its frame
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to make this BEAUTIFUL and EASY InDesign Layouts, Episode 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g0u13YjK0Cs). At 3:48 the image placed into a frame tilted at −45° comes in tilted as well. The narrator says: "we can double click into the image and then simply change this into zero".

## Problem
Double-clicking a frame (or Direct Selection, or `selection.set {content: true}`) selects the placed graphic, and `transform.info` reports its values separately. But `transform.set`, which the Transform panel, Control bar and Properties use, always transformed the frame. Setting rotation 0 with the image selected turned the whole frame upright, and the tutorial's pills with it.

## Fix
`transform.set` acts on the placed graphic inside each frame when the selection is content, or when `content: true` is passed. The frame stays where it is.
- **Rotation, shear, scaleX/scaleY:** absolute, about the reference point of the graphic's bounds. They are measured the same way `transform.info` reports `content`: on the pasteboard with Transformations are Totals on, otherwise relative to the frame.
- **x, y, width, height:** the graphic's bounds on the page, as InDesign's content values are.
- **Undo:** one step, like the frame version.
- **No graphic:** frames without a placed graphic are skipped. If none of the targets holds one, it's an error rather than a silent no-op.
- **Unchanged:** a frame selection (or `content: false`) works exactly as before.

This matches #415 (moving a placed graphic inside its frame), which adds the same `content` rule to `transform.move`. The two are independent, and both are needed for the tutorial's step: straighten the image, then drag it into place.

## Tests
- `rotating_the_content_leaves_the_frame_as_it_is`: a frame at −45° with an image. With the content selected, rotation 0 leaves the frame at −45° and makes the image upright; scale 50% acts on the image; undo restores it. Without the fix …

title: Unnamed colours apply to selected text
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to make this BEAUTIFUL and EASY InDesign Layouts, Episode 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g0u13YjK0Cs). At 6:30 the narrator says "I'm going to go into my text box, highlight the text, … double click on that box right there and then paste in the same color": they paste a hex colour into the Color Picker with text selected.

- **One undo step**, through the same targets as Character formatting. At a caret in an empty story, the colour applies to what is typed next.
- **Objects:** an object selection works as before.
- **Enabled when:** objects, text or table cells are selected.

The Color Picker dialog (opened from the Swatches panel) needed no change: with text selected, its OK now colours the text.

title: Double-clicking the Fill or Stroke box opens the Color Picker
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to make this BEAUTIFUL and EASY InDesign Layouts, Episode 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g0u13YjK0Cs). At 5:28 the on-screen caption reads "Double Click Box to go Into Fill Options": the narrator double-clicks the Fill box in the Tools panel and picks the blue in the Color Picker. They do it again at 6:39 and 8:57 to colour text.

## Problem
In InDesign, double-clicking the Tools panel's Fill or Stroke box opens the Color Picker. DesignCraft opened the Swatches panel instead. The Color Picker itself existed, but it could only be reached by double-clicking a chip in the Swatches panel.

## Change
`toolbar::fill_stroke_proxy`:
- **Double-click:** opens the Color Picker for the box double-clicked, Fill or Stroke. When the boxes overlap, the box in front wins.
- **Starting colour:** the selection's current fill or stroke, or the selected text's colour when text is selected.
- **Accessibility:** the Stroke box reports its name to screen readers, as the Fill box already did.

OK in the picker runs `object.color`, as before. With #551, that also colours selected text. This PR doesn't depend on #551: with objects selected it works on main.

title: Sections: the section marker shows the section's marker text
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #556.

- A section marker character shows the marker text of the section its page belongs to; parent-page items composed for a page use that page's section. A section with no marker shows nothing; parent pages themselves show "Section".
- Changing a section's marker recomposes the frames that show it.

Test: two sections, one with a marker, a parent-page frame and a document-page frame with the marker; renaming the marker updates both.

title: IDML: font family names keep their spaces; FontStyle "Nothing" inherits
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #558.

- `AppliedFont` keeps the family name as written (a family whose name ends in a space matches its font); lookups try the name as written, then trimmed, then without a format suffix.
- `FontStyle="Nothing"` leaves the style unset, so it inherits; export doesn't write "Nothing".

Tests: a family name with a trailing space resolves to that family, and a trimmed name still falls back; an IDML with `FontStyle="Nothing"` inherits the paragraph's style before and after a round trip.

title: Images: clipping paths from IDML clip the image on screen and in PDF
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #450.

- A placed graphic can carry a clipping path (`Graphic.clip`): its kind (detect edges, alpha channel, Photoshop path, user-modified), the path in the graphic's space, and the IDML options (invert, include inside edges, restrict to frame, threshold, tolerance, inset). Documents without one load and save unchanged.
- IDML import reads `ClippingPathSettings` and `ClippingPathGeometry`; export writes them back.
- The canvas, raster export and PDF export clip the image to the path inside the frame clip; an inverted path clips to the outside.
- `object.clippingPathOptions` reports the clipping path, inverts it or removes it (Object › Clipping Path › None).

Tests: IDML import and round trip; a pixel outside the path shows paper and one inside shows the image (and the reverse when inverted); PDF output has the clip; the command with undo.

Follow-ups: a Clipping Path Options dialog, and text wrap Same As Clipping following the path once contour wrap (#384) lands.

title: IDML: anchored objects take unset settings from their object style; left-aligned X offsets read in the layout's direction
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #555.

- Each anchored-object attribute missing from an item's own `AnchoredObjectSetting` comes from its object style chain (applied style, its BasedOn styles, `[None]`), and only then from the IDML defaults.
- `attr_or_style` reads every item attribute it resolves (fill colour, tint and overprint, and the stroke attributes) through the same chain: applied object style, its BasedOn styles, then `[None]`. IDML documents keep their defaults on `[None]`, so an item that sets nothing takes them from there.
- For a left-aligned custom anchored object, IDML stores the X offset with the opposite sign: import negates it so a positive offset moves the object right, and export writes it back. Centre- and right-aligned offsets keep their sign.
- A rotated group's bounds are its children's outlines under the full transform. They were the box of the children's rotated boxes, which overstated them and placed rotated anchored groups off their position. This changes `Item::bounds()` for every group, so selection boxes, align and distribute use the tighter bounds too.

Tests: settings from `[None]`, a local attribute overriding the style, a BasedOn chain; left-, zero- and centre-aligned offsets on import, in the composed position, and after a round trip; a rotated group of rotated children (`rotated_group_bounds_follow_the_children_outlines`).

title: Text wrap: anchored objects wrap text
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #557.

- Anchored objects with text wrap push away the text of other stories on the same spread, like page items.
- Custom and above-line anchored objects also wrap their own story's lines after their anchor; inline objects stay in their line. The story is composed again until the objects stop moving, at most four extra passes.
- Canvas, PDF and the commands share the same composition; the cache key and signature include the stories that wrap a story, and editing a story with wrapping objects repaints the frames it wraps.
- With no wrapping anchored objects the layout is unchanged (one scan of the stories' anchored objects per composition).

Tests: another story's text wraps and follows the object when it moves; its own story's later lines wrap while the anchor line stays; no wrap gives identical lines; a Jump Object case with vertical centring terminates; damage covers the wrapped story's frame.

title: Swatches: Load Swatches refuses .ase files over 100,000 colors and merges in linear time
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`ase::read` accepted any number of colors in a swatch exchange file, and `swatch.load` looked up each incoming name with a linear search through the document's swatches. In a test build, loading 25,000 colors used 0.7 s of CPU, 50,000 used 2.5 s and 100,000 (a 5.2 MB file) used 9.6 s. No limit applied to larger files.

- `ase::read` returns an error ("the file holds more than 100000 colors") for a file with more than `ase::MAX_COLORS` (100,000) colors. vectorcraft (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/644) and photocraft limit their `.ase` readers to 100,000 entries as well.
- `load_swatches` looks up each name's first swatch in a `HashMap` and indexes each color it adds. The 100,000-color file now loads in under 0.1 s. The merge follows the same rules as before: names already in the document are kept unless `replace` is set, a name repeated in the file matches its first copy, and a locked swatch is left unchanged.
- The change adds one line to the Progress log in `ROADMAP.md`.
- `contributors/people.toml` gets my own entry, in its own commit.

Validation:
- `ase::tests::more_than_max_colors_is_an_error` fails without the limit (100,001 colors read as `Ok`).
- `cmd::style::color_tests::loading_swatches_matches_the_first_swatch_of_each_name` checks the merge with and without `replace` for two swatches of one name, a hidden unnamed color, a name repeated in the file and `[Black]`. It passes before and after the change.
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-color --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo xtask ci` passes its 6 steps: 1,190 tests passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.

title: Blend modes don't blend with the paper
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while rebuilding the page from the InDesign tutorial [How to make this BEAUTIFUL and EASY InDesign Layouts, Episode 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY). At 9:03 it sets a column of black "INDESIGN" text to Color Dodge, "so that when it meets that [the image] it changes color". Where the text runs over blank paper it stays black.

## Problem
The renderer (canvas and raster export) painted the paper, then blended page items with it, as if the paper were an object. So black text in Color Dodge over blank paper dodged the white to white and vanished, and other blend modes were affected the same way.

In InDesign the paper isn't a backdrop: over blank paper an object in any blend mode shows as it is, and only the objects below it are blended with. PDF works the same way, since the page group starts transparent, and DesignCraft's PDF export, which paints no paper, already matched.

## Fix
`render::draw_spread`: on spreads where any item, or a parent-page item, uses a blend mode other than Normal, the items are drawn in their own transparent group, which is then laid over the paper once. Spreads without blend modes render exactly as before.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/blend-over-paper/before.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/blend-over-paper/after.png) |

(Black text in Color Dodge across a photo and blank paper. Before, it vanished over the paper.)

## Tests
- `render/tests/blend_over_paper.rs`: black in Color Dodge stays black over blank paper and still blends over a coloured rectangle; Normal is unchanged. Before the fix, the pixel over the paper is white (255).
- Render (golden images included), engine, PDF and UI tests pass (except `package_refuses_windows_directory_redirects`, which needs symlink privilege this Windows account lacks); clippy is clean.

title: Styles: Load Styles from another document or IDML file
author: noah1400
body:
Styles could not be taken from one document into another, so a client's styles had to be rebuilt in every new file (point 1 in #405).

- **Panels:** the Paragraph Styles and Character Styles panels get a menu with Load Paragraph Styles… / Load Character Styles… and Load All Text Styles….

- **What comes along:** the styles a loaded style names (based on, next style, nested, line and GREP styles), the swatches it uses (a tint with its base colour), named lists and export tags. A style that only comes along never replaces one the document has, and swatches the document has stay as they are.
- **Commands:** `style.load {path | base64, name?, paragraph?, character?, conflicts?}` does it in one undo step and reports what was added, replaced and renamed. `style.load.list` lists a file's styles and which ones clash. A load that changes nothing leaves no undo step, and one that would make two styles based on each other is refused.

title: Eyedropper: sample a placed image's colour into the selected text or objects
author: moppeeer
body:

In InDesign you can select some text, switch to the Eyedropper (I) and click a photo. The text takes the image's colour under the pointer. title: Step and Repeat: InDesign's dialog with Create as a grid and Preview

**Before:** Edit › Step and Repeat… (⌥⌘U) opened the generic command form. Its fields were `Count` (hint "1..1000"), `Dx`, `Dy`, `Rows`, `Columns` and `Ids`, with offsets in bare points and no preview.

title: Effects panel: the level row, Isolate Blending and Knockout Group
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign's Effects panel shows two things DesignCraft's lacked:
- **A level row:** it names what the settings apply to, with its blend mode and opacity. In LYH Studio's poster tutorial this reads "Group: Color Dodge 100%" after Color Dodge is set on the grouped text ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY), 5:37).

title: Fix: white text invisible when selected
author: vxkj1211
body:
## Summary
- `draw_inverse_highlight` filled the selection background with opaque black and inverted the glyph colour, so white text on a dark backdrop (dark frame fill, a photo behind the frame, etc.) turned into black-on-black and disappeared when selected
- The selection highlight now inverts against the colour actually painted under the selection: the page is rendered off-screen at low resolution and the selection bounds are sampled (`sampled_background`), so solid fills, gradients, images and items painted below the frame all invert correctly
- Selected glyphs keep their inverse colour, so black text on paper still selects as white-on-black (the 67ac9f1 behaviour is unchanged for the common case) and white text on a dark backdrop now selects as black-on-white

## Root cause
- `canvas.rs` inverted the glyph colour against a fixed opaque-black highlight: white glyphs became black on black
- A first attempt (semi-transparent highlight, original glyph colour) was rejected in review because it degraded the common black-text-on-paper case; the second attempt inverted solid-fill colours only and missed image backdrops

## Validation
- `cargo xtask ci` fully green (fmt, clippy -D warnings, full workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm32)
- Manual: white text over an image backdrop, a black frame fill, and a black rectangle painted below the frame all stay visible while selected; black text on paper selects as before

title: Gradient feather on a group: fade it on screen, and don't hide it in PDF
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

LYH Studio's poster tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY), 5:52) groups 14 lines of "LYH+STUDIO". It then drags the Gradient Feather tool over the group so the lines fade towards the bottom. DesignCraft stored the feather (`object.gradientFeather` on the group) but did not draw it correctly:

- **Screen / PNG:** no fade at all. Groups never went through the effects path (`draw_item_fx` is only reached by leaf items).
- **PDF:** the whole group disappeared. The luminosity mask covered `it.inner_bounds()`, the bounds of the item's own path. A group has no path of its own, so the mask was a box of zero size and everything else was masked out.
- **Feather by angle (no drag):** the gradient's ends were computed from that same empty box.

The fix:
- **`Item::feather_bounds()`:** the box a gradient feather spans. That is the path's bounds, or for a group its objects' bounds.
- **Render:** a feathered group draws its objects in one layer, then fades that layer with the same mask as other objects. The mask is factored out as `fx::gradient_feather_mask`. It is padded for text and strokes that reach past their frames. It sits inside the group's blend/opacity layer, so Color Dodge and other blend modes still apply to the faded result.
- **PDF:** the group's mask spans its objects, with the same padding.
- ROADMAP progress-log line added.

Not in this PR: the other soft effects (drop shadow, glows, satin and so on) are still drawn only on leaf objects, not on groups. That would be a follow-up.

title: IDML: tracked deleted text takes no room in the layout
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #581.

- Text in `<Change ChangeType="DeletedText">` imports as text marked deleted; inserted and moved text is marked inserted.
- Composition skips a paragraph whose text is all deleted along with its return (or the return before it): no lines, spacing or list number; for keep options it stands in for the paragraph before it.
- Export writes the marks back as `Change` elements, including a deleted paragraph return.

Test: a story with a deleted word, a deleted empty Keep With Next paragraph and inserted text composes the same lines as the story without the deletions, and the marks survive an export round trip.

Not covered yet: a deleted return between two paragraphs that both keep live text doesn't join them.

title: Footnotes: notes stack baseline to baseline
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #582.

- Each footnote keeps its first and last baselines, its first line's leading and its last line's descent. A note's first baseline sits at the previous note's last baseline plus Space Between plus its own first-line leading; only the last note's descent counts toward the area's height.
- The space reserved while composing and the placement at the end use the same height, so body text fills the page up to the notes.

Test: four one-line notes (Space Between 0 and 3) sit exactly leading plus Space Between apart, the area's height matches, and the body's last line fits above the notes where one more line wouldn't.

title: Hyphenation Zone applies to the Single-line Composer only
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, the **Hyphenation Zone** (Hyphenation Settings, default 3p0) applies only to unjustified text set with the **Single-line Composer**. Adobe's help describes it as "the amount of white space allowed at the end of a line of unjustified text before hyphenation begins", for the Single-line Composer only. The default **Paragraph Composer** ignores it and weighs every break in the paragraph instead.

DesignCraft applied the zone with both composers. So in ragged paragraphs set with the default Paragraph Composer, it refused hyphens that InDesign makes.

This showed up while rebuilding LYH Studio's poster tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY)): two columns of placeholder text in Minion Pro 12/14.4, 0.1667 in gutter, left aligned.
- **InDesign breaks:** "porpo-runt", "aper-natem", "mosticsia-tur" and "ommo-luptat".
- **DesignCraft before this PR:** it hyphenated only "porpo-runt" and "ommo-luptat", moved whole words to the next line instead, and ran one line longer.
- **After this PR:** column 2 matches InDesign line for line, and 45 of the 46 lines match overall. The one exception is "dollute-cat": InDesign hyphenates it although the whole word fits with about 5 pt to spare, a rag choice its Paragraph Composer makes differently from ours.

The fix: `spacing_for` passes the zone to the breaker only for unjustified Single-line Composer paragraphs. A Paragraph Composer paragraph that falls back to the greedy breaker (tabs, very long paragraphs) still doesn't use it. The setting itself, and its IDML import and export, are unchanged.

title: CMYK blend space: blend modes blend in CMYK on screen
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign blends a print document's transparency in its transparency blend space, which is CMYK by default (Edit › Transparency Blend Space). That changes what blend modes do. In CMYK a blend mode works on each ink, and a subtractive space blends the complements. So:
- **100% K text in Color Dodge** turns a coloured area under it white: black's cyan, magenta and yellow are 0, their complements 1, so the dodge clears those inks.
- **Over paper** the same text stays black, because blend modes don't blend with the paper.

LYH Studio's poster tutorial relies on this ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY), 10:07): a column of black "INDESIGN" lines in Color Dodge turns white where it crosses the lilac photo.

DesignCraft's PDF export already gives such pages a DeviceCMYK page group, so viewers blend correctly. On screen, though, vello blends in RGB, and dodging with black barely changes anything. The existing CMYK view then only passes the finished RGB image through the working CMYK profile.

## How

New `render::blendspace` module. Separable blend formulas work channel by channel, and a subtractive space blends the complements of the inks. So when a spread in a CMYK blend space has anything transparent, it is drawn twice through the ordinary renderer:

1. **C, M, Y pass:** a new internal plate mode, 4, paints each colour's cyan, magenta and yellow complements into R, G and B. vello then applies every blend mode, opacity, group, mask and effect to them as usual, so that is the CMY blend.
2. **K pass:** plate 3 paints the black complement into a second raster in the same way.
3. **Back to the screen:** the four inks are converted to sRGB once, through a new 9⁴ CMYK → sRGB table built from the working colour settings. With Display all blacks as rich black, 100% K shows as 0/0/0. The result goes over the paper and canvas background; the paper is never part of the backdrop.

This covers parent-page items, blended objects inside groups, effect blends (a…

title: (fix)Small frame wrap for overset small text boxes
author: seanth
body:
Text wrap: small single-character frames (tombstones) are set

An article’s closing tombstone, a one-character text frame (e.g. a 7.6 pt symbol in a 10.5 pt box), shows nothing (overset) whenever its spread has a text-wrap object anywhere, while InDesign sets it. Two causes: every text frame took every wrap object on its spread, overlapping or not; and free_slot’s minimum gap (1.5 em of the paragraph’s size, meant for slivers beside a wrapped object) also applied when nothing cut the line, so with a 14 pt paragraph style no line fit a frame under 21 pt. Now only overlapping objects wrap a frame, and the minimum only applies to gaps a wrap cut.

Tests: small_single_character_frame_sets_beside_unrelated_text_wrap, narrow_frame_sets_lines_no_wrap_object_reaches (fail before, pass after). On a real InDesign document with 12 tombstones, all 12 are set and no other story’s layout changes. Addresses #587 and probably(?) also fixes #476.

title: Move a placed graphic inside its frame: content grabber and Direct Selection
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign you reposition a placed image inside its frame in either of two ways:
- **The content grabber:** the ring that appears at the centre of a graphic frame while the Selection tool is over it.
- **Direct Selection:** dragging the image with that tool.

LYH Studio's poster tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY), 8:20) does exactly this: "if I click in the center of this I can drag this guy up and down".

In DesignCraft both gestures moved the frame, because `transform.move` always moves objects even when the selection is the frame's content. There was no way to move only the graphic, from the GUI or from commands.

This PR adds:
- **`transform.move {content?: bool}`:**
  - The placed graphic of each frame moves in the frame's inner space, so a rotated or scaled frame follows the pointer on the page. The frame stays put, and locked frames stay.
  - It defaults to whether the selection is content, when no `ids` are given. Frames without a graphic move as before, so a Direct Selection drag of a text frame still moves the frame.
- **Selection tool:**
  - Over a graphic frame, the content grabber ring shows at the frame's centre and the cursor becomes a hand.
  - Dragging the ring selects the graphic (Direct Selection style) and moves it. Shift constrains. Elsewhere on the frame, dragging still moves the frame.
- **Direct Selection:** dragging a placed graphic moves it inside its frame. Shift-click still toggles, and Alt-drag still duplicates.
- ROADMAP progress-log line added.

The same drag, from the frame's centre upwards.

title: Double-click a frame handle to fit the frame to its content; Fit Frame to Content fits text frames
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, double-clicking a selection handle fits the frame to its content:
- a corner handle fits both sides;
- a top or bottom handle fits the height;
- a left or right handle fits the width.

LYH Studio's poster tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ibk1UOyWqY), 9:30) does this: "double click the edge right there". It fits the INDESIGN text frame around its line before snapping it into the page corner.

In DesignCraft:
- Double-clicking a handle of a text frame switched to the Type tool.
- Object › Fitting › Fit Frame to Content (`object.fit {mode: fitFrameToContent}`) fitted graphic frames only and skipped text frames.

This PR adds:
- **Selection tool:** a double-click on a selection handle runs `object.fit {mode: fitFrameToContent, axis}`. The axis is `both` for a corner, `height` for the top or bottom handle, `width` for a side. A double-click inside a text frame still switches to the Type tool.
- **`object.fit` Fit Frame to Content on text frames:**
  - The bottom goes to the last line's descent and the right side to the longest line's end, plus the insets; the top-left stays.
  - The width is fitted only for one-column frames.
  - Overset text grows the frame first: the text is composed on a copy with a tall frame.
  - It applies to horizontal frames that end their thread only. Vertical, type-on-path and earlier threaded frames are left as they are.
  - The new `axis` option is checked (an unknown value is an error), and graphic frames fit as before.
- ROADMAP progress-log line added.

## Before / after

An oversized text frame holding "INDESIGN", selected, then its bottom-right handle double-clicked.

title: Toolbox Fill/Stroke proxy works on text; Shift+X, D, X, / and J
author: moppeeer
body:
The toolbox Fill/Stroke proxy follows the selected text, or the text of selected text frames when Formatting Affects Text is enabled. Swap, Default and Apply None update that target through commands. With a non-text object selected, those operations keep editing the object even when J is on.

- Shift+X swaps fill and stroke; D restores defaults; X selects the front colour well; / applies None. Single-key shortcuts stay inactive while typing.
- J and the toolbox formatting buttons use `app.formattingAffectsText {on?: bool}`, backed by `UiState::formatting_affects_text` and `panels::colors_affect_text`. These are the same command/state/helper interfaces used by #84, so integration can retain one formatting target.
- Text selection targets text automatically. The explicit formatting flag targets whole text-frame stories only when a text frame is selected; it never sends rectangle edits to an empty text target.
- UI labels are translated, and the roadmap entry describes the target behavior.

This branch is standalone on main. #84 contains broader text-editing, caret-formatting and panel support; when combining them, retain its shared formatting implementation and these proxy shortcuts.

The existing Windows package-redirect test also gains a junction fallback for OS error 1314 (missing symlink privilege). It still tests an actual directory reparse point and verifies that no file is written outside the package.

title: Canvas: arrow keys and Tab keep keyboard focus on the canvas
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes the view jumping in #594.

- While the canvas has keyboard focus, arrow keys, Tab and Escape stay with it. Before, an arrow key moved focus to the nearest button in that direction (often the status bar's spread buttons) while typing went on, and the next Space or Return pressed that button: the view moved to another spread or back to the first one.
