title: Ctrl/Cmd + the + key zooms the canvas, not the whole window
author: PiMinusMax
body:
On a German keyboard (KDE Plasma, Linux), Ctrl and the + key scaled the whole window instead of zooming the canvas, and the window snapped back right away. Ctrl+- zoomed the canvas as it should.

**Cause:** Zoom In's shortcut is `Cmd+=`, which matches `Key::Equals`. A German keyboard has its own + key, so the press arrives as `Key::Plus`. Shift+= on a US keyboard arrives the same way. No shortcut matched, so egui's built-in keyboard zoom (`Options::zoom_with_keyboard`, on by default) took the key and changed `zoom_factor` for the whole UI. On the next frame, `DesignApp::logic` set it back to the UI-scale preference. Ctrl+- worked because `Key::Minus` is the same on both layouts and `shortcuts()` consumes it first.

**Change:**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`: in `shortcuts()`, `Key::Plus` also matches shortcuts bound to `=` (Zoom In, and Fit Selection in Window with Alt). Shift is ignored for that match, so Shift+= on a US keyboard works too.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: `zoom_with_keyboard` is off. The UI scale is a preference, so egui's Cmd+Plus/Minus/0 can only make the window jump.

**Test:** `cmd_plus_zooms_the_canvas_not_the_window` presses Cmd+Plus, Cmd+Shift+Plus, Cmd+= and Cmd+-. Each one has to change the canvas zoom in the right direction and leave `zoom_factor` alone.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm; 1377 tests), on top of main e862e0a.

title: Save: delegate atomic writes to craft-atomic
author: aiongg
body:
- `crates/engine/src/atomic.rs` keeps `write_atomic`, `write_atomic_with` and `write_file` with the same signatures; their bodies call `craft_atomic::atomic_write` / `atomic_write_with`. No call site changes, so this merges independently of #604.
- `craft-atomic` comes from storytold/craft-libs, pinned by `rev` like `craft-print` (`e9546e191dd62f2bc1d61eca45dbdc2f1b3c1d8e`). It is a native-only dependency of the engine, next to `tempfile`; the module is still not built for wasm.
- Kept in DesignCraft: `write_file` maps errors to `EngineError` (craft-atomic's messages already name the path and say whether the original was kept), and `write_atomic_with` turns a panicking writer into an error so the temporary file is removed. Recovery checkpoints and package output keep their own writers: they refuse redirected entries and replace links instead of following them, which craft-atomic does not offer.
- Permissions are unchanged for saved and exported files: a new file follows the umask and a replaced file keeps its permissions. Staging files are named `.<name>.<pid>-<n>.craft_tmp`.

Tests: the existing atomic tests pass against craft-atomic (replacement without leftovers, a failed write keeps the original, long names, new files follow the umask, replaced files keep their mode, read-only files and folders, symlinks and link loops, rename retry, a panicking writer). `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run -p designcraft-engine`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Dialogs: drag the title to move the window
author: aiongg
body:
- Pressing on a dialog's title row and dragging moves the dialog. This lets you see the page behind it, for example the New Document preview (#683, #679). The row shows the grab cursor; widgets in the body (fields, sliders, text selection, scrolling) behave as before.
- The About window moves the same way by its tab row; the tabs stay clickable.
- The dialog stays modal with the same backdrop.
- A dragged dialog may go partly off-screen. Its title row stays inside the window vertically, and at least 100 px of it stays inside horizontally. A dialog that has not been dragged is kept inside the window as before.
- A dialog opens centred. It keeps its position while it is open, also when its content resizes. Another dialog, the same one opened again, or a resize of the window centres it again, so OK and Cancel stay reachable.
- Both hosts use one helper, `crates/ui-egui/src/modal_drag.rs`: the modal stays anchored at the centre and is shifted by an offset kept in egui's temporary memory, limited every frame against the current window.

Tests: a kittest test drags the Create Table dialog's title by (100, 60) and the dialog moves by that; a drag in the body leaves it in place; a drag far past the top edge keeps the title row inside; reopened, it is centred again; dragged by (-900, 0), 100 px of it stays inside the left edge. The existing resize test (dialogs at three window sizes keep the title, OK and Cancel visible) passes. `cargo clippy -p designcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`, the dialog and About tests, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Scripts: GREP replacements like `$1` stay literal
author: aiongg
body:
- A script string is looked up as a whole-value reference only when it is exactly `$` + step number or `last` + zero or more `.segment` (letters, digits, `_`, `-`). Any other string starting with `$` stays as written, so a GREP replacement such as `$1` followed by a nonbreaking space no longer fails the script with "bad reference".
- `$$` writes a literal `$` anywhere in a string: `"$$1"` passes the bare GREP group `$1`, and `"$${0.id}"` passes `${0.id}` unchanged.
- `${N.path}` interpolation and the "unclosed `${`" error work as before.
- The `designcraft-cli script --help` reference, the MCP `batch` tool description and `docs/agents.md` describe both rules.

Fixes #749.

Tests: `script::tests::only_well_formed_references_resolve` (literal `$` strings, `$$`, references and interpolation) and `script::tests::a_script_grep_change_keeps_its_group_reference` (end-to-end `find.change` GREP script on "a v Praze"; fails before the fix with "bad reference").

title: Colour management on craft-cms
author: aiongg
body:
- ICC transforms in `designcraft-color` go through `craft-cms` from storytold/craft-libs (pinned at e9546e1, like craft-print): the built-in RGB working spaces, user `.icc` files, Lab conversion, gamut error and soft-proofing of ICC CMYK spaces. The Generic CMYK output profile is encoded by craft-cms. `moxcms` is no longer a direct dependency of `designcraft-color`.

Related: #684

**Tests:** new tests pin the default CMYK swatches to reference values (0/50/100/0 → 243,146,0; 0/60/100/0 → 239,124,0; K100 → 28,28,27; C+M → 48,38,131), saved-name handling and the output intent. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace` (1379 passed), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask assets`.

title: New Swatch names a gradient "New Gradient Swatch"; gradient swatches from colour swatches
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign's Swatches panel **New Swatch** button takes what is current:
- a gradient built in the Gradient panel becomes a swatch named **"New Gradient Swatch"**. It is listed, and the object keeps using it.
- an unnamed colour (mixed in the Color panel) becomes a listed swatch;
- a named swatch selected in the panel is duplicated as "… copy".

LYH Studio's gradient tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38QZEZ5ZpP0), episode 6) does this at 2:09: "we want to make sure that we actually create a new swatch for it … a new gradient Swatch pops up". The rest of the page then uses that swatch: the background, the circles, the "1969" text and the loop's stroke.

On main, New Swatch always adds the same orange colour swatch. There's no way to make a gradient swatch at all: `swatch.create` takes only a colour, and gradients edited in the Gradient panel stay unnamed and unlisted.

## How

**Engine (`cmd/style.rs`):**
- `swatch.new {swatch?, target?: fill|stroke}` is InDesign's New Swatch. It takes `swatch`, or the selection's fill (or stroke):
  - an unnamed gradient is listed under "New Gradient Swatch" (with a number if taken) and stays applied, through `swatch.addToSwatches`;
  - an unnamed colour is listed under its own name;
  - a listed swatch is duplicated as "<name> copy";
  - `[None]` and `[Registration]` are refused.
- `swatch.create {name?, gradient: {kind?, stops: [{location, swatch | color, opacity?, midpoint?}]}}` makes a named gradient swatch. Stops take a colour swatch by name, as dragging a swatch onto the Gradient panel's stop does. A stop naming a gradient or a missing swatch is refused, as are fewer than two stops and an unknown kind.

**Swatches panel:** New Swatch runs `swatch.new`. With nothing selected it still adds a colour, as before.

Docs (target-app parity) and ROADMAP updated.

## Before / after

A circle with a magenta-to-cyan gradient made with `object.gradient` (as the Gradient panel does), then New Swatch:

| Before (main)…

title: Swatches: dropping an .ase file on the window loads its swatches
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`open_dropped` sent every dropped file that is not a document to `file.place`, so a swatch exchange (`.ase`) file dropped on the desktop window failed with a "Can't Place the File" alert: "invalid parameters for `file.place`: unsupported or corrupt image".

Validation:

- On macOS, `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo xtask ci` passes fmt and clippy and stops at the test step, where `backend::tests::remote_executes_once_when_app_restarts_between_calls` in `designcraft-mcp` fails with `WouldBlock`. title: Radial gradients stretch with the object's box (an ellipse), as InDesign draws them
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign draws a radial gradient in the object's bounding box. On a non-square frame it's an **ellipse** that reaches the frame's sides as well as its top and bottom, and a Gradient Swatch tool drag keeps the box's proportions.

LYH Studio's gradient tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38QZEZ5ZpP0), episode 6) switches the left page's background to Radial at 3:16. It's magenta in the middle and cyan at every edge of the page: "more of a circular gradient … a nice blend of a blue and a pink". It stays that shape while the centre is moved with the Gradient Swatch tool (3:23–3:35).

DesignCraft drew a circle with a radius of half the longer side. On a portrait page it reached cyan only at the top and bottom, and the sides stayed purple.

## How

- **doc:** `Fill::radial_ellipse(bounds)` returns the gradient's centre and its horizontal and vertical radii:
  - by default, the box's centre and half its width and height;
  - with a Gradient Swatch tool vector, the vector's start, with its length measured as if the box were square, so a drag keeps the box's proportions.
- **render:** the radial paint is that circle, stretched by the paint transform.
- **PDF:** the radial shading gets the same stretch through its transform.

The stored vectors are unchanged (IDML round-trips as before). Docs (target-app parity) and ROADMAP are updated.

## Before / after

A 612 × 792 pt rectangle with a magenta-to-cyan radial gradient:

| Before (main): a circle; the sides stay purple | After: the frame's ellipse | InDesign (the video, 3:21) |
|---|---|---|

title: EPUB/HTML: anchored objects are exported where they are anchored
author: switch87
body: Fixes #766. An image anchored in a story was missing from both `file.exportEpub` and `file.exportHtml`. `story_html` dropped the object mark (U+E00E, filtered with the other private-use marks), and `reading_order` only walks page items, while an anchored object lives in `Story::objects`. ## Changes - **`story_html_with`** splits each run's text at the object marks and writes the markup for the matching `Story::objects` entry in place of each mark. - **`body_html`** uses it for every story: - An inline (or custom-positioned) object's graphics go into the paragraph as ``. - An above-line object becomes `` with its alignment. - Groups are walked, so graphics inside an anchored group are written too. - **`graphic_html`:** the free-graphic code (the `` or HTML5 player, file registration, alt text) is split out, so free figures and anchored objects share it. Free figures export as before. - **`story_html`** on its own keeps leaving objects out, as before. It has no package to put the images in. ## Tests - `anchored_objects_are_exported_in_place`: - An inline object lands between A and B, and an above-line one, centred, between C and D. - The image is in the package, and the single-file HTML has both. - The `designcraft-epub` tests and the engine's `epub` tests pass, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt are clean. - The issue's repro on this branch: `OEBPS/images/10.png` is in the EPUB, and the XHTML has `First paragraph before the figure.` The alt text still falls back to the file name, as for free figures; that is #774.

title: EPUB/HTML: list paragraphs share one ul/ol, and pre lines one block
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #767.

`story_html` wrote each paragraph as its own element with its style's export tag. So `li` paragraphs came out without a list around them, and every line of a `pre` style was a separate `<pre>`.

- **Lists:** consecutive `li` paragraphs share one list.
  - A style with a numbered list type gets `ol`, a bulleted one `ul`.
  - A style without a list type of its own (bullets typed in the text) gets `<ul style="list-style:none">`, so its items don't get a second marker.
  - A change of list type closes one list and opens the next.
- **Preformatted text:** consecutive `pre` paragraphs of the same style and direction are one `<pre>`, with their lines separated by newlines. The block closes at the next paragraph that isn't one of its lines.

Test: `lists_and_preformatted_blocks_are_grouped` covers a bulleted list, then a numbered one, a two-line `pre` block followed by a `p`, and a typed-bullet `li`. It fails without the change. The `designcraft-epub` tests pass, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt are clean.

title: EPUB: the navigation lists the headings, with a title in the book's language
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #769. Fixes #770.

## Changes

- **Headings in the navigation:** headings (`h1`–`h6` export tags) get an `id` in the EPUB's XHTML (`s{section}-p{paragraph}`). `nav.xhtml` now lists the `h1`–`h3` headings of the stories in reading order, linked to those ids and nested by level (a deeper heading goes in an `ol` inside the previous item; skipped levels count as one).
- **Fallback:** a document without any heading keeps the old navigation, one entry per story labelled with its first paragraph.
- **HTML export:** single-page HTML has no navigation, so it gets no heading ids and its markup is unchanged.
- **Title:** the navigation's title follows `language`: Inhoud, Inhalt, Table des matières, Índice, Indice, 目次, 目录, and Contents for the rest (`contents_title`). `file.exportEpub` takes `tocTitle` to set it, passed through as `EpubOptions::toc_title`.

## Tests

- `navigation_follows_the_headings`:
  - Two chapters with a section in between produce the nested list in that order. A second story that starts with body text ("Text after the figure.", as in the issue) doesn't appear.
  - The headings carry their ids.
  - `language: nl` gives "Inhoud", `toc_title` overrides it, and a document without headings falls back to the first paragraph.
- `tests/export_tag_styles.rs` compares the EPUB markup without the new heading ids.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-epub` and `-p designcraft-engine` pass, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt are clean.

title: EPUB: real modified time, a stable unique identifier, and a cover image file
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #771. Fixes #773.

## Changes

- **`dcterms:modified`** was always `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
  - `file.exportEpub` now passes the export time (`EpubOptions::modified`).
  - On the web, where `SystemTime::now` isn't available, and in the crate when no time is given, it is the document's last save time, else its creation time. Formatting is `iso8601`, a civil-date conversion with no dependency.
- **`dc:identifier`** defaulted to `urn:designcraft:<title slug>`, so two books with the same title shared it.
  - The default is now a `urn:uuid` derived from the title and the document's creation time: the same on every export of a document, different between documents.
  - `file.exportEpub` takes `identifier` (an ISBN URN, for example), which was already in `EpubOptions` but not exposed.
- **Cover:** `file.exportEpub` takes `coverImage`, a PNG or JPEG file used as the cover (`cover-image` plus a cover page), instead of only rendering the first page (`cover: true`, unchanged). A JPEG is packaged as `images/cover.jpg` with `image/jpeg`. Anything else is refused with an error.
- **Params doc** updated for both new parameters.

## Tests

- `iso8601_timestamps`: covers the epoch, 29 February 2000, a 2026 time and a pre-1970 day.
- `package_metadata_and_cover_image`:
  - The identifier is stable between exports and differs for another creation time.
  - Modified comes from the document or from the options.
  - A JPEG cover is packaged as a JPEG.
- `epub_cover_image_file_and_identifier` (engine): a JPEG file as `coverImage`, an ISBN identifier and no fixed date. A text file is refused.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-epub` and `-p designcraft-engine` pass, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt are clean.
- I couldn't run `cargo xtask wasm` locally (no wasm32 std on this machine). The time source is behind `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`.

title: EPUB/HTML: no file name as alt text, readable image names in the package
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #774.

## Changes

- **Alt text:** an image without alt text in Object Export Options used to get its file name as `alt` (e.g. `alt="anim.gif"`), which screen readers read aloud.
  - It is now decorative: `alt=""`.
  - `file.exportEpub` returns a `warnings` array that names those images (`images_without_alt`), so they can be found and given alt text. Video and sound are left out of it.
- **Package names:** images, posters and media were packaged under their asset id (`images/441.gif`). They are now `images/<name>-<id>.<ext>`, with the name from the original file name: lowercase ASCII, other characters as `-`, at most 40 characters. The id keeps two files of the same name apart. A name with nothing usable (`???.png`) keeps the bare id.

## Tests

- `images_get_readable_names_and_no_file_name_alt`:
  - An image without alt (`/tmp/Anim Frame (1).GIF` → `images/anim-frame-1-<id>.gif`, `alt=""`, reported).
  - One with alt text (`photo-<id>.jpg`, alt kept).
  - One whose name has nothing usable.
- `epub_cover_and_fixed_layout` checks the new, empty `warnings` array.

This touches the same lines as #779 (anchored objects): whichever lands second needs a small rebase, which I'll do.

title: EPUB/HTML: generic font fallback from the font's class, and optional font embedding
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #775.

## Generic fallback

Every `font-family` used to fall back to `serif`, so Montserrat came out as `"Montserrat", serif`.

- The engine now passes each stylesheet family's generic family, from the font's classification (`FontDb::family_kind` → `FontClass`):
  - serif and slab serif → `serif`
  - sans → `sans-serif`
  - monospaced → `monospace`
  - script → `cursive`
  - decorative → `fantasy`
- A family that is unknown, or a symbol or unclassified font, falls back to its name: `… Mono`/`Courier`/`… Code` → monospace, `… Sans`/`Gothic`/`Grotesk`/`Helvetica`/`Arial`/`Verdana` → sans-serif, else serif.
- EPUB and HTML both use it (`EpubOptions` and `HtmlOptions::generic_families`).

## Embedding

`file.exportEpub {embedFonts: true}` packages the faces the stylesheet names (`stylesheet_fonts`):

- Files go in `OEBPS/fonts/`, each with an `@font-face` rule (weight and style from the style name) and a manifest item (`font/ttf`, `otf`, `woff` or `woff2` by signature).
- A face is left out when:
  - it isn't available (the font database fell back to another family);
  - its OS/2 `fsType` forbids embedding (`FontFace::restricted_licence`, as the PDF export checks);
  - or it's part of a TrueType collection.
- Each one left out is named in a new `warnings` array in the result.
- Embedding is off by default.
- **Fonts are packaged whole, not subset.** Subsetting needs a subsetter outside krilla, so I'd do it as a follow-up if wanted.

## Tests

- `generic_fallbacks_and_embedded_fonts` (crate):
  - The name guesses, and that only CSS generic families are accepted from the map.
  - Weights and styles from style names.
  - The `@font-face` rule, the manifest item and the packaged file of an embedded OTF.
  - HTML using the generic families without embedding anything.
- `epub_font_fallbacks_and_embedding` (engine):
  - Source Sans 3 gets `sans-serif`.
  - Nothing is embedded unless asked.
  - With `embedFonts`, the Source Sans 3 file is packaged and declared, and a miss…

title: Styles: name the attributes in the params docs, and a wrong one in the command's error
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #777.

## Changes

- **Params descriptions:** `style.paragraph.create`, `style.paragraph.edit`, `style.character.create` and `style.character.edit` described `chars?: {…}` / `para?: {…}` without the attribute names. They now say these take the attributes `type.char` / `type.para` take, and name the common ones (`fontFamily, fontStyle, size, leading, tracking, fill, …` and `align, leftIndent, firstLineIndent, spaceBefore, spaceAfter, …`).
- **Errors:** a wrong attribute gave `invalid parameters for \`style\`: unknown attribute \`font\``. Now:
  - The error names the command and the group: `invalid parameters for \`style.paragraph.create\`: chars: unknown attribute \`font\`; did you mean \`fontFamily\`?`.
  - The suggestion is the nearest attribute (edit distance up to a third of the key's length), or one the key starts or ends (`font` → `fontFamily`). Without one, the error lists all attributes in camelCase.
  - The suggestion is built in `set_json` (the attrs macro), so `type.char`, `type.para` and `find.change` get it too.

title: EPUB: one content file per chapter, split before each h1
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #768.

**Builds on #782** (heading ids and the headings navigation): this branch contains #782's commit, so please merge that first. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## Changes

The whole book was written to one `content.xhtml`. Large books loaded slowly on e-readers, and chapters didn't start on a new page.

- **Split:** the EPUB body is now split before every `h1` into `content.xhtml`, `content2.xhtml`, `content3.xhtml`, ….
  - The first file keeps its old name, so a book without `h1` headings is packaged as before.
  - Each file is a complete XHTML document with the stylesheet.
- **Sections stay well formed** (`split_chapters`):
  - When a split falls inside a story's `<section>`, that section is closed and reopened in the next file.
  - When a story opens with its `h1`, its `<section id=…>` moves into the new file, so no empty section is left behind and its id stays with it.
- **Manifest and spine** list the chapter files in reading order, after the cover if there is one.
- **Navigation:** each entry links to the file its heading ended up in (`content2.xhtml#s1-p0`).
- **HTML export** stays one page. The split marks only appear in the EPUB body.

Not included: splitting on paragraph styles set to start on a new page, or on objects with "page break before". `h1` covers the common case, and those can follow if wanted.

## Tests

- `chapters_are_split_at_h1`: a title page, then a story that opens with a chapter and has a second one in the middle, becomes three files.
  - Each file holds its own content and balanced sections, with no marks left.
  - The spine and manifest have three items, and the navigation points into `content2`/`content3`.
  - HTML is unaffected.
- `split_chapters_keeps_sections_well_formed`: no split, a story opening with `h1`, a split mid-section, and an empty body.
- `navigation_follows_the_headings` (from #782) now expects the second chapter in `content2.xhtml`.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-epub` and `-p designcraft-engine` pas…

title: Saving: an error never leaves an empty file or a document marked saved
author: aiongg
body:
- When the native writer failed, `to_bytes` returned empty bytes. Save then wrote a 0-byte file over the document, marked it saved, dropped its recovery checkpoint and reported success. `file.serialize` returned an empty download the same way.
- `to_bytes` (and `cmd::file_bytes`) return a `Result`. Save, Save As, Save a Copy, `file.serialize`, `file.package`, snippet export and the clipboard snippet propagate the error ("could not write the document: …"). A failed save leaves the existing file untouched, the document unsaved and its recovery checkpoint in place.
- One concrete trigger: a placed file over 4 GiB, which zip rejects unless the entry has zip64 sizes. Asset entries near or over that size are written with zip's large-file option, so such documents save. Smaller entries are written exactly as before.
- Web: `DownloadFn` returns `Result<(), String>`, and the browser download returns its error instead of logging it. Save marks the document saved only after the download has started; otherwise it reports "could not download …" and the document stays unsaved. A failure to schedule the object-URL revoke, after the click, is logged and does not fail the save.

Fixes #741.
Fixes #708.

Tests: `cmd::file::save_tests::a_save_that_cannot_write_the_document_changes_nothing` (injected writer failure: save, save a copy and serialize are errors; the file on disk, the dirty state and the recovery checkpoint are unchanged), `tests::large_assets_are_written_with_zip64_sizes_and_open_again` in designcraft-format, and `menus::tests::web_save_marks_the_document_saved_only_after_the_download_starts` in designcraft-ui-egui (failing download: error, still dirty; succeeding download: clean).

title: Recovery: an explicit recovery folder never overwrites another instance's checkpoints
author: aiongg
body:
- Document uids start at 1 in every process. When two running apps saved recovery data to the same folder given with `file.recovery.save {dir}`, a dirty document replaced the other app's `<uid>.designcraft`/`.json` and a clean one deleted them. A later run reusing a folder with older checkpoints did the same.
- In a folder that is not the run's own folder, a run replaces or removes only the entries it wrote or recovered there (tracked per process, keyed by the canonical folder path). A dirty document whose uid is taken by an entry it did not write fails the save with a clear error before anything is written; first writes are published without replacement, so an entry made after the check is not overwritten either.
- A folder whose run lock another running app holds is refused for saving and recovering, with an error that says so.
- The default per-run folders behave as before, and `file.recovery.open` still recovers entries a crashed run left in any folder; recovering an entry makes it the run's own, so Save and Close of the recovered document remove it.

Fixes #715.

Tests: `recovery::tests::a_clean_document_leaves_another_runs_entry_in_a_chosen_folder`, `recovery::tests::a_dirty_document_does_not_overwrite_another_runs_entry_in_a_chosen_folder` (both fail before the fix), `recovery::tests::a_folder_another_running_app_holds_is_refused`.

title: Story Editor stays with its document; Undo restores the selection from before the command
author: aiongg
body:
- Story ids are counted per document. With the Story Editor open, switching to another document made the editor show, and edit, that document's story with the same id.
- The Story Editor is bound to the document of its story. It hides while another document is active, comes back when its document is active again, and closes when its document closes. Its edits go only to its own document.
- Undo restored the document from before a command but the selection from after it, so undoing a new frame left the vanished frame selected. Undo now restores the selection from before the command; Redo restores the one after it.

Fixes #729.
Fixes #716.

Tests: `story_editor::tests::editor_stays_with_its_document` (two documents with the same story id; typing after switching documents changed the other document's story before the fix) and `tests::undo_restores_the_selection_from_before_the_command` in designcraft-engine (select A, create B, Undo selects A, Redo selects B).

title: Path edits respect locked layers; Properties links open panels when docking is on
author: aiongg
body:
- A path on a locked layer, or inside a locked group, could still be reshaped through `path.setAnchor`, `path.moveAnchors`, `path.appendAnchor`, `path.reverse` and the other `path.*` edit commands. Only `path.setAnchor` checked the object's own lock.
- Every `path.*` command that edits an existing object (`setAnchor`, `moveAnchors`, `appendAnchor`, `reverse`, `close`, `addAnchor`, `deleteAnchor`, `convertAnchor`, `erase`, `smooth`, `split`) now refuses with "the path is locked" when the object, a group around it, or its layer is locked. The document and undo history stay unchanged. `path.reverse` with several ids still skips locked ones and errors only when every target is locked.
- In a customized panel layout, the Properties panel's Stroke, Opacity, Effects, Text Wrap, Character, Paragraph and transform more-options links did nothing: they set the legacy flyout, which is not drawn while docking is on.
- Those links now run `window.panel`, which activates the panel in the docked layout and opens the flyout otherwise. An already open flyout stays open.
- Link labels in panels report themselves as links to accessibility tools.

Fixes #735.
Fixes #736.

Tests: `cmd::object::path_edit_tests::path_edits_leave_a_path_on_a_locked_layer_alone` and `cmd::object::path_edit_tests::path_edits_leave_a_path_in_a_locked_group_alone` (eleven `path.*` edits on a path on a locked layer, or in a locked group, each error; anchors unchanged and the path stays open) and `panel_docking::tests::properties_stroke_link_opens_the_stroke_panel_in_a_custom_workspace` (docking on, clicking the Properties Stroke link docks and activates the Stroke panel).

title: Text recomposes when the baseline grid, a wrap layer's visibility or section numbering changes
author: aiongg
body:
- The composition cache reused a story's layout while its own items and styles were unchanged, so three document-level edits had no effect on existing text until something else touched the story: changing the document baseline grid (start or increment), showing or hiding a layer that holds a text-wrap object, and renumbering a section (start number, style, prefix or marker) without adding or removing one.
- The cache signature now includes the baseline grid start and increment, the visibility of each wrap object's layer, and a hash of every section's numbering settings. The running-header and cross-reference index signature uses the same section hash, so cross-reference page numbers follow a renumbering too.
- Lookups stay cheap: the additions are a few values per lookup plus one flag per wrap object already in the signature.

Fixes #718.

Tests: `tests::cache_recomposes_when_the_baseline_grid_changes`, `tests::cache_recomposes_when_a_wrap_layer_is_hidden` and `tests::cache_recomposes_page_numbers_when_a_section_is_renumbered` (designcraft-compose); each returned the stale cached composition before the fix.

title: Word import: table cells skip deleted text and field codes; Normal style formatting is kept
author: aiongg
body:
- Table cells read their paragraphs with the same run rules as body text. Deleted text (`w:del`), moved-away text (`w:moveFrom`) and field instructions (`w:instrText`) no longer show up in cells; inserted and moved-in text and field results do. Tabs, line breaks and special hyphens in cells come through as they do in body text, and paragraphs inside content controls in a cell are read. Cells stay plain text as before; a page or column break in a cell ends its paragraph.
- Word's Normal comes in as its own paragraph style named "Normal" instead of being dropped, so text formatted only by Normal keeps its font, size and spacing when placed with the default options.
  - Its definition is Word's document defaults (`w:docDefaults`) with Normal's own properties on top. Any other paragraph style that isn't based on another style also gets the document defaults beneath it.
  - Paragraphs without a paragraph style get Word's default paragraph style (the one marked `w:default`, otherwise `Normal`).
  - Styles based on Normal are based on "Normal".
- "Normal" conflicts only when the document already has a style with that name; then Use Existing, Redefine and Auto-Rename work as for any other style.
- To merge Word's Normal into `[Basic Paragraph]`, map it with the existing style map (`styleMap: {"Normal": "[Basic Paragraph]"}`). No style is added and the text uses the document's `[Basic Paragraph]` definition, whatever the conflict option, because mapped styles are not imported.
- "Default Paragraph Font" still maps to `[None]`: in Word it means "no character style" and has no formatting of its own.
- Styles used only in footnotes are imported too.

Fixes #721.
Fixes #722.

Tests: `docx::tests::table_cells_read_text_like_body_paragraphs` (deleted text, a move source and a PAGE field in a cell and in a body paragraph give "kept 7" in both), `docx::tests::normal_is_its_own_style_over_the_document_defaults` (docDefaults 11 pt and 8 pt space after, Normal 13 pt Georgia, a style ba…

title: EPUB export includes tables, footnotes and endnotes
author: aiongg
body:
- Reflowable EPUB and HTML export wrote only paragraph text. Tables, footnote text and endnote text were dropped without any warning, along with the reference numbers in the text.
- A table becomes an HTML `<table>`. Header rows go in `thead` and footer rows in `tfoot`. Merged cells get `rowspan`/`colspan`, kept within their row group. Each cell's text uses the same paragraph and character styling as body text.
- A footnote reference becomes a superscript note link (`epub:type="noteref"`, `role="doc-noteref"`). The note follows its paragraph as `<aside epub:type="footnote" role="doc-footnote">` and starts with a link back to the reference. Numbers and labels come from Document Footnote Options.
- An endnote reference links to an endnotes section at the end of the book (`epub:type="endnotes"`, `role="doc-endnotes"`), in number order, with the Endnote Options heading and labels. The heading is also an entry in the EPUB navigation. The endnote frame's generated story is not exported a second time.
- The single-page HTML export gets the same content with ARIA roles but no `epub:type` attributes.
- Nesting (tables in cells, notes in notes) stops at a fixed depth. A table whose cell grid does not match its row and column counts is skipped.

Fixes #724.

Tests: `tests::tables_footnotes_and_endnotes_are_exported` (2×2 table cell texts inside `<table>`; footnote reference linked to its aside; endnote linked to the endnotes section and the nav; plain HTML without `epub:type`) and `tests::table_rows_groups_and_merged_cells` (thead/tbody/tfoot, colspan, rowspan clipped at the footer) in `crates/epub/src/lib.rs`.

title: IDML export keeps overridden parent items
author: aiongg
body:
- A page with overridden parent items exported to IDML lost the override: every page was written with an empty `OverrideList`, and the local copy lost its link to the parent item. After reopening the file, the parent item showed again next to its edited local copy.
- Export writes each page's `OverrideList` as the ids of its overridden parent items, and writes `OverriddenPageItem` on the local copy.
- Import reads `OverriddenPageItem` back, so the copy stays linked to its parent item (Remove All Local Overrides finds it again).

Fixes #725.

Tests: `tests::round_trips_overridden_parent_items` (parent frame overridden on page 1, export and reimport: the page lists the parent item, the copy points at it, and the page shows one frame).

title: PDF export leaves out form fields, buttons and media that aren't shown
author: aiongg
body:
- A form field, button, video or sound inside a hidden group, on a hidden or non-printing layer, or marked non-printing was left off the page artwork but still exported as an interactive field, link or embedded media file.
- Fields, buttons and media are now collected with the same rule as the page content: the item's layer is visible and printable, and the item and every group around it are neither hidden nor non-printing. A hidden or non-printing group leaves out everything inside it.
- The rule lives in one place in `export.rs` (`layer_exported`, `item_exported`, `exported_items`) and the page drawing uses the same predicates.

Fixes #726.

Tests: `tests::only_printed_fields_and_buttons_export` (a field and a button in a hidden group, on a hidden layer, on a non-printing layer and marked non-printing, plus one shown pair: the PDF has one widget and only the shown button's link).

title: macOS: menu-bar commands run at once
author: aiongg
body:
- A command chosen with the mouse in the system menu bar ran only on the next egui frame, and nothing asked for one: the pointer is over the menu bar, so the window gets no input until the mouse comes back or a key is pressed. File › Open, Place and Save As therefore seemed to take 10–20 seconds (more than 90 s when the user waited without moving), while ⌘O was instant.
- `NativeMenu::install` registers `MenuEvent::set_event_handler`, which forwards each event to the menu's own channel and calls `request_repaint`, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do. `poll` drains that channel.

Fixes #784. A shared menu bridge for all Craft apps is proposed in storytold/craft-libs#65.

Tests: macOS-only code with no headless menu bar to drive; `cargo clippy --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p designcraft -- -D warnings` passes. Checked by timing on a Mac before the fix (8, 12, 15 and >90 s, then 0.4 s after the next input).

title: File › Open Recent, and recent files with previews on the start screen
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Fixes #706.

**File › Open Recent.** Opening or saving a document moves it to the front of the list, with no duplicates. Save a Copy and exports don't count. The submenu lists the files by name, with the full path as tooltip, then Clear Recent Files. It is disabled when the list is empty. A file that is gone shows an alert when chosen and stays listed, so a disk that isn't connected comes back. Preferences › File Handling sets how many are kept (default 20, 0–100). The macOS menu bar rebuilds the submenu when the list changes.

**Start screen.** Below the community card, "Recent files" shows the last eight as cards. Each card has a picture of the first page and the name without `.designcraft`, on up to two lines. The full path is the tooltip. A file that is gone has a dimmed name and a grey page.

**Previews in the file.** Save and Save a Copy put a picture of the first page in the `.designcraft` zip as `preview.png` (320 px on the longer side, stored as is: 57 KB for the sample magazine, 154 KB for a page that is one photo). The start screen reads only the zip's directory and that entry, so it doesn't open the document. Files saved before this have no picture and show a blank page until they are saved again. Opening is unchanged: `load` ignores the entry. A page that can't be drawn leaves the picture out.

**Commands:** `file.openRecent {index}`, `file.recentFiles` → `[{path, name, exists}]`, `file.clearRecent`, and `app.openRecent` in the UI. `designcraft_format::save_with_preview` / `read_preview` and `designcraft_engine::cmd::recent_preview` back the start screen. Prefs: `recent_files`, `recent_files_max` (in prefs.json). On the web the list stays empty and there are no previews.

**Tests:** order and no duplicates, the cap, surviving a restart, Clear, a missing file is an error that keeps it listed, hostile indices are errors (never panics). For previews: the preview round-trips without the document, and files without one, legacy JSON, garbage and missing files…

title: Refuse command params the description doesn't name (#776)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #776.

## What changed

Unknown parameter keys are no longer ignored silently. Callers from outside the app get a parameter error naming the key, plus the nearest accepted key or the full list:

- `text.select {story, start: 0, end: 5}` → `invalid parameters for `text.select`: unknown parameter `end`; the command takes: story, anchor, focus` (keys are checked in sorted order)
- `style.list {bogus: 1}` → `… unknown parameter `bogus`; the command takes no parameters`
- `file.new {widht: 300}` → `… did you mean `width`?`

**Engine.** I added `crates/engine/src/cmd/params.rs`, ported from VectorCraft (#1442 there, same organisation), without the effects part. `doc_keys` reads the accepted keys from each command's `params` description. It handles `{a} or {b}` alternatives, `a? | b?` alternative keys, and `…same as other.cmd` references. `check_keys` / `check_params` are re-exported from the crate. A command that documents `ids` also accepts `id`, because `cmd::targets` reads both. `Session::execute` itself does **not** check, so journals written by older versions still replay (an integration test covers this). Inside the engine's own unit tests it does check, under `#[cfg(test)]`, as VectorCraft does, so every key a test passes is an audit of the descriptions.

**Entry points that check:**
- MCP `tools/call`: an argument the tool's input schema doesn't list → JSON-RPC **-32602**. `execute` params, and **every `batch` step** (`commands` or `script`), are checked before anything runs → **-32602**. A refused batch leaves the document untouched.
- MCP headless backend (`Headless::exec`), which also covers `designcraft-cli script` headless.
- Control channel `engine.execute` / `ui.menu.invoke` / `command`, which also covers MCP and `designcraft-cli script` in `--connect` mode.
- `designcraft-cli run --cmd`.

The app's own panels and tools (`app.run`) and the `script.run` command are not checked, because they go through `Session::execute`.

**Missing required keys are no…

title: fix: show Hangul in the UI with the system's Korean font
author: xoincare
body:
## Problem

Opening a Korean InDesign file shows every Hangul character in the interface as an empty box (tofu): document names, paragraph/character style names, layer names, text in panels and dialogs. The bundled UI faces (Source Sans 3, JetBrains Mono) and craft-fonts (Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Arabic) have no Hangul, and egui doesn't discover system fonts.

## Fix

`theme::install_fonts` adds the system's Korean face to every font family as a fallback:

- Windows: Malgun Gothic (`malgun.ttf`, `malgunbd.ttf` for the semibold families)
- macOS: Apple SD Gothic Neo
- Linux: Nanum Gothic, or the KR face of Noto Sans CJK (collection index 1)

Details:
- The face is read once per run (`OnceLock`), because `install_fonts` is called again from several panels.
- For a `ko` interface it goes right after the app's own faces. For every other language it goes at the end, so Han characters keep their Japanese or Chinese forms and existing stacks don't change order.
- When no face is found, or on the web (`wasm32`), nothing changes.
- No font files are added to the repository, as `standards/fonts.md` requires.
- `font_definitions` is unchanged, so the existing font tests still check the bundled and craft-fonts stacks exactly.

## Testing

- New test `hangul_ui_glyphs_come_from_the_system_korean_face`: with `en` and `ko`, every family has glyphs for Hangul text. It skips when the machine has no Korean font.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib -- theme::`: 4 passed.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean on Windows.
- `cargo check -p designcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: builds.
- Manual check on Windows 11 through the control channel: a layer named "한글 레이어 테스트" and a paragraph style named "본문 단락 스타일" render correctly in the Layers panel and in Paragraph Style Options.

I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci`. With Rust 1.99, the wasm clippy pass stops at two `needless_return` errors in `cr…

title: Preferences: OK without vertical units keeps them
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #806.

Preferences OK read the vertical units by indexing the dialog's fields. A dialog opened through `ui.dialog.open` with `horizontalUnits` but no `verticalUnits` made that panic on the UI thread, outside the crash guard, and the app exited.

- The units are now read with `get`, and a ruler the dialog doesn't name keeps its units.
- Edit › Preferences fills both fields, so nothing changes for the dialog as a person uses it.

The steps from the issue now get an ordinary error reply, because `bg.relativeTo` is missing from those fields too. That is no crash and this PR leaves it alone.

Validation: `preferences_ok_sets_only_the_ruler_units_it_is_given` panics on main at `dialogs.rs:2040`; its second case pins that vertical units the dialog does name are still applied. On a release build the steps from the issue no longer end the app. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Open .indd and .indt files through indd-utils
author: aiongg
body:
- `.indd` and `.indt` documents open through File › Open, drop, the web inbox, `file.open`, `file.openBytes`, `file.openIdml` and the CLI.
- The engine converts them to IDML in memory with [storytold/indd-utils](https://github.com/storytold/indd-utils) and imports the result through the existing IDML path. The crate is pinned by rev like the craft-libs crates; it is MIT OR Apache-2.0 and has no dependencies.
- The converter's warnings come first in the open result's `warnings`, before the IDML importer's and the font warnings.
- A file the converter can't read is an open error, shown in the Can't Open the File alert; no document is added.
- Routing: a path or name ending in `.indd`/`.indt`, or bytes starting with the INDD signature (the web inbox passes the name without its extension). `opens_as_document` and the desktop and web Open dialogs list indd/indt.
- Works on the web: indd-utils builds for wasm, and `cargo xtask wasm` passes.
- Docs: README, gaps.md item 2 (now the real-file corpus), file-format-parity.md, roadmap.md, target-app-parity.md and a ROADMAP progress-log line. Readiness numbers are unchanged until a corpus measures the conversion.

Closes #21. Related: #114, #98.

Tests: synthetic bytes only. Signature-bearing junk, a zero-filled `.indd` and a short `.indt` all fail as open errors with no document added; a dropped unreadable `.indd` raises the open alert. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass; the engine's indd/idml/open tests (41) and the UI's open/drop tests (25) pass.

title: Images: reject EPS bounding boxes with nonfinite corners or size (#740)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #740.

`bounding_box` in `crates/images/src/eps.rs` checked only that the corners were ordered. A `%%BoundingBox:` line with `inf` corners, or with extreme finite corners such as `-1e308 0 1e308 50` whose width overflows to infinity, was accepted, and `eps_proxy` then returned that nonfinite physical size for placement.

Now a box is accepted only when all four corners and the derived width and height are finite (and, as before, positive). A bad `%%HiResBoundingBox:` falls back to the plain `%%BoundingBox:`, the same way a missing or malformed one already did. `eps_proxy` is the only consumer, so the fix sits in the one parser it calls.

Test `eps_bounding_box_rejects_nonfinite_sizes` covers the points the issue asks for: a normal box, infinite corners, finite corners whose difference overflows, reversed corners, and the HiRes-to-plain fallback.

title: Compare the format version without narrowing it to u32 (#739)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #739.

`load_zip` read `version` from `meta.json` as a `u64` and cast it to `u32` before the too-new check. A value such as `2^32 + 1` wrapped to `1`, passed the check and the file was read as a supported document.

The check now compares the `u64` with `u64::from(VERSION)`, and `FormatError::TooNew` carries the `u64`, so the error shows the version that is really in the file. `TooNew` is only built and matched inside `crates/format`. Nothing else changes: supported versions load as before, and the error message is the same.

Test: `newer_version_is_not_narrowed_to_u32` in `crates/format/src/lib.rs` checks `VERSION + 1`, `2^32 + VERSION` (which wraps to `VERSION` when narrowed) and `u64::MAX`, and expects `TooNew` with the exact value each time. On main the `2^32 + VERSION` case is accepted by the version check.

The issue also says that missing or malformed metadata needs a compatibility policy. I left that out: today such files are still read from `document.json`, and changing that is a maintainer decision. This PR only fixes the narrowing.

title: Fix overset preflight page for frames inside translated groups (#738)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #738.

The overset check in `preflight::check` called `page_of` with `Affine::IDENTITY` as the parent transform, so a text frame inside a group was placed on a page by its own bounds only and the group's transform was ignored. A group moved across a facing-page spread got its overset error reported on the page the frame started on.

It now passes `d.parent_xf(&loc)`, which is what the per-item checks further down in the same function already do (their walk carries the parent transform into `page_of`), and what other commands use to bring nested items into spread space.

Test: `overset_page_tests::overset_frame_in_a_moved_group_names_its_displayed_page` makes a 3-page facing document, groups an overset text frame with a second frame on the left page of spread 1, and moves the group 612 pt onto the right page. Preflight must report page index 2. Before the fix it still reported page 1.

title: MCP: render_page and screenshot are not read-only because they can write to path (#733)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #733.

`render_page` and `screenshot` take an optional `path` and write the PNG there, but their tool definitions said `readOnlyHint: true`. A client that uses the hint to skip approval would let them write files without asking.

Both now pass `read_only = false`, the same as `export_png`, which also writes to `path`. Nothing else changes: the tools still return the image, and `path` still works.

Test: `tools_that_write_files_are_not_read_only` in `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs` checks that `render_page`, `screenshot` and `export_png` take `path` and have `readOnlyHint: false`. It fails on main for `render_page` and `screenshot`.

The issue also suggests splitting image-return and file-writing into separate tools. I left that out because it changes the tool API and is a maintainer decision; this PR only corrects the hint.

title: fix(render): cap the failed-image cache at 64 entries (#728)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #728.

The process-wide image cache in `crates/render/src/images.rs` remembers assets that failed to decode so they are not retried every frame. That `bad` map held a strong `Arc<Vec<u8>>` per failure and was only emptied by `images::clear()`. The pixmap budget eviction never touched it, so each distinct broken asset kept its encoded bytes alive for the rest of the process.

**Change**
- `bad` entries now carry an insertion stamp from the cache's existing `clock`.
- A new `Cache::mark_bad` inserts the failure. Above `MAX_BAD` (64) entries it drops the oldest one, which releases its `Arc` and so its encoded bytes. The only insert site, the `None` branch of `decoded`, now goes through it.
- An evicted asset is decoded again if it is drawn later and is marked bad again if it still fails. Since the cap is 64, this happens at most once per asset each time 64 newer failures have come in, not every frame.
- Module docs mention the cap.

The bound is on the number of entries, not on bytes. Failed assets are normally still held by the open document, so the cache only adds retention after the document drops them, and 64 is the most it can keep.

**Test**
`images::tests::failed_assets_are_capped_and_oldest_is_dropped` marks 74 distinct buffers as failed. It then checks that the map holds exactly 64, that the first buffer is gone with its `Arc::strong_count` back to 1 (the cache let go of the bytes), and that the newest buffer is still in the map. Without the cap the map holds all 74 and the test fails.

title: fix(pdf): leave form fields and media out of PDF/A-2b exports (#743)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #743.

PDF/A-2b export runs krilla's archival validator inside `pdf.finish()`, but form fields and (with `media: true`) video/sound were added afterwards by `forms::add_fields` as an incremental update. That update is never validated, and what it writes is not allowed in PDF/A-2: the AcroForm sets `NeedAppearances true` (text fields have no appearance streams), and media go in as Screen annotations with rendition actions. The file then said it was PDF/A-2b but did not conform.

PDF/X-4 already skips this update and warns "form fields and media were left out". PDF/A-2b now does the same, with its own warning ("PDF/A-2b: form fields and media were left out"). Plain and interactive PDF exports are unchanged. `docs/target-app-parity.md` now says form fields are not exported in PDF/X or PDF/A.

On the issue's other points: checking the final bytes with an external conformance checker is out of scope here (none is in the test setup). Writing PDF/A-compliant fields (with appearance streams) would be a separate feature.

Test: `pdfa_leaves_out_form_fields_added_after_validation` adds a text field. A plain export still gets `/AcroForm` (the control). The PDF/A-2b export has the `pdfaid` metadata, has no `/AcroForm` or `NeedAppearances`, and reports the warning. Without the fix the PDF/A export contains the AcroForm update, so the test fails.

title: fix: eyedropper ignores inactive states of a multi-state object (#737)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #737.

`image_under` (the Eyedropper's check for whether a placed raster shows under the pointer) walked every child of a group, so in a multi-state object an inactive state could decide between pixel sampling (`color.sample`) and attribute matching (`object.matchAttributes`).

It now walks `Item::shown_children()`, the same visibility rule that multi-state objects use elsewhere: only the active state when the item has states, all children otherwise. Z-order (topmost first) and the other inclusion rules (hidden items, unfilled frames, raster vs. vector graphics) are unchanged.

Test: `eyedropper_ignores_inactive_states_of_a_multi_state_object` builds a two-state object with a filled vector frame and a raster image in the same place, and checks both orders the issue asks for: active raster samples pixels, active vector (raster inactive above it) does not. Without the fix the second case samples the hidden raster.

title: fix(cli): reject --pdf-options that is not a JSON object instead of panicking (#731)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #731.

**Cause.** `run --pdf-options JSON` parsed the flag into an arbitrary `serde_json::Value`, and the following `--export OUT.pdf` did `p["path"] = json!(out)` on a copy of it. `serde_json`'s `IndexMut` panics on arrays, booleans, numbers and strings, so for example `--pdf-options '[]' --export out.pdf` crashed the CLI instead of reporting an error.

**Fix.** The shape is checked when `--pdf-options` is parsed:
- a JSON object is used as before;
- `null` is treated as `{}` (no options), which is what it already did, because indexing promotes `null` to an object;
- any other JSON value returns `--pdf-options: expected a JSON object`, printed as `designcraft-cli: ...` with exit status 1, like the other `run` argument errors (`--cmd ID: ...`, `bad --page`).

The error comes before any export runs. Nothing else changes: `file.exportPdf` called through `--cmd`, `script` or MCP gets its params through the engine, which does not take this path.

**Test.** `tests/cli.rs::pdf_options_that_are_not_an_object_are_an_error_not_a_panic` runs `run --sample --pdf-options V --export out.pdf` for `[]`, `true`, `1` and `"x"`, and checks exit status 1, a `--pdf-options` message and no panic. Without the fix the process panics (exit 101). It also checks that `null` still exports successfully.

title: fix: drop the background render when a display option changes (#730)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #730.

**Cause.** The display-option commands (View › Overprint Preview, Display Performance, and the others) clear `canvas.shown`, but leave `canvas.pending` alone. If the background render that was started with the old options finishes on the next frame, `render_texture` accepts it (the token matches and the document key does not include display options), puts it back in `shown`, and the coverage check then treats the stale pixels as current until something else invalidates the canvas.

**Fix.** `render_texture` now keeps a `DisplayKey` of every option that feeds `RenderOptions` (display quality, separation plate, rich black, overprint preview, proof colours, tag markers, and the highlight / note / added-text prefs). When the key differs from the one the texture and the request in flight were made with, it drops `shown`, `pending` and `pending_doc` before collecting finished renders, so the old result is ignored and the view is redrawn with the current options. Because the check runs in `render_texture` itself, it covers every way an option changes (menu commands, Preferences dialog, keyboard shortcuts), not only the two menu entries the issue cites.

**Test.** `display_option_change_drops_the_render_in_flight` (canvas.rs): with a texture and a request in flight, an unchanged key keeps both; after switching display quality, both are dropped.

title: Keep a missing graphic missing when it is pasted into another document (#720)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #720.

When items are copied into another document (`duplicate_from` → `renumber` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs`), each asset reference goes through `Document::adopt_asset`. That returns `None` when the source document does not have the asset (a missing graphic), and the old code then kept the numeric id as it was. If the destination already used that id for a different image, the pasted frame showed that unrelated image.

The new helper `adopt_or_dangle` keeps the old behaviour when the id is free in the destination, and only when the destination already uses the id it gives the reference a fresh unused id. The pasted reference stays missing, as it was in the source. It is used for all three places that `renumber` remaps: graphic content, media posters, and assets referenced from stories (inline/anchored graphics, graphic table cells). The issue suggested this approach ("remap to fresh missing-asset placeholders"). Rejecting the paste would lose the whole item for a missing link, which the existing missing-link handling never does.

Data merge has its own `renumber` in `datamerge/fill.rs`. It copies template items into a document cloned from the same template, so both sides share the id space and the collision cannot happen there. That code is left unchanged.

Test: `pasted_missing_graphic_does_not_show_an_unrelated_target_asset` in `links.rs` (next to `pasted_graphics_reuse_the_identical_asset_of_the_target`) pastes a graphic whose asset is missing in the source into a document that has another image under that id. It checks that the pasted graphic does not point to that image and stays missing. Without the fix it gets the destination's image.

title: fix(geom): decompose of a flattened transform reports 0 shear instead of NaN
author: saadkhantareen
body:
## Summary

`decompose()` in `crates/geom/src/decompose.rs` computed shear as `((a*c + b*d) / det).atan()`. For a flattened transform (for example an object scaled to zero height), the determinant and the numerator are both 0, so the shear came out as NaN. That NaN propagates: `transform.set` starts from `decompose(current)`, changes only the fields it was given, and feeds the rest back into `compose()`, so setting just the rotation of a flattened object wrote a NaN affine transform onto it. A NaN shear (only reachable in the singular 0/0 case) now reports 0, since shear is unrecoverable once a transform is flattened; every other case is unchanged.

## Changes

- `crates/geom/src/decompose.rs` (+32/−1): report 0 shear when the computed shear is NaN; a non-zero numerator over a zero determinant still limits to ±90°.
- Same file: new regression test `flattened_transform_has_no_nan_shear` covering flattened compose/decompose round-trips and direct singular matrices.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p designcraft-geom` — 57 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p designcraft-geom decompose` — 2 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo fmt --check -p designcraft-geom` — clean
- The full workspace test suite was not run; the change is confined to the `designcraft-geom` crate, whose tests pass as above.

title: Gradient strokes: on screen, in PDF, in IDML and the Gradient panel
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, a gradient swatch works on a stroke as on a fill. The gradient runs across the object's box, the Gradient panel edits whichever of fill and stroke is in front of the toolbox's proxy, and the Gradient Swatch tool drags it.

LYH Studio's gradient tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38QZEZ5ZpP0), episode 6) uses this twice:
- at 1:19, the first gradient lands on a circle's stroke ("right now it is on the stroke");
- at 9:13, the loop on the right page gets "the same gradient Swatch as the stroke" at 20 pt.

On main, a stroke is painted with a single resolved colour, so a gradient swatch shows as its first stop. There's no way to set a stroke's gradient angle or vector, and the Gradient panel only looks at fills.

## How

- **doc:** `Stroke::gradient_angle` and `Stroke::gradient_vector`, as on `Fill`, plus `Stroke::as_fill()`, which gives the stroke's paint as a fill so it's painted the same way.
- **render:** `draw_stroke` paints with `set_fill_paint` over the path's box. A dash gap's colour is drawn under it, and the gradient is restored afterwards. The paint transform is reset after the stroke.
- **PDF:** the stroke's paint is a gradient shading through `fill_paint` when its swatch is a gradient, and is used for arrowheads and stripes too.
- **engine:**
  - `object.gradient {target: stroke}` edits the stroke's gradient: kind, stops, reverse, angle, and the Gradient Swatch tool's `from`/`to`;
  - `bake` moves the stroke's vector with the shape (scaling, for example).
- **IDML:** `GradientStrokeStart`, `GradientStrokeLength` and `GradientStrokeAngle` round-trip, as the fill's do.
- **Gradient panel:** acts on the stroke when the Stroke box is in front (#600's `UiState::stroke_front`), as InDesign's follows the Fill/Stroke proxy. "The stroke isn't a gradient." is translated in all nine languages.

Docs (target-app parity) and ROADMAP are updated.

author: Nmarello
body:

title: Gradient swatches on text, laid across the text frame as in InDesign
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

Text can take a gradient swatch as its fill or stroke. As in InDesign, the gradient is laid across the **text frame's box**, not each glyph or line. Type on a path uses the path's box.

LYH Studio's InDesign tutorial (episode 6, [8:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38QZEZ5ZpP0&t=508s)) selects the "1969" headline and clicks "New Gradient Swatch" (magenta → cyan) in the Swatches panel. On main, a gradient character fill falls back to the gradient's first stop, so the headline is flat magenta.

![before / after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/gradient-text/gradient-text.png)

*Left: main. Middle: this PR on screen. Right: this PR's PDF, placed back. The text stops short of the frame's right edge (310 pt), so it ends just before full cyan, as in InDesign. The PDF looks lighter because its shading blends in CMYK while the screen blends display RGB, as for every gradient today.*

## How

- **Screen** (`crates/render/src/text.rs`): a style's fill and stroke resolve to a `TextPaint`, either solid or gradient. A gradient is painted through the existing `set_fill_paint` over the frame's inner bounds, in text space (`text_local⁻¹ · inner_bounds`).
- **PDF** (`crates/pdf/src/text.rs`, `export.rs`):
  - While a frame's text is drawn, the exporter keeps the frame's box in text space.
  - Each run's paint is a shading laid out in that space and mapped into the run's own space (`fill_paint_in(…, origin⁻¹)`), so skew and horizontal scale don't bend it.
  - Outlined runs (faces krilla can't embed) and type on a path get the same paint.

## Tests

- `gradient_text_tests::a_gradient_on_text_spans_its_frame_on_screen_and_in_pdf`: red → blue text across a 300 pt frame. Ink at the left is red and ink at the right is blue, both on screen and in the exported PDF placed back.
- I checked the PDF in MuPDF too: the shading runs from x 20 to x 310 in page space, which is the frame.

title: Gradient panel in InDesign's layout; drop swatches from the Swatches panel onto its stops

title: Images: CMYK TIFFs with alpha decode for display
author: govindaroyaiub
body:
`image` reads four-ink TIFFs but rejects five-sample CMYK with alpha (`Unsupported … Color(Unknown(0))`). That is how InDesign stores its preview of a transparent Photoshop file, so those graphics drew nothing.

- `decode_rgba` falls back to the existing `decode_cmyk_tiff` when `image` can't read the file. It converts the inks to RGB the way `image` converts the four-ink TIFFs it does read, so the two look the same, and keeps the alpha.
- `pixel_size` reads such files' size from the TIFF header.
- Screen, PNG and PDF all decode through `decode_rgba`, so all three get them.

Test: `cmyk_tiff_with_alpha_decodes_to_rgba` (an opaque black pixel and a fully transparent one; size, colour and alpha).

title: macOS: no AccessKit, so launch no longer crashes on Touch Bar Macs
author: govindaroyaiub
body:
On a MacBook Pro with a Touch Bar, DesignCraft aborted at launch about one time in four:

```
NSRangeException: Cannot remove an observer <_NSTouchBarFinderObservation> for the key path "nextResponder" from <WinitView>
```

AccessKit's macOS adapter changes the window view's class at runtime (`object_setClass`), which breaks AppKit's key-value observation of that view. The Touch Bar's responder observer then can't unregister and AppKit throws.

- The `accesskit` eframe feature is now off on macOS only. Windows and Linux keep it, through a `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` dependency entry.
- Measured with a launch loop on the affected Mac: 0 of 24 launches crashed without AccessKit, against about one in four with it.

The trade-off is that macOS loses screen-reader access through AccessKit until its adapter stops subclassing the view, so I'm raising it as a PR rather than deciding it myself. I couldn't find a synthetic regression test for an AppKit abort that only happens with Touch Bar hardware; the comment above the dependency records the cause and the measurement.

Validation: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, assets, layers and wasm pass. One exception: `designcraft-mcp`'s `remote_executes_once_when_app_restarts_between_calls` fails on this Mac (`WouldBlock`), on untouched `main` too.

title: IDML: anchored settings from object styles, whole paragraph rules, style names with trailing spaces, Western leading
author: govindaroyaiub
body:
Four import fixes, found opening real InDesign retail flyers (price tags, badges, rules behind labels). Each is small; they're grouped because they're all in `import.rs`, but I can split them if you prefer.

- **Anchored objects:** settings an anchored item doesn't state itself (position, alignment, reference points, offsets) now come from its object style chain, then `[None]`. Before, items whose settings live on their object style came in inline.
- **Paragraph rules:** a style or range that overrides only part of a rule, such as just `RuleAboveColor`, keeps the other settings from its paragraph style chain (`BasedOn`, or the range's applied style). The rule used to lose its weight and offset. The chain walk is capped at 16 levels.
- **Style names ending in a space:** nested, line and GREP style references keep a character style name like `"Decimals "` when that name exists. InDesign allows it, and trimming named no style. Other references are still trimmed.
- **Western leading:** InDesign writes `LeadingModel` and `CharacterAlignment` as defaults in Western documents too, where its composers ignore them. They now apply only when the document uses a Japanese composer or has CJK text. Otherwise Western text got Japanese leading. The scan is iterative, so deep markup can't overflow the stack.

Tests:
- `anchored_objects_take_unstated_settings_from_their_object_style`
- `style_names_ending_in_a_space_and_partial_rule_overrides_import`
- `western_documents_ignore_the_japanese_leading_model_indesign_stores_by_default`

title: Images: EPS shows through its proxy at display time; simple PostScript (QR codes) is drawn
author: govindaroyaiub
body:
InDesign embeds its generated QR codes (Object › Generate QR Code) as EPS. Opened in DesignCraft they drew nothing, because only File › Place turned an EPS into its proxy.

- `decode_rgba` draws any EPS through `eps_proxy`, and `natural_size` measures it by its bounding box in points. Screen, PNG and PDF export all decode through these, so all three show it. The document keeps the EPS bytes, so saving and IDML export are unchanged.
- `eps_proxy` now also draws PostScript that only fills rectangles in solid colours:
  - `setcmykcolor`, `setrgbcolor`, `setgray`, `rectfill`, and one-operator procedures such as InDesign's `/rf { rectfill } bind def`
  - drawn at 8 px per point, so the modules stay crisp when zoomed
  - anything else (paths, text, images, transforms) keeps the TIFF preview or the placeholder, as before
- Input is treated as hostile: limits on tokens (2M), rectangles (200k), painted area (64× the image) and procedure-definition length, and no panicking paths.

Checked on a real InDesign flyer: the QR code renders, and Apple's Vision QR detector reads the rendered page's code back to the right URL.

Tests:
- `simple_rectangle_eps_is_drawn_like_a_qr_code`: colour and position of modules
- `eps_draws_through_its_proxy_at_its_bounding_box_size`: size in points, drawn pixels and transparency

title: Several updates to TextFrame, Toolbar Stroke/Fill, Panels and Typography panel
author: andrestelex
body: ### Toolbar Fill/Stroke - X swaps fill/stroke state - Shift-X swaps the fill/stroke of selection - Selecting Text mode applies fill or stroke to the text frame content - Swatches panel shows where swatches will be applied ### Text Frame Behaviour - Double-clicking a text frame with the Selection tool edits its text: the canvas counts presses itself (egui reports a double click only at the release), and 2/3/4/5 clicks select the word or run of spaces, line, paragraph and story (`text.selectLine`, `text.selectParagraph`, `text.selectStory`; pointer events take `clicks`). - A space typed at a line's end moves the caret past it. - Bold and Italic toggle through the family's linked styles (Italic → Bold Italic, Bold Condensed → Condensed), with B/I buttons in Properties. - Edit menu Copy, Cut and Paste of text use the system clipboard (paste falls back to DesignCraft's clipboard); ⌘C/⌘V on objects work on Linux/Windows. - ⌘-click with the Type tool selects like the Selection tool, leaving the text. - Formatting affects text (J) colours the text of the selection or selected frames; X brings Fill or Stroke to the front, Shift+X swaps them. - A corner handle fits the width and height, a top or bottom handle only the height, a side handle only the width. title: Gradients between process colours blend as inks (C 50 M 50 halfway), as InDesign shows them
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

Gradients between process colours now blend as inks, as InDesign shows them.

Every gradient in LYH Studio's InDesign tutorial (episode 6: the background, the circles, "1969", the loop) runs from `C=0 M=100 Y=0 K=0` to `C=100 M=0 Y=0 K=0`. InDesign blends those stops as inks, so halfway is C 50 M 50, a light lilac; the video's ramp reads about (133, 129, 189) there. On main, DesignCraft converted both ends to RGB and blended in RGB. Halfway came out a darker violet, (117, 88, 189) instead of (135, 119, 181), so the whole page looked different from the video.

The same RGB blending also affected PDF export. A midpoint between CMYK (or grey) stops became an RGB colour, so the PDF shading turned RGB with a "mixed color spaces converted to RGB" warning.

![before / after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/gradient-inks/gradient-inks.png)

## How

- **color:** `Color::lerp` blends CMYK with CMYK or grey, and grey with grey, in ink space. Any pair involving RGB still blends in RGB, so `harmony` and other callers are unchanged. `Gradient::sample` and the midpoint stops follow from this.
- **`Gradient::display_stops`:** the expanded stops, plus 16 samples through each span that isn't RGB at both ends. It's for renderers that interpolate between stops in RGB, and the screen renderer (`set_fill_paint`) now uses it. The Gradient panel's ramp and thumbnail already use `sample`, so they follow too.
- **pdf:** midpoints stay in the stops' space, so a CMYK gradient with a midpoint stays a DeviceCMYK shading. `gradient_color_spaces` now expects no conversion for CMYK or grey midpoints; mixed RGB/CMYK stops still convert, with the warning.

## Tests

- `gradient::tests::process_stops_blend_as_inks`: magenta → cyan is C 50 M 50 halfway; display stops sample the span; a CMYK midpoint stays CMYK; RGB stops aren't sampled; grey meets CMYK as inks; RGB with CMYK blends in RGB.

title: Preferences: Story Editor size stays finite and in range
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #821.

Preferences OK stored whatever number the dialog held as the Story Editor font size. A size that is not finite (`"nan"`, `"inf"`, or a number too large for an `f32` such as `1e39`) was written to `ui.json` as `null`. The next launch could not read the file, started with the default UI settings without a message and saved them over it on exit, so saved workspaces and custom shortcuts were lost.

- The size is now kept between 8 and 36 pt, the range of the dialog's slider.
- A value that is not a finite number leaves the size as it was. So does a dialog opened through `ui.dialog.open` without the field, which used to reset the size to 14 pt.
- Edit › Preferences fills the field and its slider is limited to that range, so nothing changes for the dialog as a person uses it.

The issue also notes that a `ui.json` that can't be read is dropped without a message and overwritten at exit. This PR leaves that alone.

Validation: `preferences_ok_saves_a_story_editor_size_that_loads_back` fails on main with `invalid type: null, expected f32`; its cases also pin the clamping at both ends and that a size within the range is stored as given. On a release build the steps from the issue leave `"storyEditorSize": 14.0` in `ui.json`, and the workspace and the shortcut are still there after the next launch; `1e39` is stored as 36. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Swatches panel header like InDesign's (Fill/Stroke proxy, container/text, Tint); swatches go to the fill or stroke in front (blocked by #592)

## What

The Swatches panel gets InDesign's header row, and a click on a swatch goes to whatever is in front, as in InDesign.

In LYH Studio's InDesign tutorial (episode 6), "1969" is coloured from the Swatches panel at 8:28 and the loop's stroke at 9:15. InDesign's Swatches panel opens with a header: the **Fill/Stroke proxy**, **Formatting affects container / text**, and **Tint**. DesignCraft's panel had none of this. It showed an "Applies to fill" label, a click always set the fill (stroke was in a right-click menu), and the bottom row was a hint ("Right-click: stroke, groups") and a plus button.

- **Engine** (`object.fill`, `object.stroke`):

title: INDD: graphics whose linked file is missing show InDesign's preview
author: govindaroyaiub
body:

title: Respect Find/Change scope and first-match limits
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Selecting the first “red” in “red red” and choosing Find Next could select and replace the second word outside the Selection scope. Retain the original search bounds as Find Next paints successive hits, and consume those bounds when Change All confirms.

A document-scoped `find.change` request with `first:true` could change one match in every matching story. Limit the command to one match across the document, skipping stories with no match. For separate stories “red red” and “red”, changing “red” to “blue” should produce “blue red” and “red”, with `count: 1`. Keep the existing Change All behavior for `first:false`. This enforces DesignCraft’s command contract.

Keep the context in the engine so the dialog, commands and control channel agree. Restart continuation for matcher changes, and discard the context after external selection changes, edits, document changes or dialog dismissal/replacement. This includes selecting the same word again and a failed native file drop that replaces Find with an alert. Match within the bounded substring, preserving UTF-8 and zero-width GREP progress. Existing Text/GREP controls and visual layout are retained.

Repair selection endpoints that fall inside a Unicode character after replacement, preserving the range’s direction. Replacing the selected X in “éX” with “🙂” can then be followed by Selection Find. Already-valid offsets retain their existing behavior, and carets stay collapsed. Regression cases cover both directions, multiple replacements, empty results and unaffected stories.

The scope follows Adobe’s [public search-scope guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/desktop/get-started/settings-and-preferences/search-scope-options.html): Selection stays within selected text. The context lifetime, forward continuation and post-replacement boundary policy are DesignCraft behavior. Child/cell/note story traversal and the separate GREP dialect work in #316 are outside this change.
