title: Keep merged-cell selection highlighting and formatting consistent
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Selecting a row or column that intersects a merged cell could omit that cell from highlighting and formatting when its top-left corner was outside the selection. Replacing cell text could also leave the caret inside a UTF-8 character, causing subsequent quote typing to fail.

Resolve selected grid positions to unique owning cells for highlighting, text formatting, cell options, cell styles and conversion from graphic to text cells. Cell-style creation samples the owner of the selection's upper-left grid position. Preserve the selection rectangle, existing UI paint style and controls, stroke-edge rules and merged-cell move restrictions.

Repair cell-text selection endpoints with the existing character-boundary flooring helper. Keep valid offsets unchanged; when the selected table has disappeared, preserve the existing parent-caret fallback by flooring the old anchor and collapsing both endpoints there.

Adds 11 regression test declarations: 2 document, 8 engine and 1 UI. Coverage includes row/column selections crossing merged cells, owner ordering and bounds, unchanged neighbors, formatting and unique cell counts, graphic conversion, style sampling, LTR/RTL stroke masks, rejected merged-cell moves, canvas paint output, and UTF-8 caret repair with forward/reverse selections, quote typing and the removed-table fallback.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` (1,387 passed, zero failed, four ignored), the locked WebAssembly web check, and all 11 focused regressions passed. Linux native row/column replays verified formatting of both selected owners with unchanged neighbors; a caret replay verified Unicode replacement followed by quote typing. Offscreen UI menu replays, both screenshots and five saved native documents were inspected. Development/test debug information was disabled, with debug assertions and overflow checks enabled. Other OS runtimes and browser execution were not tested.

title: Canvas: baseline grid draws only the lines on the page
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #844.

With Show Baseline Grid on, the canvas walked the grid from its start, one line per step, with no bound. A start far above the page made the next frame draw lines until the app ran out of memory. The start can come from `document.preferences`, a saved file or an IDML package.

- The lines drawn are now the ones inside the page, `start + n * increment` for n >= 0, found without walking the lines above it. Snapping already treats the grid this way (`pass_baseline`).
- At most 15,552 lines are drawn per page, one per point of a 216 in page, so no input makes the loop long.
- A grid that starts on the page looks as before. A start above the page no longer draws lines over the pasteboard above it.

The start itself stays as the document holds it; this PR changes only the drawing.

Validation: `baseline_grid_lines_are_the_ones_on_the_page` fails on the old line walk (83,333,400 lines for a start of -1e9); it also pins the cap, the bottom edge and a start that is not a number. On a release build the steps from the issue keep answering at under 1 ms a frame, and a `.designcraft` file and an IDML package with that start open and stay responsive. On screen, the default start, a start of -30 and a start of -1e17 each draw the lines on the page only. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Compose: cross-reference index no longer rebuilds itself
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #851.

The cross-reference index composed its destination stories through the cache. A destination story with a running header variable asked for the running-header index; that index composed the story holding the cross-reference, which asked for the cross-reference index again. Neither index was ever finished, the stack overflowed and the app aborted, which the panic guard can't catch.

- `XrefIndex::build` now composes a destination story that holds a running header without resolving it, the way it already composed one that holds cross-references. The cross-reference index no longer asks for any other index, so the loop can't form from either side.
- The page of a destination in such a story is found with the header's text left out. It differs only where that text would push the destination onto another page.

Validation: `cross_reference_into_a_story_with_a_running_header_composes` aborts with a stack overflow on main; it also pins that the reference still shows its destination's page and that the header still shows the other story's paragraph. On release builds the steps from the issue render in the app and through `designcraft-cli`: the first frame shows "See .Chapter one" and the reference reads "“Chapter one” on page 1". The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: macOS DMG: hdiutil create -srcfolder, so the installed app passes codesign --strict
author: Deeev201
body:
## What

The macOS DMG is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder` instead of `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` + `convert`, the way VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1085) and PdfCraft (storytold/pdfcraft#823) already do, with the same five-try `hdiutil_retry` for CI's "Resource busy". After signing, the image is mounted and the app inside is checked with `codesign --verify --strict --deep`, so this can't regress silently.

## Why

`makehybrid -hfs` stamps a `com.apple.FinderInfo` extended attribute on every file in the image. Gatekeeper still accepts the app (`spctl` says "Notarized Developer ID"), but `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on the app in the mounted DMG, or on a copy installed from it with Finder or `ditto`, fails:

```
DesignCraft.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

This shows up in the current releases of PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, EffectCraft and DesignCraft (VectorCraft, LightCraft and PdfCraft, which already switched, pass).

## Checked

- `bash -n packaging/macos/package.sh`
- A small signed test bundle packed both ways: `makehybrid -hfs` left FinderInfo on all 7 files and `--strict` failed; `create -srcfolder -fs HFS+` left none and `--strict` passed.
- I couldn't run the full signed/notarized packaging locally (no Developer ID), so CI's packaging job is the real test.

title: Control: bound click and drag input before queuing events
author: MMexicann
body:
`ui.click` previously accepted an unrestricted `count`, adding two events per click on the UI thread. Drag steps were clamped independently, so `ui.drag` could also queue an unlimited number of endpoint clicks. This could freeze the app or exhaust memory.

Validate positive integer counts and the complete event cost before queuing the first event. Clicks and drags share a 10,003-event budget with already pending synthetic input, preserving capacity for the existing 10,000-step drag. Checked arithmetic rejects overflow-sized inputs. Rejected requests preserve the queue, including any pending button releases; capacity becomes available as ordinary frames consume input.

Documents the limits and intentional rejection of oversized gestures and invalid counts. Adds five tests covering exact limits, limits exceeded, combined steps/counts, pending input, malformed values, arithmetic overflow, queue draining, and ordinary event order/buttons/modifiers.

Validation:
- The bounded regression failed before the fix: 5,002 clicks returned success.
- All five new regression tests pass.
- `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci`: all six gates passed (formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, layers, WebAssembly). Workspace tests: 1,381 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored; all 15 WebAssembly crate checks passed.

Fixes #732.

title: fix(compose): odd/even page starts keep their parity at the top of a frame
author: xoincare
body:
## Problem

A paragraph whose Start Paragraph option is **Next Odd Page** stays on an even page when it begins at the top of a frame there. Likewise, **Next Even Page** stays on an odd page. Odd and even page break characters behave the same way.

In a book, this happens whenever a section ends exactly at the bottom of an odd page: the next part or chapter opener, styled "Next Odd Page", opens on a left-hand page instead of the following right-hand page.

Repro with `designcraft-cli`: a facing 3-page document, a threaded story whose first frame is on page 2, and the first paragraph set to `startParagraph: "nextOddPage"`. `toc.entries` reports the paragraph on page **2**. Expected: page **3**, with page 2 left empty.

Cause: `compose_story` applies a start option only when `cur.last_baseline.is_some()`. That is correct for Next Page / Next Frame / Next Column, since at the top of a frame there's nothing to break away from. But it also drops the parity requirement of Next Odd / Next Even Page.

## Fix

New `Cursor::start_at_top`: at the top of a frame, a Next Odd Page or Next Even Page start moves on with `next_page(.., Some(parity))` when the frame's page has the other parity. Every other start option at the top of a frame does nothing, as before.

It is called at the three places that skip start options at the top of a frame:
- paragraph start options
- break characters ending the previous paragraph
- tables

## Testing

- New test `odd_and_even_page_starts_keep_parity_at_the_top_of_a_frame` (`crates/compose/src/tests.rs`). A paragraph sits at the top of page 2 after a page break. Next Page and Next Even Page leave it on page 2; Next Odd Page moves it to page 3. Without the fix it fails: `left: [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2)]`, `right: [(0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 3)]`.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-compose`: 171 passed (1 ignored), including the existing `break_characters_end_their_paragraph_and_keep_page_parity`.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --tests --no-fail-fast`: everyt…

title: Tables: table.options limits header and footer rows
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #861.

`table.options` added rows until the table held the requested header and footer rows, without an upper limit. The Table panel's Header Rows and Footer Rows fields send the typed number as it is, so a large number froze the app and exhausted memory.

- Both counts are now capped at 100, the limit `table.insert` already applies to the same two values.
- The cap is in the command, so the panel, the control channel and MCP all get it. The panel then shows the count the table really has.

Validation: `table_options_limits_header_and_footer_rows` fails on main with `(5000, 5000, 10001)` header, footer and total rows instead of `(100, 100, 201)`. On a release build the steps from the issue answer at once and leave 100 header rows, with memory flat at 200 MiB; typing 200000 into the panel's Header Rows field does the same. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

author: wdunn001
body:
## What this gives a user

Open and Save As reach cloud storage through CollabCraft, the service every Craft app talks to.

title: Typography panel
author: andrestelex
body: ### Typography panel proposal Typography designers were requesting updates to the OpenType features UI implementation in Adobe products for ages. Some software like Affinity has a better solution. This is a proposal to have an initial approach to OpenType features, that is easy to understand (as much as possible) for users in general and easy to access. Ideally, typesetting operations could all be moved to this panel (for example, setting 'All caps' only from there and not from Character Panel. A Typography panel (Window ▸ Show Panel, and the icon column) lists the features of the selected text's fonts, merged over those fonts, grouped as Ligatures, Alternates, Stylistic Sets (named by the font), Figure Style, Figure Width, Figure Position and Capitals. A section or choice appears only when a font offers it. This feature is an advantage over Adobe products where there is some menu diving. It's similar to Affinity approach. Each feature is a checkbox: checked when all of the selection has it, a dash when only some of it does, empty when none does. A feature only some of the selection's fonts offer is italic. Mutually exclusive choices are checkboxes too, and choosing one turns the others off. `type.openTypeFeatures` reports each feature's applied and available state over the selection. `type.feature` turns features on or off across the selection, keeping each run's other features. The fonts crate reads GSUB and GPOS feature lists and stylistic set names. The Character panel's OpenType menu is now a button that opens or focuses the Typography panel. The icon column's Typography entry reused the Character icon. It now uses an "OT" glyph (panel-typography), and a test checks it is neither the placeholder …

title: Character panel: live variable font sliders, aligned rows, axis-only style names
author: andrestelex
body: ### Summary Fixes a set of Character panel issues found while using variable fonts. The sliders didn't update live or accept typed values, the Size/Tracking and Leading/Baseline rows didn't line up, and the panel was wider than it needed to be. Style names with axis settings now show their axes instead of the named style, and auto leading is shown in parentheses. Changes - Live variable font sliders. Dragging an axis slider previews the change on every frame and commits it as one undo step on release. - Typed values. Each axis has a number field beside its slider, so typed values apply. The slider's own value box never received typed input, because changes only applied on release. - Aligned layout. Each axis row is label, slider, value field, so every slider has the same length. Size/Tracking and Leading/Baseline sit in two equal columns with matching label and field widths. - Auto leading. Auto leading is shown in parentheses, for example (14.4), as the paragraph panel shows it. - Axis-only style names. A style with axis settings shows its axes alone, in parentheses (for example (wdth:110,wght:620,ital:1)), instead of the named style. This applies in the Character panel and the Text Frame floating bar. - Panel heading. The repeated "Character" heading is removed, so the family picker starts the panel. Notes for reviewers - The live drag and typed-value paths aren't covered by automated tests, since no bundled font is variable. They need a manual check with a variable font. These were tested in OSX with several Variable Fonts and were working fine.

title: Type tool: dead keys and input-method composition on the canvas
author: andrestelex
body: Problem Accents typed with dead keys didn't work in text frames on macOS. ⌥E then I typed ei instead of í, and ⌥N and ⌥U failed the same way. Japanese and Chinese input methods couldn't compose either. Every other app, and DesignCraft's own dialog text fields, handle this fine. Cause: macOS composes dead keys only for a window that has asked for its input method, and winit follows that. egui asks only when one of its own text fields has focus. The canvas never asked and ignored the input method's events. With the input method off, macOS sends the bare key, so ⌥E arrived as a plain e. Fix - Canvas (crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs): - While the Type tool has a caret, the canvas asks for the input method and tells it where the caret is, which is where the candidate window for Japanese or Chinese appears. - The text being composed goes to the new text.compose command. The finished text is typed with text.insert. - Engine (text.compose {text}, Session::composition()): - The text being composed is shown in the story as an interaction preview. It takes the exact format the next typed character would get: font, size, colour, tracking, and any format chosen at the caret. - It is never part of the document. It isn't recorded or undoable, and when it commits, the result is typed as one undo step with smart quotes and autocorrect applied. - Any other edit, caret move, tool change or drag drops it first. The canvas then tells the input method to forget it, so the next key can't finish an accent that's gone. - Display: the text being composed is drawn on a pale-yellow box with its glyphs in their own colour and no underline, as in macOS text fields. This reuses the renderer for InDesign-style inverted selec…

title: Support dragging across checkbox controls
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Fixes #681.

Drag across eligible checkboxes to apply the starting box’s opposite state. Preserve ordinary clicks and sparse attributes’ unset → on → off → unset cycle, and skip mixed, disabled, covered or clipped controls.

When a drag release needs another repaint, Enter waits for that endpoint to settle before applying and closing the dialog. Cancel, changed targets and Undo/Redo discard unfinished gestures.

title: Facing pages take their side from their section's page numbers (odd on the right), as InDesign shuffles them
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In a facing document, a page's side now follows its page number, as in InDesign: odd numbers are right pages.

In Chris Nielsen's "[Numbering PAGE SECTIONS in an InDesign Document](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9KVs37om0BM)", the spread 8–9 is selected (6:59) and Numbering & Section Options starts a section at 1 (7:07). The section starts on page 8, a left page. InDesign makes it a lone right-hand page 1, and the pages after it shuffle: TOPIC SECTION 4 moves to the left page 2. He then undoes it (7:16).

DesignCraft kept page 1 on the left, followed by "2 | 3, 4 | 5", so odd numbers sat on left pages.

![InDesign, DesignCraft before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/section-page-sides/sides_compare.png)

## How

- **`Document::repaginate`** (`doc/build.rs`) gives each facing page the side of its own number: `page_number` counts each section from its start number. Odd numbers are right pages, or left pages bound right to left. This replaces the special case for an even Start Page # (Document Setup), which follows from the same rule. Lone pages and spreads that don't shuffle behave as before.
- **`layout.section`** repaginates when a section starts, changes or is removed. Objects go with their pages, and it is one undo step.

The doc, engine, IDML and ui-egui tests pass (821), and clippy is clean. The exceptions are the usual Windows-only `recovery::` and symlink tests.

title: ui_shot: render every script line so long scripts don't time out on the GPU
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

`examples/ui_shot.rs` (the headless screenshot tool used for PR images) failed on long scripts with:

```
render failed: PollError: The requested Wait timed out before the submission was completed.
```

I hit this while replaying Chris Nielsen's "[Numbering PAGE SECTIONS in an InDesign Document](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9KVs37om0BM)". The script builds a 50-page facing document, adds parent-page numbers, sets seven sections and then takes one screenshot. It failed every time. With a screenshot after each section, it worked.

## Why

`Harness::step()` doesn't render, so each frame's texture changes wait for the next `render()`. Every edit redraws the Pages panel's 50 thumbnails as new textures. Without screenshots in between, the final render had to upload all of them at once, and the GPU wait timed out.

## How

After every script line that isn't a screenshot, ui_shot calls `harness.render()` and drops the image, so texture changes are applied as they come. Scripts run a little slower; screenshots are unchanged.

## Testing

- **Before:** the 50-page script fails on main's ui_shot ("render failed").
- **After:** with this change it renders, in about 1 min 45 s.
- **Clippy** is clean on the examples. No test covers it: it's a dev tool, and the failure depends on the GPU.

## Dependencies

None.

author: moppeeer
body:
## What

The Direct Selection tool (white arrow) pressed on a corner or anchor of an object that isn't selected now selects it and pulls just that point, as in InDesign.

In Chris Nielsen's "[The Adobe InDesign Toolbox](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t12Va8ThcaE)" (9:57–10:48), the black arrow selects a graphics frame and switching to the white arrow selects all its anchor points. title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `designcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: designcraft`;
  - `conflicts: designcraft, designcraft-bin, designcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.designcraft`, not `designcraft`.** The AUR already has `designcraft`, `designcraft-bin` and `designcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.7.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `designcraft-0.7.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.
- `pacman -Qip` reads the package, and `.PKGINFO` has the expected name, versi…

title: Render: wide effect blurs are drawn at a lower resolution
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #904.

A drop shadow, inner shadow or outer glow with a large size made one render need gigabytes. Two buffers grew with the blur:
- On the multithreaded pipeline, `with_filters` drew the effect into an offscreen image reaching three standard deviations of the blur past the object on every side, up to 65,023 px a side.
- vello pads a filter layer by the same distance on every side. That one also hit single-threaded contexts (the web build): with a filled frame, a 10,000 pt shadow ran away there as well.

A blur wider than 1,024 device pixels (3σ) is now drawn offscreen at a lower resolution, where it is 1,024 px wide, and scaled back up with bilinear filtering. The offscreen image stays within 1,024 px of the window on every side, and vello's padding within another 1,024 px. A blur that wide has no detail to lose: next to main, a 1,200 pt shadow at the fitted zoom and a 100 pt shadow at 1000% differ by at most 3/255 per channel. Narrower blurs take the same path as before.

The sizes are still stored as given; #643 adds limits where they are set.

Validation: `a_wide_blur_is_drawn_offscreen_at_a_lower_resolution` fails on main with a 30,204 px offscreen image for a 10,000 pt shadow at 100%. On a release build the steps from the issue, drop shadows from 5,000 to 100,000 pt, inner shadow and outer glow at 10,000 pt, the single-threaded renderer (`DESIGNCRAFT_RENDER_THREADS=0`) at 10,000 and 20,000 pt, and 10000 typed into the Effects panel's Size field all keep answering, with memory under 400 MiB. A 10 pt shadow renders byte-identical to main. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Color parsing: bare CMYK is always 0..100, so C 1 is a 1 % tint
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #910.

#510 fixed the mixed case by picking one scale per colour, but kept "every component within 0..1 means fractions" for the older form, so `{"c": 1, "m": 0, "y": 0, "k": 0}` still became solid cyan. Those values are ordinary print tints, so the guess can't be made safely. `parse_color` now reads a bare `{c,m,y,k}` as 0..100 always, as the params docs already say. Fractions still work through the colour's own form, `{"model": "cmyk", …}` (what `color.convert` takes and returns), which is read without guessing. Nothing in the repo sends the bare form as fractions; the Color panel already sends percentages, so its C/M/Y/K of 1 or less now apply as typed. RGB arrays keep the current rule; I left them out since the issue is about CMYK, happy to extend the fixed scale to `[r,g,b]` too if you prefer.

This touches the same function as #660 (thanks @aiongg), which adds the `{model, …}` branch with range checks for the panel and picker; I kept mine minimal so either can rebase onto the other easily.

The 1/255 steps mentioned in the issue come from the PDF writer (inks are written as 8-bit), not from parsing; not changed here.

Validation:
- `color_tests::cmyk_percentages_of_one_or_less_stay_percent` (swatch.create C 1 → object.fill → PDF export, plus `object.color` C 0.5 M 0.5): fails on main (`got 1 0 0 0`, the swatch is C 100 %), passes here; the PDF assertion alone also catches the old rule (`[[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]]`)
- `percent_components_at_most_one_stay_percent` updated: its fraction case now uses `{"model": "cmyk", …}`
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib cmd::style::` and `cmd::colorsettings::`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; the full `cargo xtask ci` is left to the checks here
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Package: a missing link stays missing, with no empty file in Links/
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #908.

`write_links` (used by `file.package` and `links.copyTo`) wrote every placed asset's bytes into the Links folder and relinked the document to the copy. A missing link has no bytes, so it came out as a 0-byte file, and since the link status compares the file with the (empty) copy in the document, the reopened package listed it as `ok` while preflight still flagged it. Now an asset with no bytes is skipped: nothing is written for it and it keeps its original path, so it stays `missing` in the packaged `.designcraft` and `.idml`, and the report keeps listing it as `(missing)`, which is what InDesign's Package does. Thanks for the detailed repro.

A linked file that is gone but whose bytes are still in the document (a native `.designcraft`) is still copied, since there is something real to copy. I left `links.list` alone for 0-byte files already sitting on disk from older packages; happy to add that too if you want it here.

Validation:
- `cmd::package::tests::package_leaves_missing_links_missing`: places two linked SVGs, exports IDML without embedding, deletes one, reopens and packages. Fails on main (`a missing link is not copied`: Links/gone.svg exists), passes here; the present link is still packaged and reported `ok`
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib cmd::package` and `cmd::links`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: PDF: a placed PDF 1.7 with /Version /1.7 in its catalog goes into PDF/X-4 exports
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #907.

#40 made a placed PDF 1.7 go into PDF/X-4 (1.6) by relabelling its `%PDF-1.7` header, but hayro's `Pdf::version()` prefers the catalog `/Version` over the header, so a file that sets both (TCPDF does) still reads as 1.7 and the export fails naming it. `placed_pdf` now also relabels `/Version /1.7` to `/1.6` in place (same length, so the xref offsets hold), the same thing `qpdf --force-version=1.6` does to the catalog. That also covers a 1.4 header with a 1.7 catalog key. A catalog inside a compressed object stream is still left as it is and the export keeps naming the file, as before; happy to switch to an incremental update of the catalog if you'd rather cover that case too.

Validation:
- `placed_pdf_print_tests::catalog_version_17_placed_in_pdfx4` (a hand-built one-page PDF with `/Version /1.7` in its catalog, headers 1.7 and 1.4): fails on main (`logo.pdf is PDF 1.7: save it as PDF 1.6 or older`), passes here; the output is `%PDF-1.6` and reads as 1.6. `pdf_17_placed_in_pdfx4` still passes.
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-pdf -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Footnotes: Span Footnotes Across Columns sets notes across the frame
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #915.

The IDML import and the Footnote Options dialog already store `span_columns`, but `crates/compose/src/notes.rs` reserved room and stacked notes per (frame, column) at the column width, so the option never reached the layout. With it on, a frame's notes now share one area across all its columns: they're composed at the frame's text width, every column of the frame reserves their height, and they're stacked against the frame bottom with the rule above. When the reference sits in a later column, the earlier columns have already been set down to the bottom, so the frame is re-laid from its first paragraph with that room remembered (the remembered height only grows, so the re-lay can't loop). With the option off nothing changes.

One thing to note: if after the re-lay the reference moves on to the next frame, the first frame keeps the band empty. It only happens when the reference sits in the last line or two of the last column (with three columns, 1 position in 20 in my probe). That felt better than chasing it back and forth, but happy to switch if you'd rather handle it differently.

Validation:
- `footnotes_span_columns_across_the_frame_bottom` (2-column frame, one note referenced in column 1 and then in column 2): fails on main (the note rect is 36..230, one column wide), passes here; with the earlier-column re-lay disabled it fails on "column 0 text clears the note"
- `cargo test -p designcraft-compose --lib footnote`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

author: moppeeer
body:
## What

The Free Transform tool (E) now works as InDesign's. Before, it was a placeholder that did nothing.

![InDesign, DesignCraft before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/free-transform/ft_compare.png)

## Behaviour

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

DesignCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

DesignCraft 0.8.0's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `designcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.8.0 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `designcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: Images: indexed-colour TIFFs decode through their palette
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #927.

Neither `image` nor `tiff` (0.11) decodes PhotometricInterpretation 3, so `pixel_size` and `decode_rgba` in `crates/images` returned `None` for palette TIFFs: `file.place` failed with "unsupported or corrupt image" and PDF export skipped the image. Now a palette TIFF with 1-, 2-, 4- or 8-bit indices is read by `tiff` as if it were gray (a copy of the file with tag 262 set to 1), so strips, tiles and compression are still `tiff`'s job, and each index is looked up in the ColorMap, whose 16-bit entries are scaled with `>> 8`, as Photoshop and Pillow write them. Both `file.place` and the export go through these two functions, so they now place and print the logo.

I kept it in its own functions, checked before the `image` path, so it should sit next to #830 (CMYK TIFFs with alpha) without conflicts. Patching the tag rather than unpacking strips ourselves felt like the smallest way that keeps LZW/PackBits/Deflate working; happy to switch if you'd rather go another way.

A possible follow-up, left out here: `links.list` reports `status` from the file on disk (present / modified), not from whether it decodes, so an undecodable image still reads `ok`. Making it and preflight say so is a separate path.

Validation:
- `palette_tiff_decodes_through_its_colormap` (8-bit raw and LZW, 4-bit raw, fixtures written in the test with the `tiff` encoder): fails on main (`pixel_size` gives `None`), passes here; reading the ColorMap's low byte instead of `>> 8` makes it fail again
- issue repro with the Pillow files (`pal_raw.tif`, `pal_lzw.tif`): `file.place` ok, `links.list` pixels [64, 48], `file.exportPdf` no warnings, and the rendered PDF shows (0, 128, 255)
- `cargo test -p designcraft-images --lib tiff`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-images --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Type tool: a press over a locked empty frame draws a new text frame instead of converting it
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

The Type tool now draws a new text frame over a locked empty frame, as InDesign does. Before, it turned the locked frame into a text frame.

In Adobe's "[Set up a modern magazine layout](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/how-to/design-magazine-layout.html)" (Brian Wood):
- **2:12:** a frame is drawn round the spread inside the margins, given a 6 pt stroke and locked with ⌘L "so you don't accidentally move the frame".
- **4:01–4:23:** the Type tool draws the quote, heading and body text frames on top of it.

In DesignCraft the press landed inside the locked frame and the Type tool converted that frame into a text frame, putting the caret in it. No new frame was drawn, so the text frames couldn't be made where the video makes them.

![InDesign, DesignCraft before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/type-tool-locked/tl_compare.png)

## How

- **`tools/text.rs`:** the Type tool takes a hit only on:
  - text frames, locked ones included, since InDesign lets you edit text in a locked frame;
  - unlocked empty frames, which it converts as before.

  Over a locked empty frame, the press goes on to draw a new text frame.
- **`text.placeCaret`:** refuses to convert a locked empty frame, or one on a locked layer, so the engine and the control channel follow the same rule.

## Tests

`the_type_tool_draws_a_text_frame_over_a_locked_frame` (engine, through the tool's pointer events):
- A Type tool drag over the locked, stroked page frame draws a new text frame at the dragged rectangle, and the locked frame stays empty.
- `text.placeCaret` on the locked frame is refused.
- Once unlocked, a press converts it as before.
- It fails without the change.

The tools, engine and ui-egui tests pass (781), and clippy is clean.

## Dependencies

None.

title: fix: find optical-size fonts named by their WWS family and style (#911)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #911.

InDesign names an optical-size face by its WWS names (name IDs 21/22, e.g. "Kepler Std Display" / "Light"), but the font database only read the typographic names (IDs 16/17, falling back to 1/2: "Kepler Std" / "Light Display"). So an IDML naming the face the InDesign way reported "Missing font" in `preflight.run` and `font.list`, and the text fell back to the default font, even with the font in `Document Fonts`.

## What changed

- A face now also records its WWS family and style when they differ from the typographic ones (`FontFace::wws`, and the system font catalog entries).
- The WWS family counts as an alias wherever a family is looked up:
  - availability (`has_family`, used by `preflight.run` and `font.list`), for document, loaded and installed (cataloged) fonts;
  - loading an installed family from the catalog;
  - face resolution (`face`): when no face has that typographic family, faces whose WWS family matches are tried, and the style is matched against their WWS style ("Light" finds the "Light Display" face);
  - the style list (`styles`), so `font.list` doesn't report "Light" as a missing style (`styleMissing`).
- Typographic names still win: the WWS names are only tried when no face has the requested typographic family, so existing lookups don't change.

## Tests

`optical_size_face_is_found_by_its_wws_names` (crates/fonts) loads a synthetic document font with typographic names "DocFont Kepler" / "Light Display" and WWS names "DocFont Kepler Display" / "Light" (new `testing::font_with_wws` helper). It checks that the WWS family is available, resolves to the face, and lists "Light" as its style, and that the typographic names still work. The test fails on main.

title: Rulers: a document zero point, a ruler origin, and guides from the ruler corner
author: zydvc26s67-web
body:
## What

Implements the InDesign-style ruler zero-point feature: the '+' crosshair where the rulers meet (top-left) was purely decorative — this makes it work.

- **Drag** the ruler corner to move the document's zero point. Rulers and X/Y fields (Control, Properties, Info, `transform.set`) now measure from it, on every spread. It's real document state, so it round-trips through IDML (`ZeroPoint`) and survives save/reload.
- A **click that stays in the corner** does nothing (no accidental nudges).
- **Double-click** resets the zero point back to the default (top-left of the current spread's first page).
- **Right-click** the corner for Lock/Unlock Zero Point, so it can't be moved by accident.
- **Cmd-drag** (Ctrl on Windows/Linux) from the corner adds a horizontal *and* vertical guide through the drop point, as one undo step — matching InDesign's combined zero-point/guide gesture.
- Preferences › Units & Increments gains a **ruler origin** setting (Spread / Page / Spine) that the zero point is measured from; IDML reads/writes it too (`RulerOrigin`) instead of assuming the spread.

New engine commands: `view.zeroPoint {at?, reset?}` and `view.lockZeroPoint {on?}` — neither is an undo step, so undo/redo leave the zero point and its lock alone, as in InDesign. `guide.add` gains `orientation: "both"` with `point: [x, y]` for the one-undo-step H+V pair from the corner drag.

Localized strings added for Origin / Spine / Lock / Unlock Zero Point (ar, it, ja, pt-BR, uk).

## Why

This is the feature the user asked for directly: in InDesign, clicking the '+' in the ruler corner and dragging resets the ruler's zero point, which you then use as the new reference for placing guides. title: Keep XLSX formula text results as text on import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/xlsx.rs:50-57 (fn value, the `_` arm)` (no existing issue): XLSX import turns text formula results like "01234" into numbers (leading zeros lost).

## Cause
In `value()` in `crates/textimport/src/xlsx.rs`, only `t="s"`, `t="inlineStr"` and `t="b"` cells were read as text. Excel stores the cached text result of a formula as `t="str"`. That cell type went through the numeric parse and format, so "01234" became "1234" and "1E5" became a number.

## Fix
`value()` has a new `t="str"` arm that returns the cached `<v>` text unchanged. This covers both `import()` (`file.place`) and `records()` (data merge). The module doc comment now mentions formula strings.

## Verified
- Regression test `formula_text_results_keep_their_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib formula_text_results_keep_their_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Numeric cells (no `t`) and the other cell types (`e`, `d`) still use the existing number formatting.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Type: let a blank line's hidden paragraph mark take leading immediately
author: zydvc26s67-web
body:
## Problem

In InDesign, you can select the hidden paragraph mark (pilcrow) at the end of a blank line and change its leading, which changes that line's height. DesignCraft had no equivalent: an empty paragraph has no visible characters, so there was nothing for a caret to land on that the formatting commands actually applied to.

Concretely, `type.char` either:
- deferred the attribute change to "the next character you type" (in a non-empty story), silently discarding it as far as the current blank line was concerned, or
- only ever applied to the story's sole run when the *entire* story was empty.

Neither path let you change the leading of a blank line sitting between two other paragraphs — so there was no way to make a blank line taller or shorter.

## Fix

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`: added `empty_para_mark()` to recognize when a caret sits exactly on an empty paragraph's own hidden `\n` mark (its only character). `format_chars`/`apply_char_attrs` now apply attributes directly to that one-byte run immediately, instead of deferring to typing format.
- `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`: an empty paragraph produces no glyphs of its own, so the line-height fallback previously always used the paragraph's plain default leading. It now resolves the hidden mark's own character run (if overridden) first, so a leading change actually changes the rendered line height.

## Testing

Added `leading_applies_to_an_empty_lines_hidden_paragraph_mark` (in `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`), which selects the blank line between two paragraphs, applies a 40pt leading override, and asserts both that the override is stored immediately (no pending typing format) and that the composed line's rendered leading reflects it.

- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-compose`: all passing
- `cargo fmt -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-compose --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, asse…

title: Fix overflow in layout.pages.insert when `after` is u64::MAX
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/build.rs:377 (Document::insert_pages), called from crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs:91` (no existing issue): layout.pages.insert panics with integer overflow when `after` is u64::MAX.

## Cause
`Document::insert_pages` computed `(a + 1).min(n)` with an unchecked add. For `after = u64::MAX`, that panics with an overflow in debug builds. In release builds it wraps to 0 and inserts the pages at the start. The command also cast the JSON `u64` to `usize` with `as`, which truncates on 32-bit targets.

## Fix
`insert_pages` now uses `a.saturating_add(1).min(n)`, so an out-of-range `after` clamps to the end of the document. The command converts `after` with `usize::try_from(v).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` and uses `n.saturating_sub(1)` for the default. The regression test checks that the original pages stay first and the new pages come last, as well as the page count.

## Verified
- Regression test `insert_after_u64_max_appends_at_the_end`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --test insert_pages_bounds`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other commands that cast JSON numbers to `usize` are unchanged, as is the rest of the `insert_pages` logic.

title: Keep viewBox-only placed SVGs at viewBox size on IDML import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #950

## Cause
For a placed SVG, `graphic` in the IDML importer sized the graphic from `GraphicBounds`. InDesign writes the art's bounds there, and the art can overhang the viewBox (e.g. `-11 0 200 100`). The exporter then stretched the viewBox onto that larger size, so the whole SVG was scaled and shifted.

## Fix
When an SVG's root element has a `viewBox` and no absolute `width`/`height`, the importer now sizes the graphic by the viewBox, at one unit to the point. The `(l, t)` offset is unchanged, so the origin lands where GraphicBounds' Left/Top put it. This also applies when a linked SVG's asset is reused by a second placement.

## Verified
- Regression test `placed_svg_with_only_a_viewbox_keeps_its_viewbox_size`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-idml --lib placed_svg_with_only_a_viewbox_keeps_its_viewbox_size`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
SVGs with `width`/`height` are still stretched onto their GraphicBounds, as InDesign does. Non-SVG graphics and the PDF export code are unchanged.

title: math: cap LaTeX expression nesting depth so hostile input can't overflow the stack
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`math.svg` and `math.insert` accept an unbounded `latex` string, and the parser's recursive descent (`arg`/`atom`/`list`/`list_until_right`) recursed once per group. A controller request or a pasted formula with ~100k nested braces, `\frac`s or `\left(`s overflows the stack — a process abort the command guard cannot catch — losing every open document's unsaved state.

The fix adds a `MAX_NESTING` (256) cap to the parser: past it, groups stop descending and the rest of the input is consumed iteratively, so parsing stays linear with a bounded stack. A regression test feeds 100k nested braces, `\frac`s and `\left(`s to `to_svg`: the old code aborted with a stack overflow, the new code typesets an SVG. Real formulas nest a few dozen levels at most, so the cap changes nothing in practice.

Partially addresses #920 (finding 2, LaTeX recursion). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: idml: read PDFAttribute PageNumber so placed PDFs show their page
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A placement of a multi-page PDF lost its page number through IDML: `graphic()` always made the asset with `page: 0` and keyed `linked_assets` by path alone, so every placement of one file showed page 1 no matter what `PDFAttribute/@PageNumber` said. Import now reads `PDFAttribute/@PageNumber` (1-based) into `Asset.page` (0-based), and the read-once map is keyed by `(path, page)` so the same file at different pages stays apart. Export writes `PDFAttribute` back for pages past the first, so round trips keep the page; missing or malformed values mean page 1, as before. The regression test places one file at pages 2, 1 and 2, asserts the two assets' pages and their placement mapping, and round-trips through export both linked and embedded.

Fixes #905

title: layout.section: keep the settings the command does not name
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`layout.section` removed the section at a nonzero start with `retain()` and only then looked it up to preserve its properties, so the lookup always fell back to the defaults: editing one field (a marker, a start number) silently reset the style, prefix, include-prefix flag and start number. The existing section is now read before the list is rebuilt, and the rest of the command is unchanged. The regression test makes a Roman-numbered page-2 section with prefix `A-` and marker `First`, updates only the marker, and asserts startNumber, style, prefix and includePrefix are kept and the page label stays `A-i`.

Fixes #717

title: dtd: cap parameter-entity expansion instead of trusting a pass count
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`parse()` expanded parameter entities with up to eight passes of whole-string replacement, re-inserting each entity's original value and cloning the text every pass; a pass count is not an output bound, so a few hundred bytes of nested entities inflate multiplicatively (the test's 449-byte DTD reaches ~4 MB, and deeper chains go to gigabytes). Expansion now stops once it has added more than 1 MiB over the input and returns an error instead of continuing to allocate. The regression test builds a nested-entity DTD under 500 bytes and asserts it is rejected with the budget error, while a small inline entity still parses.

Fixes #713

title: script.run: roll a failed script back instead of stranding its edits
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A script whose later step failed kept the successful prefix in the document but truncated the prefix's own undo entries, and returned before the command's aggregate undo entry was recorded, so the edits could not be undone at all. `script.run` now snapshots the document, selection and history before it runs and restores them when a step fails: all-or-nothing, with the existing one-undo-step behavior on success unchanged. The regression test runs a `frame.create` followed by an unknown command, asserts the document has no frame, that nothing is left to undo, and that the next edit undoes normally.

Fixes #709

title: guard: restore the whole command transaction on a panic
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The guard restored only the active document's content and selection, so a command that edited through a nested successful command and then panicked left the nested edit's undo entry (and no redo) behind, and a command that opened or switched documents restored nothing at all. `guarded()` now snapshots every open document with its history and selection, the active index and the journal length, and restores them on a panic before the crash-recovery save. The active document's revision still moves forward so caches refresh, and a pre-existing interaction is cleared as before. The two regression tests pin the history/redo case and the document-collection case; the whole engine package is green.

Fixes #742

title: Color panel: the Tint field keeps typed text and applies it on Enter or leaving the field
author: guillehr2
body:
Part of #945: the Tint field. The C/M/Y/K and R/G/B fields that #945 reports are covered by #660, and this PR leaves them alone.

## Problem

A named swatch in the Color panel shows a Tint row: a slider with its value box. The value box was the `egui::Slider`'s own `DragValue`, and it had two problems:
- **It snapped back while you typed.** The panel reads the tint back from the document every frame. egui 0.36's `DragValue` drops the text being edited when the value it gets differs from the value it stored the frame before. Selecting "100%" and typing 60 went 100 → 6 → back to 100 → 1000, the same 10060 pattern #945 reports for the CMYK fields.
- **A typed tint was never applied.** The panel applied the tint only on the slider's `drag_stopped()`, so a value typed in the box was ignored.

## Change

- The slider still applies on release. It no longer draws its own value box (`show_value(false)`) and is sized like the C/M/Y/K tracks under it.
- The value box is now a `widgets::NumField`, the same field the Swatches panel uses for its Tint and the Properties panel for its values:
  - it keeps typed text while it has focus;
  - it applies the value on Enter or when it loses focus, clamped to 0–100 %.
- Both the slider and the field call `apply_swatch` as before, so what gets applied is unchanged.
- Scope: `crates/ui-egui` only. This PR doesn't touch `channel()`, the Color Picker or the spectrum, which #660 changes. #660 doesn't change the Tint block either, so the two don't overlap once #660 is rebased on current main.

## Before / after

Selecting the Tint field of a C=100 swatch, typing `6` and then `0` one frame apart, then pressing Enter. The images were rendered offscreen with `egui_kittest` (wgpu) at 2x.

| | Typed "60" | After Enter |
|---|---|---|
| Before (main): the field shows **1000**, and the tint stays 100 % | ![before, typed 60](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guillehr2/designcraft/25f3f839325bc62bb0cf767212bf9cfe2b456fed/color-panel-tint/before-2-typed…

title: Record one undo step for the four arrange shortcuts
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs:143-150` (no existing issue): Bring Forward / Send Backward / Bring to Front / Send to Back add two undo steps per command.

## Cause
`object.bringToFront`, `object.bringForward`, `object.sendBackward` and `object.sendToBack` each called `s.execute("object.arrange", …)` from inside their command handler. The inner call recorded an undo entry, and the outer command then saw the changed document and recorded a second entry with the same before-state. Each shortcut therefore needed two Undo presses.

## Fix
The four handlers now call the `arrange` function directly instead of going through `Session::execute`. Only the outer command records history, so each one adds exactly one undo step, the same as `object.arrange`.

## Verified
- Regression test `arrange_wrappers_add_exactly_one_undo_step`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib arrange_wrappers_add_exactly_one_undo_step`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`object.arrange` itself and the generic undo recording in `Session::execute`.

title: Report corrupt archive entries instead of treating them as missing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #719

## Cause
When reading `.designcraft` zips, the `read` helper in `load_zip` turned every lookup or read error (bad CRC, failed decompression) into `None`. A damaged embedded asset therefore loaded with empty data, and saving the document made the loss permanent. In textimport, `part_capped` returned `Ok(None)` when a DOCX/XLSX part was present but unreadable, so a damaged `word/styles.xml` or `xl/sharedStrings.xml` was dropped without an error.

## Fix
Both helpers now return `None` only for `ZipError::FileNotFound`. An entry that exists but fails to open, decompress, pass its CRC check or (for DOCX/XLSX parts) decode as UTF-8 is now an error: `FormatError::NotOurs("corrupt …")` for native files and `ImportError::Corrupt` for DOCX/XLSX. This also covers a present but unreadable `meta.json` or `document.json`. In `load_zip`, the asset loop now checks that the document references the asset id before reading the entry, so a corrupt entry for an unused asset id does not fail the load. Previously such entries were read and then discarded.

## Verified
- Regression tests `corrupt_embedded_asset_is_an_error_not_empty_data`, `corrupt_styles_part_is_an_error_not_absent`, `corrupt_shared_strings_part_is_an_error_not_absent`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-format --lib corrupt_embedded_asset_is_an_error_not_empty_data && cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib corrupt_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Link-only assets with no embedded entry still load with empty data, and optional DOCX/XLSX parts that are truly absent are still treated as missing. A `meta.json` that reads fine but does not parse as JSON still falls back to format version 1.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Bound decompressed size and entry count of native and IDML ZIP imports
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #710

## Cause
`load_zip` in designcraft-format read `meta.json`, `document.json` and every `assets/*` entry with unbounded `read_to_end`. `import_idml_report` decompressed and kept every non-directory entry of the package, including irrelevant ones. Neither limited the entry count, so a ~1 MB archive could expand to gigabytes in memory and crash the app.

## Fix
Both readers now refuse archives with more than 100,000 entries. They read each needed entry through `take(limit + 1)` with a per-entry limit and an archive-wide byte budget, so the sizes the archive claims are not trusted. IDML parts, and native assets the document doesn't reference, are only decompressed when the import actually needs them.

## Verified
- Regression tests `oversized_document_json_is_refused`, `oversized_asset_is_refused`, `too_many_entries_are_refused`, `unreferenced_entries_are_not_read`, `oversized_part_is_refused`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test --release -p designcraft-format --lib -- oversized too_many && cargo test --release -p designcraft-idml --lib -- oversized_part too_many unreferenced`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other ZIP readers (EPUB, text import, engine, UI) are left as they are. The limits are fixed constants, not settings.

title: Preserve stored IDML page liquid rules
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
IDML import and export now preserve the six supported stored page liquid rules on ordinary and master pages: Off, Scale, Recenter, GuideBased, ObjectBased, and UseMaster (ControlledByParent).

The shared page mapping uses the case-sensitive XML literals Recenter and UseMaster. Omitted, unknown, and unsupported PreserveExisting values retain the existing Off fallback. This change preserves stored rules without adding resize behavior.

Regression tests import literal XML independently of the exporter, check emitted attributes, and round-trip ordinary and master pages with parent relationships and page fields preserved.

Validation: `cargo test --locked -p designcraft-idml liquid_page_rules -- --nocapture`; `cargo xtask ci`; `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-web`.

Refs #872.

title: IDML: import and export ruler guides
author: moppeeer
body:

The INDD was converted to IDML with storytold/indd-utils, with the licensed Articulat CF in Document Fonts. In the video InDesign shows the page with **No errors**. title: Find Font: a style that differs only in spacing isn't reported missing
author: moppeeer

title: i18n: Georgian (ka) interface language
author: devius
body:
Glyphs: Georgian needs a font face; storytold/craft-fonts#27 adds Noto Sans Georgian (script `Geor`).

## Summary

Adds Georgian (`ka`, ქართული) as an interface language, in the same shape as the Italian (`it.rs`) and Ukrainian (`uk.rs`) tables.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ka.rs`: 1,765 entries. Every key of the shared, Arabic, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Italian and Ukrainian tables has a row, plus some labels that only the code or the command table use. That covers the 1,724 measured interface strings in `docs/localization-parity.md`.
- `i18n.rs`: `("ka", "ქართული")` is appended to `LANGUAGES`, and `tr` reads the Georgian table. `count_label` uses the category-first caption that Ukrainian already uses (`გვერდი: 5`), because Georgian nouns stay singular after a numeral.
- `menus.rs`: Edit ▸ Interface Language ▸ ქართული, and the `app.language` help text lists `ka`.
- Docs: `docs/localization-parity.md` (a new row, the counts and the history) and the ROADMAP.

Commits, one per topic (the Georgian-only ones need no other language to change):

- `19bacaa` i18n: Georgian (ka) interface language: the catalog, language entry, tests and docs above.
- `5d4ed2a` text: Georgian document language; no initial capitals for Georgian: Two document-side fixes for Georgian text. Neither depends on the Georgian interface catalog.

## What does not change

- Command ids, menu paths used by scripts, the control channel and document data.
- Storage: the choice is the existing `ui.language` value.
- No assets and no fonts. The UI fonts have no Georgian, and a separate PR adds a fallback from an installed face. Without that PR, Georgian labels need a system that egui can draw Georgian with.

- text: - Every other script, IDML round-trips of existing languages, and command ids.

## Translation quality

title: Add designcraft-hub: the CraftHub client path (the v3 adapter, spec §3.6 phase C / §18.4 row 4)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

`designcraft-hub` — the app-side binding that speaks the generalized collaboration core ([`craft-collab`](https://github.com/hasan-sdaif/crafthub), extracted from figcraft's proven `figcraft-collab` and proposed as `storytold/craft-libs#128`). This is DesignCraft's row of the adoption table — the pages/layout app, fourth in the §18.4 order, carrying the row's own named feature: **region locks of the `PageRange` shape** (§6.7: locks sync as document properties).

Nothing here changes user-visible behavior. The session wiring (a v3 `NetLink` behind the app's `crafthub` feature flag, default off) lands as the pilot follow-up once this contract is reviewed.

## The honest map

DesignCraft's model is spread-shaped, not frame-shaped: a document holds **spreads** (document spreads and parent — "master" — spreads), each spread holds **pages** and top-level **items** in z-order, and items nest through `Content::Group`.

- **Spreads** (`spread` / `parentSpread`) hang under the root; pages and items hang under their spread. Items hang off the *spread*, not the page — the model's page-item association is geometric (an item's centre sits on a page), not structural, and the page commands move items by translating `xf`, which the diff sees as a plain field write.
- **Repagination is honest churn**: rebuilding spreads mints fresh spread ids, so the diff emits spread deletes and creates plus `parent` moves for the pages and items that survived — exactly what the model did (tested: `repagination_roundtrip`).
- **The property tables**: the 31 synchronized `Item` fields, the 14 `Page` fields and the 2 `Spread` fields, each with the compile-time guard that a new saved field must decide how it syncs. Two fields needed honest wire renames to keep the generic tree's own `parent`/`position` unambiguous (`Spread::parent` → `parentInfo`, `Page::parent` → `parentSpread`).
- **A group's `content` property carries its payload without its children** — a group is `{"type":"group"}…

title: Skip .ase swatches with NaN or infinite colour components
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/ase.rs:83` (no existing issue): Load Swatches accepts NaN colour values from an .ase file; the saved document then can't be reopened.

## Cause
`ase::read` built `Color::Cmyk`/`Rgb`/`Gray` directly from the f32 values in the file without checking that they are finite. The Lab branch's `clamp` also lets NaN through. A NaN swatch was added by Load Swatches, saved as `null`, and after that the whole document could not be reopened.

## Fix
`ase::read` now checks every colour component of a block before it builds the colour. If any component is NaN or infinite, that swatch is left out, the same way blocks with an unknown colour model are. A Lab colour whose sRGB conversion is not finite is left out too.

## Verified
- Regression test `non_finite_components_are_skipped`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-color --lib ase::tests::non_finite_components_are_skipped`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Swatches are skipped rather than failing the whole file, so the valid swatches in the same file still load. `ase::write` and the document format are unchanged.

title: Eyedropper: with text selected, pick up the clicked text's formatting, as InDesign does
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Typefool's *The Secret to Perfect Design Layouts* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DzarZJXEDmI)). At 12:04 the designer selects body text, takes the **Eyedropper**, and clicks the third header: the body text takes the header's settings. He then sets it to Light ("so it copies the same preferences as a header").

## Problem
DesignCraft's Eyedropper always ran `object.matchAttributes`. With text selected and a text frame clicked, that copied the clicked **frame's** fill, stroke, corners, opacity and effects onto the frame holding the text. The selected text's formatting didn't change.

## Change
- **New command `type.pickUpFormat {frame, point}`:**
  - It finds the character under the point (at the end of a line, the one before it).
  - Its character style and overrides go to the selected characters.
  - Its paragraph's style and overrides go to the selected paragraphs.
  - It is one undo step, and works in table cells too (the selection's own story).
- **Tool:** with text selected, clicking a text frame with the Eyedropper sends `type.pickUpFormat`. Every other case is unchanged: placed images are still sampled, and other objects still have their attributes matched.

Not done (InDesign has it): Eyedropper Options (choosing which attributes to pick up), and the loaded-eyedropper state, where you pick up first and then click or drag over text.

## Context
The image shows the video's pages next to DesignCraft (`main` + #468/#937 + #976 + this PR, Inter Tight standing in for Neue Haas Grotesk):

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4, optional, shared, private)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a panel in DesignCraft. It talks to a
local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the panel says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside DesignCraft and names this app's world — documents of pages, spreads and parent pages, text and graphics frames, stories threaded between frames, guides, the Pathfinder, IDML in and PDF/EPUB out — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (explain a layout step, alt text for a page, name this document, print or export advice) are framed for it. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept and copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same right-to-left pass as the rest of the interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.
- **Models** — the Gemma 4 catalogue, every figure from the model's own card: **E2B** (3.1 GB, 4 GB RAM) for the lightest machines, **E4B** (5.0 GB, 6 GB), **12…

title: End the RTF \uN fallback skip at the end of its group
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/rtf.rs:107` (no existing issue): RTF import: the \uN fallback-character skip continues past the end of the group and eats the text that follows.

## Cause
After a `\uN` control word the RTF importer sets `pending` to the group's `\ucN` count so it can drop the ANSI fallback characters. The `}` branch removed the group state but left `pending` as it was. So when a group closed before its fallback character, as in `{\b \u8364} AB`, the importer dropped the first real characters after the group.

## Fix
`pending` is now reset to 0 when a `}` closes a group, because the RTF spec ends the fallback skip at the end of the group. A regression test covers the default `\uc1` case and the `\uc2` case.

## Verified
- Regression test `unicode_fallback_skip_ends_with_group`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib unicode_fallback_skip_ends_with_group`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
How `pending` is handled when a `{` opens a nested group is unchanged.

title: Flatten deleted text variables in table cells and notes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/variables.rs:49` (no existing issue): Deleting a text variable skips its instances in table cells, which then show a different variable.

## Cause
`variables.delete` rewrote only the text of the top-level stories in `d.stories`. The text of table cells, footnotes and endnotes lives in separate stories nested inside a story, so those stories kept the deleted variable's character. After `text_variables.remove(i)` that character pointed to the next variable, and every later variable's instances in those stories stayed one index too high.

## Fix
A new read-only check, `needs_unvar`, recursively looks through a story's text, its table cells and its foot/endnotes. Deleting a variable now takes a mutable borrow of a story only when this check finds an instance. `unvar` flattens the deleted variable's instances and shifts the later ones down, recursing into cells and notes. It unshares (`Arc::make_mut`) only the tables and notes that hold such an instance, and it bumps the parent story's revision when nested text changed.

## Verified
- Regression tests `delete_variable_reaches_table_cells`, `delete_variable_reaches_notes`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib delete_variable_reaches`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Editorial notes are not changed, because their text is a plain String and not a story that can hold variable instances. Recursion into nested stories stops at a fixed depth of 32.

title: Fonts: register every explicitly supplied family for documents
author: IanHollow
body:
A build can supply a craft-fonts manifest containing Arabic, Thai or Chinese faces, and the build script embeds them, but the document font database registers only its Japanese faces. The other supplied families cannot be selected without finding another copy on the host.

Register every explicitly supplied face. The existing bundled fonts stay first, followed by the same Japanese Mincho/regular-first order, then the remaining faces in manifest order. `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` stays optional and explicit. This adds no fonts, dependencies, build defaults, UI-language preferences or fallback lookup rules.

A synthetic test checks empty input, ordering and one-time inclusion of a multi-script face. A separate test checks every supplied family with system fallback disabled. The affected fallback and composition fixtures now establish their intended font coverage explicitly. The isolated-Arabic assertion compares the full ordered glyph sequence, allowing legitimate OpenType decomposition, and reports a skip when no Arabic face is available.

The selector regression fails with the original Japanese-only selection and passes with the repair. That run compiled the extracted production selector and its actual synthetic test with Rust 1.98.1. Rustfmt, zero-fuzz application and `git diff --check` pass. Full Cargo font/compose tests with and without optional input, actual font parsing and `cargo xtask ci` remain pending. No full application build was run for this draft.

This preserves the explicit-input boundary discussed in [#682](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/682). It does not address the separate Chinese UI-font request in [#332](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/issues/332).

title: Swatches: Load Swatches numbers repeated .ase names and names unnamed colors by value
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`load_swatches` matched each name in a swatch exchange (`.ase`) file against the document, which by then held the file's earlier colors. A color whose name the file had already used was dropped (with `replace`, it overwrote the earlier color). A color with no name was added with an empty name, and every later unnamed color was treated as a repeat of it. A file of seven colors with a repeated name and three unnamed colors added three of its six new colors.

- An unnamed color is named by its value, as `object.color` names an unnamed color (`C=0 M=0 Y=0 K=55`), with `named: false`.
- A name the file has already given gets the first free number (`Red 2`, `Red 3`), as `Styles::unique_name` numbers names. In a test build, a file of 100,000 colors with one name loads in 60 ms, and a file of 100,000 unnamed colors of one value loads in 148 ms.
- This changes the documented rule of `swatch.load` ("names already in the document are kept unless `replace`"): the file's own earlier colors no longer count as names already in the document, while names the document held before the load still follow the rule.
- The `swatch.load` description states both rules, and the change adds one line to the Progress log in `ROADMAP.md`.
- vectorcraft numbers repeated names and names unnamed colors by value in the same way when it opens `.ase` files: https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/644.

Validation:
- `color_tests::loading_swatches_numbers_repeated_names_and_names_unnamed_colors` loads that seven-color file into a document that holds one of its names, then loads it again with `replace`. Without the change it fails: 3 swatches are added where 6 are expected.
- `color_tests::loading_swatches_matches_the_first_swatch_of_each_name` now expects the file's second "New" to be added as "New 2".
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- On macOS, `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo xtask ci` passes all 7 steps; the test step reports 1,962 passed…

title: Type: formatting set on a blank line applies to the text typed there
author: aiongg
body:
- With the caret on a blank line (an empty paragraph), `type.char` formatted only the line's paragraph mark. Text typed next took the previous paragraph's format instead, so a size, leading or bold chosen there was lost on the typed text.
- The blank line's paragraph mark still takes the format right away (it sets that line's height), and the format is also kept as the typing format at the caret.
- Text inserted on a blank line takes that line's paragraph mark format (`Story::insert_format_at`), so the format also holds after the caret leaves the line and comes back, after undo or after reopening the file. Every other caret position keeps taking the format of the character before it. Typing with Track Changes on and the Character panel's reading at the caret use the same rule.

Follow-up to #949.

Tests: `cmd::text::open_type_tests::text_typed_on_a_blank_line_takes_the_format_set_there` (sets size 30 on the blank line between two paragraphs, types "Middle", checks the typed text and its mark have size 30 and the first paragraph's mark does not) and `cmd::text::open_type_tests::a_blank_lines_mark_format_is_typed_after_the_caret_returns` (the same after moving the caret away and back, with no typing format pending); `leading_applies_to_an_empty_lines_hidden_paragraph_mark` no longer asserts that no typing format is pending.

title: Effects: wide feathers and inner effects stay sharp at high zoom
author: aiongg
body:
- A blur wider than 1,024 device pixels is drawn offscreen at a reduced resolution. Basic Feather drew the whole object in that offscreen image, so a wide feather (for example 200 pt at 400% on a 2x screen) made the object itself look blurry. Inner shadow, inner glow, satin and bevel clipped to the shape inside the reduced image, so their edge was coarse and bled outside the shape.
- `with_filters` takes an optional clip (path and transform). At reduced resolution it clips the composited image on the device context; at full resolution it clips as before. The inner effects pass their shape as that clip.
- Basic Feather draws the object and its clip on the device context and only renders the blurred mask through `with_filters`.
- Effects whose blur fits at full resolution render as before.

Follow-up to #912.

Tests: `a_wide_feather_keeps_the_object_sharp_at_high_zoom` (the inside of a 1,000 pt feathered frame at 8 px/pt matches the unfeathered frame) and `a_wide_inner_effect_stays_inside_the_shape_at_high_zoom` (a 2,000 pt inner shadow and inner glow at 8 px/pt leave the pixels just outside the shape's edge unchanged), both in `crates/render/tests/effects.rs`.

title: Typography panel: every OpenType toggle, exported figure styles, working Standard Ligatures
author: aiongg
body:
- Proportional Metrics, Horizontal Kana, Localized Forms, Mark Positioning, Justification Alternates and Roman Italics had no control for local text after the OpenType menu became the Typography panel. A new Other Features section lists every character-format toggle (`otf::TOGGLES`) the other sections don't show, when the selection's fonts offer it.
- Lining, Oldstyle, Tabular or Proportional chosen alone set one tag, which IDML export wrote as `OTFFigureStyle="Default"`. Choosing one now also sets the other axis: the choice all of the selection already has, else Proportional (for a style) or Lining (for a width). Turning a checked one off clears both axes, back to the font's default figures.
- Standard Ligatures showed checked with Character › Ligatures off, and checking it couldn't turn ligatures back on; its `-liga` was also dropped by IDML export. The switch now reads and sets the `ligatures` attribute (`type.char`), and `type.openTypeFeatures` reports `liga` from it. `liga` stays out of the feature list, and a `-liga` already there (from `type.feature`) counts as off and is cleared when the switch is used.

Follow-up to #881.

Tests: `panels::typography::tests::every_character_format_toggle_has_a_control`, `panels::typography::tests::a_figure_style_or_width_chosen_alone_exports_as_a_figure_style` (clicks Lining, Tabular, Oldstyle and checks the exported `OTFFigureStyle`), `panels::typography::tests::standard_ligatures_switch_the_ligatures_attribute`, `panels::typography::tests::standard_ligatures_switch_on_clears_a_feature_list_liga_off`, `cmd::text::open_type_features_tests::standard_ligatures_follow_the_ligatures_attribute`.

title: Paths: Join and Convert Point respect locked layers and groups
author: aiongg
body:
- `path.join` and `path.convertPoints` checked only the path's own lock, so they closed, joined or reshaped a path on a locked layer or inside a locked group.
- Both now use the same check as the other path edits: a path that is locked, on a locked layer or in a locked group is left unchanged. Join refuses with "the path is locked" when no selected path is editable, or when two are selected and either is locked (it no longer closes the editable one instead); Convert Point does the same when none of its points is editable, and otherwise converts only the editable ones.

Follow-up to #960.
