title: Kerning: a value at the caret kerns the pair at the caret
author: aiongg
body:
- A kerning value or preset chosen in the Character panel or Properties with a bare caret in text was stored only as the format for the next typing, so the pair at the caret did not move.

At the start or end of a story or paragraph there is no pair and the value is kept for the next typing. A selection or selected frames take it exactly as `type.char` does.
- The Kerning control in both panels calls it, and at a caret its label shows the pair's current kerning.

Follow-up to #901.

Tests: `kern_pair_tests::kerning_at_a_caret_kerns_the_pair_in_one_undo_step`, `kern_pair_tests::kerning_a_selection_or_at_the_story_start_works_like_type_char` (engine), `a_manual_kerning_value_at_a_caret_kerns_the_pair` (ui-egui Character panel).

title: Type tool: a drag after several clicks extends the selection by words, lines or paragraphs (#981)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #981

## Before
A double click selected a word (triple a line, quadruple a paragraph), but holding the button and moving did nothing: `TypeTool` set `unit_selected` on the press and returned no action for every `Drag` while it was set. In InDesign the drag grows the selection a word (line, paragraph) at a time, in either direction, anchored on the unit first selected.

## Change
- Engine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`, `lib.rs`): `text.selectAt` records the unit it selected (`Session::text_unit`). `text.extendTo` takes an optional `unit: word|line|paragraph|story`; with it, and after a `text.selectAt` in the same story/cell, the selection becomes whole units from the first unit to the unit under the point: forward, anchor = start of the first unit, focus = end of the unit under the point (never shrinking inside the first unit); backward, anchor = end of the first unit, focus = start of the unit under the point. The unit computation moved into `unit_at` (shared by both commands; an unknown unit is the same error). Without `unit` nothing changes.
- Tool (`crates/tools/src/text.rs`): the press keeps the unit its click count chose and every drag sends `text.extendTo {frame, point, unit}`; a single-click drag still sends it without `unit`. Table cell drags are untouched.

## Tests
- `multi_click_tests::a_drag_after_several_clicks_extends_the_selection_by_units` (engine): double-click "brave", extend into "world." → `(7, 18)`; back inside the word → `(7, 12)`; into "Hello" → `(12, 0)`; triple-click the first line, extend into the second → the whole text; a drag without `unit` still moves the focus by characters; `unit: sentence` is an error.
- `clicks_in_a_row_edit_and_select_text` (tools): a drag after two presses emits `text.extendTo` with `unit: "word"`, after three with `"line"`, after one without `unit` (it previously asserted the drag emitted nothing).

title: Importers: XML element nesting and DTD group nesting are bounded (#712)
author: wstock
body:
Addresses #712 for three of its four sites; the fourth (math arguments/groups, `crates/engine/src/math.rs`) already carries `MAX_NESTING` on `main` and is unchanged here.

## What was unbounded
- `textimport::docx::parse` and `idml::xml::parse` build the element tree iteratively (a stack), so parsing itself never recursed — but `El::text()`, the block walk and the tree's `Drop` all recurse one frame per level. A document nested a few hundred thousand levels deep parses fine and overflows the stack the first time anything walks it; `catch_unwind` does not recover a stack overflow.
- `engine::dtd::particle` recurses once per `(` group with no budget: `<!ELEMENT a ((((…b…))))>` with enough parens overflows while parsing.

## Change
- `textimport::docx::MAX_DEPTH = 256` and `idml::xml::MAX_DEPTH = 256`: a `Start` event that would push past it is an error (`XML elements nested deeper than 256 levels`, with the position for IDML), before the element is built. Word's and InDesign's own XML stays well under a hundred levels.
- `dtd::MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 64`: `particle` takes the enclosing group depth and refuses a group past it (`content-model groups nested deeper than 64 levels`); real content models are single digits deep.

Nothing changes for input inside the budgets; the error paths are the parsers' existing `Corrupt` / `String` errors, so importers report them like any other malformed input.

## Tests (budget and budget+1, as the issue suggests; no real stack exhaustion)
- `docx::tests::nesting_past_the_budget_is_refused` — 256 nested `<w:p>` parse, 257 are refused with the message, 100 000 are refused.
- `xml::tests::nesting_past_the_budget_is_refused` (idml) — the same for `<A>`.
- `dtd::tests::content_model_groups_past_the_budget_are_refused` — 64 nested groups parse, 65 are refused, 100 000 are refused.

title: Tools: Cmd held with another tool borrows the Selection tool for one gesture (#919)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #919

## What InDesign does
With the Type tool (or any drawing tool) chosen, holding Cmd (Ctrl on Windows) turns the pointer into the Selection tool for as long as the button is down: you can click to select a frame, drag it, or pull a handle without going to the Tools panel. With the Pen family and the Pencil, Cmd gives the Direct Selection tool instead. Releasing the button leaves the chosen tool in place.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/tooling.rs`, one field in `lib.rs`)
- `Session::temp_tool`: on a `Down` / `DoubleClick` with `mods.cmd`, when the chosen tool isn't busy and is one that borrows (`borrowed_selection_tool`: nothing for `selection`, `directSelection`, `hand`, `zoom` and a loaded place cursor — where Cmd already means something or nothing; `directSelection` for `pen`, `addAnchor`, `deleteAnchor`, `convertDirection`, `pencil`, `smooth`, `erase`, `scissors`; `selection` for everything else), a fresh selection tool is created and `with_ctx` dispatches the press, the drags and the release to it. On `Up` it is dropped (unless that tool reports itself busy). `set_tool` drops it too.
- `cursor()`: while Cmd is held over the canvas, the pointer shows what a press would borrow.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: the Selection-tool row notes it.

The canvas already passes Cmd in `Mods`, so no UI change is needed; Cmd-click *with* the Selection tool (select through) is untouched because the selection tools borrow nothing.

## Test
`tests::cmd_held_press_borrows_the_selection_tool_for_one_gesture`: Type tool chosen, a Cmd-press on a text frame selects it as an object (no caret), a Cmd-drag moves it 50 pt, the chosen tool is still `type` and the borrowed tool is gone on release; the next plain press places a caret; Cmd with the Selection tool borrows nothing; the Pen borrows `directSelection`. Fails on `main` at the first assertion (a Cmd-press with the Type tool placed a caret).

title: Scaling a text frame scales its text, as InDesign's When Scaling: Apply to Content
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Dansky's *Masking with Exclude Overlap InDesign Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TYzFYxJN-Rg)). At 2:16 he Cmd+Shift-drags the corner of the "LEARN" text frame: "you can see it will scale it proportionately, so this is a really quick way to scale text up or down". In InDesign the text grows from 70 pt and the frame still shows 100%.

## Problem
DesignCraft put the scale on the frame (Transform panel: 214.3%) and the Character panel still read 70 pt. The text only looked bigger. Type › Create Outlines, the Character panel and text added later all worked from 70 pt, and the frame's 1 pt stroke turned into 2.143 pt.

## Change
Scaling a text frame with its content now works like InDesign's default *When Scaling: Apply to Content*:
- **The frame:** its path takes the scale, so it shows 100%.
- **Character attributes** follow the vertical scale:
  - point size, absolute leading and baseline shift;
  - the text stroke weight (stroked text only);
  - underline and strikethrough weights and offsets, when they are set.
- **Horizontal scale** takes the difference between the two axes (a frame made wider than high).
- **Paragraph attributes:** left, right, first-line and last-line indents follow the horizontal scale; space before and after follow the vertical scale.
- **Where it applies:**
  - a handle drag with Cmd (`transform.resize {content: true}`);
  - the Scale command (`transform.scale`);
  - the Transform panel's scale fields (`transform.set {scaleX, scaleY}`).
- **Unchanged:** these cases keep the old behaviour, with the scale on the frame as a whole:
  - a story threaded through other frames;
  - vertical text;
  - a scale that flips the frame, or isn't along its own axes.
- One undo step, as before.

Not done: InDesign's *Adjust Scaling Percentage* preference (keep the scale on the frame and show "70 pt (154 pt)"). Liquid Layout's scale rule still scales text frames as a whole.

Before and after: the same Cmd+Shift …

title: IDML: preserve liquid guides on document and parent pages
author: keynepekar
body:
IDML currently imports every guide as a ruler guide and exports every guide as `GuideType="Ruler"`. A guide-based layout therefore loses its adaptive guides after interchange. Preserve `GuideType="Liquid"` in the existing shared page mapping, on document and parent pages. Ordinary, omitted and unrecognized types retain the existing ruler-guide behavior.

Regression tests use hand-written XML independent of the exporter, inspect literal exported attributes, and round-trip mixed horizontal/vertical guides. They cover spread/page/spine ruler origins, page/spread scope, positions, locks, layers, and liquid guides on a page whose adaptive rule is off. Both new tests fail before the two-line production fix.

Refs #872 (liquid guides only). #972 already handles stored page rules; object pins and resize constraints remain out of scope, so #872 should stay open. The relevant crate documentation, format-parity notes and progress log are updated.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL, Rust 1.99.0:

- `cargo test --locked -p designcraft-idml liquid_guides -- --nocapture`: both tests pass; both fail on the original implementation.
- CLI smoke test: create two frames and a liquid guide, export IDML, reopen, create an alternate layout at twice the page width. The crossed frame grows from 200 to 400 pt; the other remains 100 pt.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all seven gates pass (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, 1,968 tests passed / 5 ignored, PDF dependency pins, assets, layers and WASM).
- `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-web`: passes.

No manual InDesign runtime verification was performed.

title: fix(text): Character panel: VF sliders preview live implementation
author: andrestelex
body:
Dragging a variable font axis slider previews the change on the page and commits it as one undo step when the slider is let go. The panel gathers what every axis slider did in a frame before acting, so with several axes a drag no longer commits and reopens the change on every frame. A click, an arrow key or a value typed in the field beside each slider applies at once. Narrow axes (Skia's weight runs 0.48-3.2) step by hundredths; a slider snapping a value that is off its steps no longer counts as a change.

Live previews are commands, so the panel stays on app.run: edit.preview {label, command, params} shows an edit on the document as it was before the preview began, edit.commitPreview makes it one undo step, edit.cancelPreview drops it. A preview no panel held in the last frame (its slider let go, or the panel closed) is committed at the start of the next one.

The Character panel drops its repeated heading, lays Size, Kerning and Baseline, and Leading and Tracking, out in two columns whose captions and fields line up, shows auto leading in parentheses, and shows a style with axis settings as its axes alone, here and in the Text Frame floating bar.

This is an update to previous pull request https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/885

title: Text: Digits setting in the Character panel and character styles; page numbers and list numbers follow it
author: soro-82
body:
## Description

There was no usable way to draw the figures 0–9 as Persian (or Arabic) digits. The Digits menu in the Character panel only appeared for right-to-left paragraphs, the Character Style Options dialog had no Digits setting, and the page-number marker ignored the setting entirely. title: fix: IDML links in a subfolder beside the package load on another machine
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
An IDML package opened away from its author's machine keeps image links such as `/images/logo.png` that don't exist on the new machine. Link lookup only tried the package folder and its `Links/` folder, so images kept in an `images/` folder next to the .idml showed as missing.

Link lookup now also tries the link's trailing folders under the package folder, longest first (at most 8 components): `/images/logo.png` finds `<package>/images/logo.png`.

- Regression test: `opens_links_from_a_subfolder_beside_the_package`
- Checked on a real 16-spread package: 22 links went from missing to ok
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm)
- ROADMAP.md progress-log entry added

title: feat(text): TextFrame: double-clicking handles fits to content
author: andrestelex
body:
Double-clicking a handle of the selected text frames fits them to their text: a corner fits the width and height, the top or bottom handle the height, a side handle the width. Object > Fitting > Fit Frame to Content (object.fit fitFrameToContent) now fits text frames too, with an `axes` parameter (both|width|height); the handles run it for every selected text frame, so fitting several is one undo step.

Fitting only shrinks a frame bigger than its text, measured by composing the story at trial sizes (alignment, indents, tabs, drop caps and wraps all count):
- the height is the smallest that keeps the frame's text, when the frame holds its story's end; text that runs on (overset, or into the next frame of its thread) keeps the frame's height, so it never stretches down a long story;
- the width shrinks only when no line wraps (every line ends at its paragraph or a break), to the narrowest that keeps every line as it is.

The text stays in place: the edge kept is the one the text sits against (left, right or centre) and, vertically, the frame's vertical justification. Rotated frames fit in their own space; insets stay around the text. Empty, locked, vertical and type-on-a-path frames are left alone.

On a one-line frame the threading ports sit on the side handles: a double click on a port with no link to break now reaches the handle under it.

title: Tables: Fit to Frame Width option, columns follow the text frame's width
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1025.

A table can now follow its text frame's width. InDesign users asked for this in the InDesign team's own table thread (https://redd.it/1luvoma, the reply with 134 points: "lock a table to 100% of the frame width").

**Behaviour**
- New table option **Fit to Frame Width** (`TableOptions::fit_to_frame`, default off). When it is on, composition scales the stored column widths by *available width / natural width* in both directions, so the table fills the text column (minus paragraph indents) and follows every frame resize, wider or narrower. Without the option nothing changes: a table is only scaled down when it is wider than the column, as before.
- The stored column widths are not rewritten; with the option on they act as proportions. Undo, save and reopen keep the option. It is written to the document only when on, so older files and readers are unaffected.
- `table.options` takes `fitToFrame: bool`; any other value is an error that leaves the table unchanged (the whole call is rejected). `table.get`/`table.options` report `options.fitToFrame` when it is on.
- Applying a table style keeps the option (styles set borders and fills field by field).
- Table panel: a "Fit to Frame Width" checkbox under "Repeat Header Rows".

**IDML:** InDesign has no equivalent table attribute, so this stays a DesignCraft-only option: IDML export writes the stored column widths and drops the flag. Noted in `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

**Tests** (test-first; both engine tests failed before the composition change)

title: idml: one unusable CJK metric no longer refuses the whole file
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Composite-font and mojikumi metrics are taken from the file with no sanity check (`crates/idml/src/import.rs:502`, `:536` — `El::num` at `crates/idml/src/xml.rs:96` has no filter), and `Document::check()` refuses exactly the values a hostile or merely unusual part can carry — a zero or non-finite `relative_size`/`horizontal_scale`/`vertical_scale`/`baseline_shift` (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:734`) — with `import_idml` running that check on the finished document (`crates/idml/src/import.rs:93`). So `RelativeSize="0"` or `BaselineShift="NaN"` on one `CompositeFontEntry` anywhere in the package fails the whole import with *"invalid composite font metrics"*: a document that can no longer be opened, with nothing in the UI saying which value caused it.

Every neighbouring number in this importer already filters (`Prefs::num`, `inset_spacing::number`, `KerningValue`, guides), and the command path rejects the same metrics (`style.rs:31`) — the import path was the one gap.

**Fix:** filter where the number is read — `.filter(|v| v.is_finite() && *v > 0.0).unwrap_or(100.0)` for the three scales, `.filter(|v| v.is_finite()).unwrap_or(0.0)` for the shift and the three mojikumi values. One unusable entry degrades to a usable default instead of refusing the file.

**Regression test:** `unusable_cjk_metrics_do_not_refuse_the_whole_file` — on main the import fails with `Invalid("invalid composite font metrics: Rubies")`; with the patch it opens and the entries carry the fallbacks. Full `designcraft-idml` suite green (92 passed).

title: format: refuse to save a document that can't be read back
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The document JSON is written without ever being read back (`crates/format/src/lib.rs:66`), and serde_json serializes a non-finite `f64` as `null` — which a coordinate can't be deserialized from (`invalid type: null, expected f64`). A non-finite coordinate is easy to reach through the app's own command surface: `file.place` computes `x + bw * k` with `k = w / nw` straight from the parameters (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:370`), so `{"command":"file.place","params":{"base64":"<1×1 png>","x":1e308,"width":1e308}}` overflows to infinity in the placed item's path anchors (`transform.scale` and `frame.create` reach it the same way; unlike `guides.rs`, `flex.rs`, `object.rs:2186` and `table.rs:859`, these entry points don't filter finiteness).

`file.save` then writes the archive — the `document.json` inside holds `null` where the coordinate was — marks the document clean, deletes the recovery copy, and reports success. The next `load` rejects the file the app itself just wrote: the user's document is reported saved and is then unopenable.

**Fix:** `format::save` checks the serialized bytes against the reader before writing them and refuses with a clear error instead of producing an unloadable file. (The complementary entry-point filters and making `to_bytes` fallible are a wider policy change deliberately left to the maintainers — `to_bytes` has six call sites.)

**Regression test:** `a_document_with_a_non_finite_coordinate_is_not_saved` — on main the save succeeds and hands back an archive `load` rejects; with the guard the save is refused. Full `designcraft-format` suite green (15 passed).

title: docx: an explicit off imports as off
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`ST_OnOff` (ECMA-376 §17.17.4) is `xsd:boolean ∪ {on, off}`: `true`/`1`/`on` are on, `false`/`0`/`off` are off. The toggle reader only counted `"0" | "false" | "none"` as off (`crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:50`), and the underline reader had the same list (`:170`) — so a property the document explicitly switches **off** imports as **on**.

Reachable through File › Place (or `links.update`, `place.styles`) on any `.docx` containing `<w:b w:val="off"/>`, `<w:i w:val="off"/>`, `<w:strike w:val="off"/>`, `<w:caps w:val="off"/>`, `<w:u w:val="off"/>` or `<w:isLgl w:val="off"/>` (through the same `on()`) — spellings produced by non-Word writers (LibreOffice/POI, Word 2003 XML conversions). Every such run comes in bold / italic / struck through / all-caps / underlined / legal-numbered, the opposite of what the document says. Word itself writes `0`/`false`, which is why existing tests never caught it; the same file already matches the `on` spelling for `w:default` (`docx.rs:472`), which is what makes this look like an oversight.

**Fix:** add `"off"` to both off-lists.

**Regression test:** `off_valued_toggles_stay_off` — on main the `off` run imports bold (`Some("Bold")`); with the patch it stays regular, `on` still means on, and the full `designcraft-textimport` suite is green (24 passed).

title: images: the DOS EPS TIFF preview is read where the spec puts it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The EPSF binary header (Adobe TN 5002; the same layout Pillow's `EpsImagePlugin` reads) is 22 bytes: magic `C5 D0 D3 C6` (0–3), `psStart` (4–7), `psLength` (8–11), `tiffStart` (12–15), `tiffLength` (16–19), checksum (20–21). The PostScript pair is read correctly at 4/8, but the TIFF pair is read at **20/24** (`crates/images/src/eps.rs:20`) — the checksum plus the first two bytes of the PostScript section (`"%!"`), i.e. an offset around 5.5×10⁸ that is always past the end of a real file. So for a spec-compliant DOS EPS, `bytes.get(..)` returns `None` and `eps_proxy` always falls through to the drawn rectangles or the grey placeholder: the TIFF preview the module documents ("the file's TIFF preview when it has one") is never used on exactly the legacy files (Illustrator 3.0, CorelDRAW, older QuarkXPress) that carry one.

The unit test encoded the same wrong layout (a 26-byte header with the TIFF fields at 20/24 and the checksum at 28), so it passed and could never catch this.

**Fix:** read `tiffStart`/`tiffLength` at 12/16, document the 22-byte header, and rebuild the test fixture on the real layout.

**Regression:** with the spec fixture, the preview assertion fails on main (`pixel_size` is `201×101` — the rectangle stand-in) and passes with the fix (`10×5` — the TIFF). Full `designcraft-images` suite green (33 passed).

title: Direct Selection moves a placed graphic inside its frame
author: pepen11
body:
The Direct Selection tool (A) selected a frame's content (`selection.content = true`) but `transform.move` ignored that flag, so dragging or nudging moved the frame together with its graphic; an image could not be repositioned inside its frame.

`transform.move` now honours the content selection (or an explicit `content: true`): a frame's placed graphic is translated in the frame's inner space (`Graphic.xf`), also for rotated frames, and the frame stays. Text frames, copies (`copy: true`) and moves to another spread move as a whole, as before. A degenerate frame matrix falls back to moving the frame, never to NaN in the document. No tool changes were needed: Direct Selection already emits `selection.set {content: true}` and `transform.move`.

Test `direct_selection_moves_the_graphic_inside_its_frame`: content move, undo, explicit `ids`, a 90° rotated frame, a text frame with the content selected. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Export PDF: compression per image class, own bleed and slug, PSD fixes, colour conversion to CMYK, CMYK JPEG, installed destination profiles
author: pepen11
body:
Export PDF options a print job needs, in five commits (each with tests; `cargo xtask ci` passes on the stack):

1. **Compression per image class, own bleed amounts, slug area.** As in InDesign: for colour, greyscale and monochrome images Bicubic Downsampling to N ppi for images above M ppi, and an Image Quality menu (JPEG maximum…minimum, or ZIP). The effective resolution is the asset's pixel width over its narrowest placement (groups and parent pages included). A placed JPEG is passed through unless downsampled, a CMYK TIFF downsamples losslessly, monochrome images are never JPEG, transparent ones stay lossless. Marks and Bleeds: with Use Document Bleed Settings off the export has its own top/bottom/inside/outside bleed; Include Slug Area widens the media box. `file.exportPdf {images: {color, gray, mono: {downsample, above, quality}}, bleed: bool | number | [t, b, i, o], slug}`; the dialog's presets fill the compression fields; settings are remembered.
2. **A PSD places at its resolution and exports under Compression.** `natural_size` reads ResolutionInfo (a 300 ppi PSD came in four times too large); files `image` can't probe are decoded by `designcraft_images` and go through the same rules.
3. **Output › Color Conversion to a CMYK destination.** No Color Conversion / Convert to Destination / Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers) with a Destination profile from the colour settings. RGB swatches and colours go through the profiles exactly; RGB rasters through a 33³ sRGB → CMYK lookup table (trilinear); grey images stay DeviceGray, CMYK keeps its numbers; PDF/A stays RGB; an unknown destination is an error. A CMYK Photoshop file keeps its inks (the composite's channels, un-matted and inverted) instead of going to RGB. Commercial Printing and PDF/X-4 presets convert with preserved numbers.
4. **CMYK images with an Image Quality go in as CMYK JPEG** through `jpeg-encoder` (MIT/Apache + IJG; Adobe-inverted samples, krilla's Decode array turns them back): converted R…

title: Fix \rightarrow closing a \left fence early in math expressions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/math.rs:393` (no existing issue): Math expressions: \rightarrow (or any command starting with "right") inside \left…\right closes the fence early.

## Cause
`list_until_right` ended a `\left` group with a plain prefix check for `\right`. It never checked that the command name stopped there, so `\rightarrow` and other `\right…` commands closed the fence. The closing delimiter was then read from the following letter, which garbled the output.

## Fix
The fence now closes only when `\right` isn't followed by another ASCII letter. This matches how `command()` reads names. `\rightarrow` and unknown `\right…` commands stay inside the fence, while `\right)` and `\right.` still close it.

## Verified
- Regression test `right_prefixed_commands_do_not_close_a_fence`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib right_prefixed_commands_do_not_close_a_fence`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The rest of the math parser, the symbol table and the layout/SVG code are unchanged.

title: Compose: a balancing trial's shortened columns don't move a kept heading on
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while comparing DesignCraft with the PDF InDesign made of Learn Skills Daily's long-document exercise (*InDesign Full Course Tutorial*, [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY); the course's `03_HP_LongDoc_Class` package includes InDesign's IDML and PDF).

On page 11 there's a two-column frame with these elements, top to bottom:
- a sidebar paragraph spanning both columns;
- the heading "Campanula Speciosa" (Keep with Next 1);
- a picture with a 15 pt text wrap over the left column, right under the heading;
- the body text, starting in the left column under the picture and continuing at the top of the right column;
- another spanning sidebar.

## Problem
To balance the columns above the second sidebar, DesignCraft tries bottoms for them from the lowest one up. A trial bottom above the picture's bottom leaves the body's first line no room in the left column. Keep options then treated that as a keep violation and moved the heading on to the next column (`force_col`), so the trial was never retried lower. Two things went wrong:
- **The layout:** the heading and its text ended up beside the picture, in the right column (in the full document, on the next page).
- **A stale trial:** the rewind went back to before the trial's paragraph and left the trial behind. If that trial later failed, `trial_failed` rewound forward to its own paragraph. That skipped paragraphs whose keep information was never recorded, and the next keep check indexed `info` out of bounds.

  This panicked in the long document once anchored objects wrap their story (#563 and its follow-up). I couldn't make it panic on `main` alone, so here it's hardening.

## Change
- **Keep violations during a trial:** when keep options would act while a balancing trial for the current band is running, the trial fails instead. `trial_failed` raises its lower bound, and the band is laid out again lower, as an overflowing trial already does. Keep options act only on the layout the balancing settles on.…

title: Anchored objects wrap their own story as their anchor lines are set (blocked by #563)
author: moppeeer
body:

My merge keeps main's `wrap_slot` and passes #563's `line_start` filter through it. **Review the last two commits.** On the document below it also needs #1039 (column balancing), and #562 (anchored settings from object styles, aiongg's) for the import.

With #563, a story's own anchored objects wrap it like this:
1. The story is composed.
2. It is composed again with each object where the previous pass placed it, up to four more times, until the objects stop moving.

In this story the pictures moved between frames from pass to pass and never settled; with 16 passes they still moved. The last pass wrapped the text around where the pictures had been the time before. The result was empty heading boxes left on a page and headings pushed into the next frame, from page 11 on.

title: Keep '-' after an RTF control word when no digit follows
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/rtf.rs:160` (no existing issue): RTF import drops a '-' that directly follows a control word when no digits follow it.

## Cause
The RTF control-word scanner consumed a '-' directly after the word as the start of a numeric parameter, even when no digit followed. The parameter then parsed to None and the hyphen was never emitted, so `Rock\emdash-roll` lost its '-'.

## Fix
The scanner now consumes a '-' only when an ASCII digit follows it. Otherwise the '-' stays in the input and is imported as literal text. Negative parameters such as `\li-720` are still consumed as parameters.

## Verified
- Regression test `hyphen_after_control_word_without_digits_is_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib hyphen_after_control_word_without_digits_is_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The handling of control symbols such as `\-` (soft hyphen) and of the delimiting space is unchanged.

title: feat: EPS support through a clean-room PostScript interpreter (designcraft-postscript)
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
Placed EPS files used to show only their TIFF preview, or a grey placeholder when they had none. This adds `designcraft-postscript`, a PostScript interpreter written from the PostScript Language Reference (3rd ed.), the Type 1 Font Format, and Adobe TN 5176/5177 (CFF, Type 2 charstrings) and TN 5012 (Type 42). No Ghostscript or other GPL code was used.

It runs an EPS program and writes what it paints as a one-page vector PDF of its bounding box. The rest of DesignCraft treats that PDF as a placed PDF.

## In the app
- **Placing** an EPS keeps the EPS as the asset (`application/postscript`). It is no longer replaced by its preview, so the link compares equal to the file and no longer shows as modified.
- **Screen**: the renderer converts the EPS (cached by content) and draws it through hayro, like a placed PDF.
- **PDF export**: embedded as vectors through krilla. CMYK and spot colours are kept; the PDF is 1.4, so it is fine for PDF/X-1a.
- **IDML** import keeps linked EPS as EPS; export writes `<EPS>` elements.
- An EPS whose program fails before painting anything falls back to the existing preview/placeholder path.

## What the interpreter covers
- The language: scanner, an explicit execution stack (procedures, loops, `stopped`, `exit`; no Rust recursion for PostScript control flow), dictionaries, strings and arrays, resources, about 330 operators.
- Graphics: CTM, paths, fill/stroke, clipping (synced to the PDF with q/Q, independent of the program's gsave pattern), `strokepath` (kurbo's stroker), user paths and forms.
- Colour: device spaces, Separation/DeviceN (tint transforms), Indexed, ICCBased, Lab.
- Images: `image`, `colorimage`, `imagemask`, multiple data sources; JPEG is passed through.
- Filters, decoded lazily as they are read: ASCIIHex, ASCII85, RunLength, LZW, Flate (with predictors), SubFile, ReusableStream, DCT; plus `eexec`.
- Shadings and patterns: types 1–7 (meshes included) for `shfill` and shading patterns, and tiling patterns (coloured and unc…

title: Keep text of inline content controls in DOCX import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:354` (no existing issue): DOCX import drops the text of inline content controls (w:sdt inside a paragraph).

## Cause
`Ctx::inline` in the DOCX importer had no arm for `w:sdt`. A content control inside a paragraph (date picker, drop-down, plain-text control) keeps its runs in `w:sdtContent`, so those runs were silently dropped. Block-level and table-cell `w:sdt` were already handled.

## Fix
`Ctx::inline` now recurses into the `w:sdtContent` of an inline `w:sdt`, the same way it handles hyperlinks and smart tags. The regression test covers a content control between runs and one that wraps a hyperlink.

## Verified
- Regression test `inline_content_control_text_is_kept`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib inline_content_control_text_is_kept`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Block-level and table-cell `w:sdt` handling, and the content control's properties (`w:sdtPr`), which are still ignored.

title: Canvas: pages show their paper while their render is on its way, not black
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Learn Skills Daily's *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY), chapter "Overview of the Pages Panel", 28:10). The instructor double-clicks thumbnails in the Pages panel to jump between pages. InDesign shows each page at once.

## Problem
When the view moved to pages the canvas texture didn't cover yet (a jump from the Pages panel, Go to Page, a fast scroll), the pages showed solid black until the background render arrived. The black was the page shadow: a page-sized black rectangle offset by 1.5 pt, painted under the texture. Only the frame edges and guides showed over it. In a release build the black lasts a moment; in a debug build, or on a heavy page, it's clearly visible.

## Change
- **Paper under each page:** every page is painted in the document's Paper colour (`[Paper]`, white by default) over its shadow and under the rendered content.
- **Page by page:** the paper is painted per page, not per spread, so spreads with pages of different sizes are covered exactly.
- **Where the render is:** nothing changes there, as it paints the paper itself.

## Context
The same moment before and after, on the course's long document:

![paper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/page-paper-while-rendering/paper_compare.png)

## Tests
- `canvas::tests::pages_show_paper_under_their_render`:
  - On a 3-page facing document, each page has a rectangle in the paper colour exactly at its place on screen.
  - Without the change, it fails.
- The UI tests pass; clippy and fmt are clean.

No dependencies.

title: Keep documents with extreme story revisions editable
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Opening a native ZIP or legacy JSON document with a top-level story revision of at least 2^63 rebases that saved counter while preserving linked stories’ fresh or stale state and local content. Normalization runs after the existing reader validates the document. Low-revision documents retain their complete model unchanged.

Five dedicated regressions cover both readers, threshold boundaries, a linked child that is also a parent, whole-document allowed changes, repeated loading, subsequent edits and explicit link updates with Undo/Redo. This PR changes only the loader and its dedicated test file.

Related: #456. The revision-wrapping change remains separate; the combined source is used for compatibility qualification.

Validation: focused load/threading suites, `cargo xtask ci`, and `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-web`, with separate #456 and combined qualification.

title: Pages: deleting pages that contain objects asks first, with Don't show again
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Learn Skills Daily's *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY), chapter "Overview of the Pages Panel", 28:42). The instructor clicks Delete selected pages in the Pages panel on the cover page. InDesign asks first, and he cancels: "it's going to say, hey, there's an issue here. Don't show again. Click okay or whatever. I'm going to cancel that cuz I did that by accident."

## Problem
DesignCraft deleted the page and everything on it straight away, from these places:
- the Pages panel's trash button;
- the Pages panel's Delete Page and Delete Spread;
- Layout › Pages › Delete Page;
- the trash in Properties › Page.

Undo brought it back, but nothing warned about it.

## Change
- **The question:** when the pages to delete hold objects, InDesign's warning comes first, titled **Warning**:
  - "The affected page contains objects. Delete the page anyway?";
  - "The affected pages…" for a spread;
  - **Don't show again**, **Cancel** and **OK**.
- **Answers:** OK deletes the pages, and Cancel keeps them.
- **Empty pages:** they go at once, as in InDesign.
- **Don't show again:** saved with the UI settings (`skipDeletePagesWarning`); later deletions don't ask.
- **Where it applies:** the UI. All four places above go through `dialogs::delete_pages`. The `layout.pages.delete` command doesn't change, so scripts and the control channel delete without asking.
- **Which objects count:** `Document::page_has_items` uses the rule `delete_pages` uses to remove items with a page: an item belongs to the page its centre is over.
- **Strings:** the new ones are translated into every table.

title: Properties: Edit Page takes the Page tool to the page and sets that page's size, as InDesign's
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Learn Skills Daily's *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY), chapter "Overview of the Pages Panel", 32:58). With nothing selected the instructor clicks **Edit Page** in Properties: "it's going to take me to my page editing dialogue box here within properties … let's say … I wanted to change this page just to be landscape." Only that page turns; the others stay portrait.

## Problem
In DesignCraft, Properties › Edit Page opened Document Setup. Its page size and orientation apply to every page of the document, so there was no way from Properties to turn one page.

## Change
- **Edit Page:** as InDesign's, it selects the Page tool on the page in view (`layout.selectPage`).
- **Properties with the Page tool:** with no objects selected, Properties shows the page's own settings:
  - a **Page** band with **Back**;
  - **Page Size**: which page (picking another selects it and goes to it), the size preset, Portrait/Landscape, and W/H. They change that page alone through `layout.pageSize`, which the Control panel's Page tool controls already use, around the reference point.
  - **Margins and Columns…**;
  - **Quick Actions › Import File**.
- **Back:** returns to the Selection tool, clears the page selection, and Properties shows the document again.
- **Outline buttons:** they now carry their label for screen readers (and tests).
- **Strings:** "Back" is new and "Margins and Columns" was missing from some tables; both are translated into every table.

The video right after Edit Page, and this PR:

- Edit Page on page 2 gives the Page tool with page 2 selected, and no dialog.

title: Styles: show paragraph overrides and clear them from the row menu
author: moppeeer
body:
Directly changing a styled paragraph's text color did not put a `+` in the Paragraph Styles panel. Its row menu also lacked **Apply "name", Clear Overrides**, used around 4:25–5:20 in [Jessica Garrity's paragraph/character styles tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG9JkAPLgs8).

The summary and selected row now show local character overrides as well as paragraph overrides. The context menu clears them through the existing command while keeping named character styles. Effective values are compared with the style definitions so equal local values and named character styles alone do not produce false overrides. Character-style feedback only counts attributes that the character style sets. Windows/Linux show the Alt modifier in the hint.

Validation: three focused Styles-panel tests pass, including a programmatic right-click and Clear Overrides, named character-style preservation, undo, and redundant-value feedback. Reviewed before/after offscreen `ui_shot` renders; no desktop automation. `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passes formatting but stops at unchanged `clippy::nonminimal_bool` diagnostics in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:783` and `crates/engine/src/tests_file_guard.rs:161`. A separate engine library run reports 531 passed, 14 failures in unchanged Windows recovery-lock/book-staging/symlink tests, and 1 ignored. These unrelated gates remain unresolved; this is a draft for that reason.

No other PR is required for this change. Checked the repository's open PRs and the author's open PRs for overlapping work. Source-style inheritance, Redefine Style, Preview and the Typography workspace are separate changes; existing font-menu/style-section PRs are not included here.

Separate checks also pass: PDF dependency pins, all 58 asset attributions, all 21 dependency layers, and cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-ui-egui.

title: Styles: captured text follows later style edits
author: moppeeer
body:
Creating a style from locally formatted text, applying that style, and editing it left the original text frozen in its old formatting. In the [styles tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG9JkAPLgs8) this breaks both the Header color changes after 2:16 and the character-style workflow after 6:02. A CLI replay on `origin/main` confirmed that the original cyan headline stayed cyan after Header became red, and the original underlined words stayed underlined after their character style disabled underline.

Applying a paragraph or character style now removes local values already supplied by that style. Real differences and named character styles remain intact. Paragraph applications also respect an exclusive selection endpoint at the next paragraph's start; Clear Overrides limits character-level clearing to a nonempty text selection. Paragraph-level formatting still applies to the affected whole paragraphs.

Five regression tests pass: capture-source inheritance and undo/redo, preservation of different overrides and named styles, sparse character styles inheriting later paragraph size changes, a UTF-8 paragraph boundary, and partial clearing. `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed formatting and stopped on unchanged `clippy::nonminimal_bool` diagnostics in UI `lib.rs:783` and engine `tests_file_guard.rs:161`; the remaining full-CI stages were not reached. The PR remains draft pending those repository-wide gates.

No hard dependency on another PR. #1060 provides the corrected override feedback; it is separate from this command behavior. Existing open PRs were checked for overlap before implementation.

title: Styles: preview paragraph and character style edits before applying them
author: moppeeer
body:
Paragraph and Character Style Options had no Preview control, so the [tutorial's color-preview step](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG9JkAPLgs8&t=240s) could only be approximated by committing an edit and undoing it.

Preview now updates every use of an existing style through the ordinary style-edit command. Each change replaces the previous preview without adding history or journal entries. Turning Preview off or cancelling restores the starting document; OK restores it first and then commits the final edit once. Renaming and export tagging wait for OK, and new-style creation is not previewed.

Validation: both new tests pass (paragraph and character preview, multiple updates, off/cancel, global propagation, one-step undo, invalid based-on cycle). The three existing layout-preview tests also pass. Reviewed the offscreen tutorial replay with Header color changing on both paragraphs and the Preview checkbox visible. No desktop automation. `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passes formatting but stops at the unchanged `nonminimal_bool` warnings in UI `lib.rs:783` and engine `tests_file_guard.rs:161`; full CI remains blocked, so this PR is draft.

No hard dependency. #1061 makes captured source text inherit subsequent style edits; the tutorial reproduction uses both. Existing #343/#359 provide extra style-dialog sections and #466 provides the font menu; those changes were applied only to the local replay and are not duplicated here. Open PRs were checked for overlap.
